violations.comments:
2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. 
Observed PIC on duty with an expired certification. 






For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

2-301.14 (G) Wash hands when switching between working with raw food and working with Ready to Eat Food. - P Observed employee crack eggs then continue handling RTE food and plating. CDI hands washed. Suggest facility crack multiple eggs in a container and scoop out in pan for service. Repeat. 

2-301.14 Wash hands before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single service and single use articles. -P Observed waitstaff come in kitchen and scoop rice for plates before serving. CDI cook staff began preparing plates for service.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods. -P 
Observed raw chicken stored above raw unwashed cabbage in walk in. CDI items relocated. Observed raw chicken skewers and cooked duck and cooked dumplings stored in the same metal pan. CDI items relocated. 

3-304.15(A) Discard gloves after a task is complete or any time they are damaged or soiled. -P Observed employee going in walk in unit to grab items for cook line and continue food prep without gloves change. CDI gloves changed and hands washed. 


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-401.11 Cook raw animal foods to required temperatures. Do not interrupt the cooking process without approved procedures. -P
Observed different plates of raw shrimp cooked then plated at 126-140F. PIC states they fully cook product but they try not to overcook where it is dry. CDI shrimp singles cooking at 161-170F.

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
Observed pan of red curry and green curry that was cooling from the night before at 43F and 46F. CDI items discarded. Repeat. 

For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P
Observed dumplings that was thawing with date prepared and missing date pulled from walk in. CDI date added. Observed no dates on tofu, duck, curry sauces, and noodles. CDI items dated. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P
Observed facility with red curry, panang curry, and noodles on time and with no time stamps. PIC states they keep the time in their head. PIC redirected to write time stamps on the containers on the line. TPHC procedures were incomplete and helped with completing remaining steps that must be followed.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed red and panang curry that was cooling in deep metal containers from the night before. PIC was not monitoring the product. CDI items discarded. Suggested using flat shallow metal containers to cool. Repeat. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

2-402.11 Use head coverings, beard guards and clothing to restrain body hair from contacting exposed food, equipment, and utensils. Observed waitstaff scooping out rice without washing hands or wearing hair restraints.

3-302.15 Wash fruits and vegetables prior to use. Observed napa cabbage that was being cut and bagged while there was still visible apple present on the surface. CDI cabbage pulled from bag and washed in prep sink prior to storing.

violations.description: Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used
violations.comments: 6-403.11 (A)Areas designated for employees to eat and drink, shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, single service/use items are protected from contamination. Observed employee drinks and food stored on counter tops, prep counters, and dry storage shelves during service. Designate separate are for employee drinks. Suggest using lower bottom shelves to keep drinks out of food prep areas. Repeat.

violations.description: No bare hand contact with RTE foods or pre- approved alternate procedure properly followed
violations.comments:
3-301.11(B) Do not contact exposed ready-to-eat food with bare hands. Use suitable utensils, single-use gloves or dispensing equipment. -P 
Observed chef touch Ready to eat bread with bare hands.
CDI - Bread voluntarily discarded.



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link: Handwashing and No Barehand Contact https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M

5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf.
Observed hand sink in the corner of the make-line with containers, wiping cloths and other items stored inside the basin.
CDI - Items removed.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed multiple food items (shrimp, garlic aioli w/ raw egg, crab meat, lobster, cheddar, Ham Sandwich, sausage gravy, easy, ham chub) inside the WIC and inside prep unit 1 (near hand sink) holding above 41F.
WIC in need of maintenance, possibly reducing ambient temperatures.
CDI - Items were voluntarily discarded.
Lobster moved to WIC to rapidly cool.



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed blanched broccolini, tapioca, Meat Ragu sauce, cooked carrots, blanched fries, and caramelized onions inside the WIC and prep units with no date mark.
CDI - Items that were cooked the previous day were properly date marked. Items that could not be traced back were voluntarily discarded. REPEAT.


3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed Watermelon radish (7/23), Feta (7/26), Ham (7/23), Peppers (7/31), Noodles (7/31) held longer than 7 days. REPEAT.
CDI - Voluntary Discard.

Facility to be placed on a risk control plan or Intent to suspend. Date marking has been out of compliance in 5 consecutive inspections.

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (B)(1) Consumer Advisory Disclosures shall indicate that the animal-derived food is or can be served raw or undercooked by using words and phrases such as raw, undercooked, cooked to order, etc., or by asterisking to a footnote per 3-603.11 (B)(2). -Pf
Observed dish containing raw animal foods (LSKC w/ eggs your way) did not have an asterisk to indicate that raw animal-derived foods are in the dishes.
10 day verification visit required.

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water.
Observed tuna thawing in ROP. REPEAT.

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta.
Observed multiple containers of seasonings near the bread and fryer station with no labels, some of which could not be identified.
REPEAT.

3-304.12 (B) In-use utensils for food that is not TCS must be stored with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed.
Observed handless scoop (bowl) submerged in flour on dry storage shelf near 3 compartment sink.

violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF. Observed establishment fail to provide documentation of training employees of responsibilities. CDI- EHS discussed with PIC, PIC conducted brief training with employees during inspection. 



For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

2-301.14 (I) Wash hands after engaging in other activities that contaminate hands. -P. Observed food employee fail to wash hands after wiping hands off on apron. CDI- EHS discussed, PIC had employee properly wash hands after discussion.

3-304.15(A) Discard gloves after a task is complete or any time they are damaged or soiled. -P. Observed food employees wiping off gloved hands on damp cloths held on prep tables. CDI- PIC removed cloths from area, had employees discard and replace gloves.

4-702.11 Utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use, after cleaning.-P. Observed employee washing and rinsing dishes without sanitizing after. CDI- EHS discussed with PIC, PIC had employee properly wash rinse and sanitize dishes. 




For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P. Observed flip top / prep unit with an ambient temperature close to 50F. TCS foods in unit held for more than 24 hours were discarded, TCS foods prepped in morning were removed to be rapidly cooled in freezer units. VERIFICATION REQUIRED on or before 8/10 to assess status of unit. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). SEE COMMENT BELOW.



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C). Observed salsa in walk-in, guac in flip top, all held outside of 7-day parameter. CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded. Observed milk held in walk-in without date label. CDI- PIC had correct date marked on container. *REPEAT*



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P - Observed a container of quinoa to be at temperatures of 105-128F in the tabletop steamtable. PIC stated that they do not reheat the item in the steamtable and it is always reheated on the stovetop first before placing into the steamtable. PIC stated they only placed it in the steamtable at 8am. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC placed back onto stovetop and rapidly reheated to 200F+.

- Observed an insert container of tater tots to be at a temperature of 88F and were stored on the prep table adjacent the stovetop. PIC stated that they usually place the tater tots into the steamtable to hold at 135F+ but the entire kitchen staff has changed within the last couple weeks and they are still going through training.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded tater tots.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed insert containers of sliced cheddar cheese and sweet potatoes to be at temperatures of 48-50F in the opentop refrigerator across from the stovetop. PIC stated that nothing is kept in the unit overnight and all items are transferred into the opentops every morning during prep and that these items may have been out of refrigeration for too long during that process. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC relocated containers to the WIC for rapid cooling and replaced them with backup containers already at 41F in the WIC.

- Observed an insert container of cooked portobello mushrooms to be overfilled in the small opentop across from the flattop grill leaving the top layers to be out of refrigeration and at temperatures of 45F. EHS observed an employee filling the container up as the inspection started and was only out of temperature for approx 30 mins. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC split the portobello mushrooms into 2 insert containers and the out of temperature mushrooms were placed back into the WIC for rapid cooling.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed an insert container of cooked brussel sprouts in the WIC to be dated marked for 7/31, making today day 8. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

- Observed insert containers of pasta salad and couscous to be in the small opentop refrigerator across from the flattop grill and were not provided with date marks of any kind. Items are from properly date marked bulk batches stating 8/3 and 8/4, respectively, in the WIC and were just missing the labels on the working containers. 

CDI - PIC date marked working containers.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

6-301.14 Post a handwash sign at each handsink. Observed handwashing sign at sink next to oven no longer readable. Replace the damaged sign.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P Observed raw chicken stored above a container of cut onions in the walk in refrigerator. Observed improvement from last inspection, points not escalated due to just one item out of compliance. 



For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed can opener blade with a lot of residue. CDI, item moved to dish area for cleaning. Ensure food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned and sanitized more often. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed multiple items prepared this morning cooling in the double door kitchen refrigerator. Observed lettuce prepared 4 hours ago at 53 F, observed multiple salsa products at 44 F prepared this morning not below 41 F after 4 hours. Items did not achieve 41 F during the 4 hours window. CDI, items discarded. 





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P. Observed several food items in the walk in refrigerator above 41 F. The food items ranged from 43 - 45 F. Items included salsa, raw chicken, beef, chicken stock, etc. Ambient temperature of the walk in was 48 F. CDI, Establishment did not have record of how long the products had been out of temperature. Products discarded except for raw chicken and beef which was at 45 F. PIC contact his refrigerator contractor and they arrived within 15 minutes. Unit was repaired and began operating under approved parameters. Recommend moving beer and uncut product to the shelves next to the door and all prepared and raw protein products to the rear of the refrigerator. Also recommend installing a plastic walk in refrigerator curtain at the door so that hot air does not rush into the unit. Ambient temperature of unit raised to the high 50’s F when the door was opened. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments:
3-101.11 Food shall be safe for consumption, unadulterated and honestly presented. -P- Observed small fruit flies land on a small portion of bread in a prep area. Flies were restricted to this area. -CDI- bread was voluntarily discarded. 
EHS stated to the PIC to ensure that that the food is protected in all portions of food prep and presentation. 
Ensure pest control is increased.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P- Observed all TCS foods in the make top including all RTE meats, RTE deli meats, sliced cheeses, and lettuce and tomato above 41F. The ambient reading of the make table was 50F upon EHS arrival. 
-CDI- All TCS foods above 41F were voluntarily discarded. 
EHS discussed with PIC about why the foods are out of temperature and explained the following. Each night the make top is turned off and all food is removed and placed into the WIC. In the morning the PIC turned the make table on and as it was dropping in temperature added all of the food inside the unit. EHS asked if the PIC waited until the unit was below 41F to add the food, to which he said no, just as it is dropping. EHS, PIC, and owner (on the phone) discussed that this SOP is incorrect and needs to be remediated and adjusted moving forward. The make top must be kept on over night so that it is already cold (below 41F) when food is added in the morning or the unit must be turned on and given ample time to reach below 41F, checked with thermometer to ensure it is 41F or below, and then once the unit is below 41F, then food can be added. EHS also explained that for these units the temperature should be below 41F for the food to hold at 41F. The PIC understood. 

After the food was discarded EHS waited and saw the make unit get to 36F ambient reading. The facility put all new items into the make unit and reopened the store. The facility temporarily closed from 10:20 to approximately 11:45 while waiting for the unit to go down in temperature. 
Failure to be in compliance for cold holding on the next inspection may lead to a risk control plan. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P- The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed open bag of RTE meat balls in the WIC with no date mark present. PIC stated that the meat balls were opened yesterday. -CDI- PIC back dated. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed pasta in several pans to be covered in walk-in cooler and at 43-44F. Marinara sauce holding 44F in walk-in cooler. Repeat violation. Assure that all TCS foods are stored at 41F, and if items are removed from cooler to re-stock that the food is not covered until it is back to 41F or below. CDI by uncovering items so that they can properly cool down to 41F and below.





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed several pans of cooked pasta covered and stacked at 43-45F. These must be cooled to 41F and below, and must not be covered until they are 41F and below. If foods are removed from walk-in they must maintain 41F and below, and not be covered and/or stacked unless they are at proper temperature. CDI by removing pan lids, and unstacking pans. Repeat violation. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOx

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments: 4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted. Pans stacked wet - these must be pyramid-stacked or otherwise arranged so that they can thoroughly air-dry quickly and cannot be towel dried. Repeat violation. Need to process utensils so that they have sufficient time to air-dry.

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments: 4-904.11 (A) Display and handle single-use and single-service articles and cleaned and sanitized utensils to prevent contamination. Observed single-service cups not in a dispenser that protects them from handling of mouth contact surface nor protected from sneezes, coughs, etc. Suggest dispenser that dispenses cups individually, or keep them in the original plastic sleeve so that they are protected from sneezes, coughs, dust, or handling.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-202.15 Cutting or piercing parts of can openers shall be readily removable for cleaning and for replacement. Observed can opener to be non-NSF and rusted. Get NSF can opener that has blade that is removable with a pin. It is also lighter in weight and not subject to rusted. 

4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. Observed several cutting boards that are very scarred and difficult to clean. Replace these more frequently or have them planed smooth so that they are easily cleaned and sanitized.

2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF Observed no employee health policy on site and minimal knowledge with staff. CDI: EHS provided updated copy of the employee health policy in Spanish today and PIC went over it with staff and had them sign it during the inspection. 



For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

violations.description: Procedures for responding to vomiting & diarrheal events
violations.comments:
2-501.11 A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. -Pf 
Observed no vomit and diarrhea clean up procedure. CDI - EHS provided Spanish version during inspection. REPEAT VIOLATION

2-301.14 (E) Wash hands after handling soiled equipment or utensils. -P Observed employee handle dirty dishes, load them into the dish washer and then immediately unload clean dishes. CDI: Dishes rewashed. Employee washed hands.

5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf. Observed server washing off her serving tray in the handsink. CDI: Employee educated and handsink cleaned for use to wash hands.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P Observed sliced cheese stored in container with raw Milanesa. CDI: Cheese voluntarily discarded. Observed raw shell eggs stored over ready to eat items in the reach in cooler. REPEAT VIOLATION
3-302.11(A)(8) Separate unwashed produce from ready-to-eat foods. Observed unwashed vegetables stored over ready to eat items in walk in cooler. CDI: Items reorganized.


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-304.11 (A) Food shall only contact surfaces of properly cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils. -P Observed squeeze bottles of sauces stored in direct contact with lettuce. CDI: Bottles removed.

4-602.11 (A) (2) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned, and sanitized per 4-702.11/4-703.11, each time there is a change from working with raw foods to working with ready to eat foods. P. Observed single prep sink in facility with both remnants of chicken and produce in the sink. Sink was not actively in use. CDI: Sink was properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized. EHS requested that facility show EHS wash, rinse, sanitize SOP for the sink. PIC did find SOP and EHS advised that it should be posted at the sink. Per permit conditions, if cross contamination at the sink is an issue, then an additional prep sink will be required to be added. 




For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .
4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed slicer for citrus, and dicer for tomatoes with food debris still on the food contact surfaces when stored as clean. Observed can opener blade with significant food debris on it stored as clean. CDI: Items moved to dish area and properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Observed rice and beans still cooling from yesterday in the walk in cooler above 41F. CDI: Items voluntarily discarded. 
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed various meats and shredded cheese cooling in walk in cooler at a rate of 0F/min. Items had approximately 30 min left to cool and then were moved to walk in freezer, separated in to shallow pans and left uncovered. Additionally product was mixed to cool to 41F in remaining time. 





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed prep unit holding above 41F. All items were 43-44F in prep top and reach in part of cooler. Items were placed in prep top from the walk in cooler this morning at about 11am. Items replaced with product from the walk in cooler at 41F. Items from prep top were placed in the walk in to cool. New products were placed on TPHC. TPHC procedures filled out during inspection. REPEAT VIOLATION VERIFICATION REQUIRED by 8/8 to ensure cooler is working and food is held at 41F or below. PIC showed EHS a receipt for a new cooler that was ordered 8/1 and is to be delivered today. Cooler should be in place by Friday per PIC. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed no date marks on items in cooler drawers and prep top units. CDI: Dates added to pans due to bulk containers in walk in cooler having original prep/cook date. Ensure all pans have correct date on them in all coolers. REPEAT VIOLATION 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Toxic substances properly identified stored & used
violations.comments: 7-102.11 Label working containers of toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers.-Pf Observed spray bottle of what PIC identified as bleach in the warewashing area that was unlabeled. violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed shredded cheese and various meats cooling in deep covered containers, some large bus tubs. CDI: Items separated, mixed, uncovered and moved to the walk in cooler. REPEAT VIOLATION 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. Observed 2 squeeze/spray bottles at grill with oil unlabeled. CDI: PIC labeled bottles.

violations.description: Insects & rodents not present; no unauthorized animals
violations.comments:
6-202.15 Protect outer openings of establishment from insect or rodent entry. Observed both back doors open to adjacent storage room. Ensure doors are closed when not in use. 
6-501.112 Remove dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests. Observed several dead pests in light covers throughout storage areas in establishment.

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments:
4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted.
Observed several containers stored as clean, stacked together, wet nested. CDI: Items separated for air drying. REPEAT VIOLATION

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-402.11 Fixed equipment shall be spaced to allow access for cleaning around the equipment or sealed to adjoining equipment or walls. Observed 3-comp and handsinks with no sealing/caulking to walls. 
4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. Observed damaged gasket on reach in door of prep cooler. Observed lid to bulk rice container cracked. 
4-101.11 (A) Food contact surfaces shall be made of safe materials. - P Observed tortillas stored in “thank you” bags. CDI: Tortillas moved to ziploc style bags that are food grade.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed shelving in reach in and walk in coolers with food debris and build up. Ensure more frequent cleaning.

6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair. Observed AC vent covers hanging down near grill area. Remove covers and utilize currently attached vent system or reattach.
6-501.114 Discard items and litter stored on the premises as they are not necessary to operation and maintenance. Observed dish washer and oven stored in attached storage room that opens to the outside. Per owner, equipment is functional. Remove unused equipment to prevent pest harborage.

violations.description: Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used
violations.comments:
6-305.11/6-501.110 Designate and use an area for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and possessions.
Observed employee food items stored in coolers above and commingled with restaurant food in several coolers. REPEAT VIOLATION Designate an area for employee items.

3635 MT HOLLY-HUNTERSVILLE RD STE 506
 
CHARLOTTE, NC 28216
rows.general_comments: Inspection led by REHS Ericka Jolley

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf 
Observed PIC unable to adequately demonstrate knowledge. Observed no certification, multiple violations for Priority items, answers to EHS’ questions were not adequate to be deemed a good demonstration of knowledge. Also observed overall pattern of non-compliance and obvious failure to ensure employees are complying with the duties. CDI - EHS discussed having someone trained/certified or someone on duty to have good knowledge of food safety at all times of operation. Provided resources to support cooling, storage order, demonstration of knowledge and sent links to food safety videos for training. -1-

2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. 
Observed no PIC with CFPM at time of inspection. 




For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf
Observed hand sink located in dish washing area with no paper towels or alternative to dry hands. CDI - Employee replaced paper towels.

violations.description: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
violations.comments:
3-402.11 and 3-402.12 Provide records from supplier to guarantee fish served raw or undercooked is free of live parasites. -Pf
Observed facility serving raw shrimp in ceviche cooked with lime and facility unable to produce parasite destruction letter at time of inspection. 10 DAY VR REQUIRED to ensure facility has parasite destruction letter. -1-

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P 
Observed unwashed avocado and limes with stickers in tact, being stored above RTE spinach and RTE pre-cooked meats in RIC on cook line. CDI - PIC restored proper storage order. 

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. 
Observed raw shell eggs being stored above RTE spinach and RTE pre-cooked meats in RIC on cook line. CDI - PIC restored proper storage order. 
REPEAT -3-

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P 
Observed the only working container of chlorine sanitizer at 0ppm. CDI - Employee emptied and re-filled with properly concentrated sanitizer. 
Observed chemical dishwashing machine dispensing 0ppm. CDI PIC brought sanitizer to connect to chlorine dish machine. -1.5-

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
Observed 4 third pans of queso, 1 pan of cooked poblanos, 2 pans of rice, and 1 pan of salsa that PIC stated were made from 10am-11am, to have missed 135F-70F cooling window. Observed 1 pan of rice cooling from 134F-99F from 3pm-5:15pm, missing the cooling time window. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items. -1.5-

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P
Observed corn, rice, and Birria oil mixture hot holding below 135F. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed plate of stuffed poblanos in RIC cold holding above 41F. Also observed many containers of salsa made on 8/4 and 8/2 cold holding above 41F. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items. -1.5-

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed insufficient date marking system throughout facility. Many items were in RIC and flip top bearing no date marking. Upon discussion with PIC many of these items were held longer than 24 hrs and require date marking. 10 DAY VR REQUIRED to ensure consistent date marking is being followed.

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (A) Provide consumer advisory for animal foods served raw or under-cooked. Consumer advisory must include disclosure and reminder.-Pf
Observed ceviche made with raw shrimp and cooked with lime is served at facility. Upon menu review, EHS notes there is no disclosure or reminder to link the two. It is also noted that there are asterisks next to many food items that may be served raw that include steak or eggs, yet no consumer advisory linking the asterisk. 10 DAY VR REQUIRED to ensure consumer advisory is fixed. -0.5-

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed 1 pan of densely packed rice covered with Saran Wrap unable to cool appropriately. Also observed 1 container of salsa attempting to be cooled in an ice bath on prep table. Ice bath was melted and not filled enough to properly cool the amount of salsa in container. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items. -0.5-

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments:
3-303.12(B)(C)(D) Unpackaged food may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice except: whole raw fruits or vegetables; cut raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, or potatoes; tofu; and raw poultry and raw fish received immersed in ice. 
Observed 1 container of raw whole fish directly in contact with undrained ice.

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments:
4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted.
Observed wet stacking on dishes being stored as clean.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-502.11(A) Maintain utensils in good repair
Observed 1 plastic container, stored as clean, broken and taped to hold together. 

4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair.
Observed sanitizer dispensing equipment and faucet at 4 compartment sink to be in disrepair. 
4-101.11 (A) - (E ) Food contact surfaces shall be (A) Safe P, (B) Durable, Corrosion-Resistant, (C ) sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated washing (D) Smooth and easily cleanable, and (E) Resistant to damage. Observed plastic thank you bag used to hold warm tortillas for storage. CDI items moved from bags and placed in container with Saran Wrap.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
Observed gaskets throughout facility in need of more frequent cleaning due to buildup of residue.

14 - Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction: 3-402.11 and 3-402.12 Provide records from supplier to guarantee fish served raw or undercooked is free of live parasites. -Pf

15 - Food separated & protected: 3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P 
Observed unwashed avocado and limes with stickers in tact, being stored above RTE spinach and RTE pre-cooked meats in RIC on cook line. CDI - PIC restored proper storage order. 

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P.

20 - Proper cooling time & temperatures: 3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P.

Observed 1 pan of rice cooling from 134F-99F from 3pm-5:15pm, missing the cooling time window. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items. -1.5-

21 - Proper hot holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P
Observed corn, rice, and Birria oil mixture hot holding below 135F. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items.

22 - Proper cold holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed plate of stuffed poblanos in RIC cold holding above 41F. Also observed many containers of salsa made on 8/4 and 8/2 cold holding above 41F. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items. -1.5-

Observed insufficient date marking system throughout facility. Many items were in RIC and flip top bearing no date marking. Upon discussion with PIC many of these items were held longer than 24 hrs and require date marking. 10 DAY VR REQUIRED to ensure consistent date marking is being followed.

25 - Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods: 3-603.11 (A) Provide consumer advisory for animal foods served raw or under-cooked. Consumer advisory must include disclosure and reminder.-Pf

It is also noted that there are asterisks next to many food items that may be served raw that include steak or eggs, yet no consumer advisory linking the asterisk. 10 DAY VR REQUIRED to ensure consumer advisory is fixed. -0.5-

33 - Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control: 3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed 1 pan of densely packed rice covered with Saran Wrap unable to cool appropriately. Also observed 1 container of salsa attempting to be cooled in an ice bath on prep table. Ice bath was melted and not filled enough to properly cool the amount of salsa in container. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded affected items. -0.5-

Observed 1 container of raw whole fish directly in contact with undrained ice.

Observed wet stacking on dishes being stored as clean.

4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair.

4-101.11 (A) - (E ) Food contact surfaces shall be (A) Safe P, (B) Durable, Corrosion-Resistant, (C ) sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated washing (D) Smooth and easily cleanable, and (E) Resistant to damage. Observed plastic thank you bag used to hold warm tortillas for storage. CDI items moved from bags and placed in container with Saran Wrap.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-102.11 (A) - (C )(1), (4)-(16) The Person in charge shall demonstrate knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of HACCP principles, and the requirements of this code by (A) Complying with the Food Code by having no violations of Priority Items during the current inspection, (B) Being a certified food protection manager, or (C) by responding correctly to the inspector's questions related to the operation of the food establishment. -Pf. violations.description: Procedures for responding to vomiting & diarrheal events
violations.comments:
2-501.11 A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. -Pf Observed no procedures for responding to vomit/diarrheal events. CDI - Written procedures were e-mailed to PIC. -0 points-

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed commercially prepared meatballs at temperatures between 44F and 48F, diced chicken at 53F, sliced tomatoes at 44F, and sliced deli ham at 44F in reach in cooler. PIC also used own thermometer to confirm temperatures. Ambient air temperature of reach in cooler was 38F. PIC stated that all items were placed in reach in cooler the day prior. CDI - TCS foods were discarded. Meatballs, tomatoes, diced chicken, and deli ham were all covered, bagged, stacked, and piled upon each other preventing cold air flow from cooling foods. TCS found near top of pile, and unobstructed from cold air fan, were 41F or less. PIC has been advised to review cooling methods for room temperature prepared foods and to abstain from piling bagged and portioned deli meats which prevents airflow. PIC has also been advised to use probe thermometer to record temperature of TCS foods instead of reading cold holding equipment external thermometer. Establishment also has additional 3-door reach in cooler that can be utilized for storage purposes. Additional single door reach in cooler is out of service. PIC has been advised to repair single door reach in to add to cold holding capacity. -1.5 points-

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed three hotel pans of reheated chicken wings in hot holding cabinet below 135F. PIC stated chicken wings have been hot holding for roughly 1 hour. CDI - EHS instructed PIC to reheat chicken wings to 165F and place back into hot holding cabinet. EHS educated staff on hot holding, reheating, and par cooking which staff seemed to think was the process. EHS did not observed par cooking. 
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed plastic container of raw salmon and plastic container of raw shrimp in double door RIC above 41F from yesterday. See temp chart. CDI - EHS instructed PIC to discarded food. It was later found that the food was placed back into the double door RIC. EHS instructed PIC to discarded food again at which point EHS did observed food being discarded. 
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed open gallon of whole milk without any date marking, PIC was unable to accurately date mark and voluntarily discarded food. 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .
CDI, PIC allowed to date/re-date the following TCS food product(s), marinara sauce, cut lettuce, cut cherry tomatoes, sliced tomatoes. Because items were date marked for eight days 7/30-8/6 and chicken wings that were observed thawing in double door RIC without thaw date from yesterday. CDI - PIC corrected date marking. In the future, the PIC may be required to discard food, per 3-501.18 (A), that is not dated or inappropriately dated in accordance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C)

2-402.11 Use head coverings, beard guards and clothing to restrain body hair from contacting exposed food, equipment, and utensils. Observed three employees working in kitchen without any form of hair covering. PIC will obtain hair coverings.

violations.comments:
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed duck fat confit in WIC held beyond seven days and dated for 30 days. EHS stated due to duck fat confit being a byproduct of cooking duck in oil, it shall be considered TCS and date marked for only 7 days; or until evidence can be obtained to show product is non-TCS. EHS observed mushroom oil also dated for 30 days. EHS observed current date within 7 days but discussed date marking oils for 7 days; oil is made from cooking mushrooms in oil and oil is then cooled, and kept in WIC. CDI - Due to being held beyond seven days, duck fat was voluntarily discarded. Date marking on mushroom oil was adjusted for seven day hold. REPEAT. ***EHS will not escalate points due to improvement from last inspection. Last inspection multiple items in deli case were observed without proper dates. Only one item was observed held beyond seven days during this inspection. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

rows.facility_name: COMFORT SUITES HUNTERSVILLE NEAR LAKE NORMAN
rows.general_comments: Through discussion with PIC, facility has discontinued the use of TPHC. They are now hot holding or cold holding all items and stated depending on the amount and time it was placed for service, items may be saved for the next day. EHS advised that facility may only cool up to 2 items. Today they stated they heat and cool sausage gravy, egg rounds, and sausage patties. PIC advised going forward only eggs and sausage would be cooled down. Gravy will be voluntarily discarded at the end of the day. Facility only has a reach in cooler and a reach in freezer, not adequate cooling equipment. If cooling can not be done safely, permit will be amended to show that all hot items must be voluntarily discarded at the end of the meal service.

5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. -Observed two empty cans inside the handsink at the front of Circle K side. -CDI- PIC removed cans.

6-301.11 Provide soap for handwashing at each handsink. -Pf -Observed no soap at the front handsink on the Circle K side. -CDI- PIC provided soap.
-REPEAT-

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
-Observed sticker residue on majority of pans stored as clean. -CDI- Dishes were taken back to 3-compartment sink to be re-washed/rinsed/sanitized. Ensure sticker residue is removed during the wash process.
-REPEAT- No point escalation due to significant improvement in sanitizing food-contact surfaces since last inspection.

Refer to temperature chart. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the items (sausage biscuit, sausage croissant, chicken wings, chicken nuggets, burger, crispy chicken sandwich, rib sandwich).
-REPEAT-

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P- Observed sliced tomatoes and shredded lettuce above 41F at right side of make line at Subway. - PIC stated tomatoes and lettuce were placed in the unit this morning, less than two hours ago. PIC moved tomatoes and lettuce into WIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed lettuce and tomatoes cooling at sufficient rates. -EHS observed paper liner underneath cold well pans for tomatoes and lettuce. EHS suggested removing liners to allow for maximum air flow. -After removing liners, check temperature to see if TCS foods are maintained at or below 41F. If not, repair cooler and do not cold hold in unit until it is repaired and properly cold holding at or below 41F. -3 day verification visit required-
-REPEAT-

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair.
Both WIC doors are not self latching and securely closing door unless pushed on. Repair.

rows.violation_text:
3 - Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting: 2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF 
Observed some documents of employee health polices hanging but did not observe any signed/documentation that employees were trained. New health agreement provided. VR to ensure training and signing. REPEAT.


For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

6 - Proper eating, tasting, drinking or tobacco use: 2-401.11 (A). Employee beverages must be stored in a designated area where contamination of food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and single-use articles cannot occur.
Personal drink stored near hot wells. Store in designated areas.

16 - Food-contact surfaces: cleaned & sanitized: 4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Dicer soiled at blades. Taken to 3 comp. Sink to be washed. CDI.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C)
Boiled eggs, lamb skewers and chicken skewers and paneer cheese not dated. CDI - Discarded.



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

35 - Approved thawing methods used: 3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf
Sauces thawing in prep sink with no running water. CDI - Water turned on.

39 - Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display: 3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor.
Bin of tikka masala sauce stored on floor in WIC. Keep food off floor.

40 - Personal cleanliness: 2-402.11 Use head coverings, beard guards and clothing to restrain body hair from contacting exposed food, equipment, and utensils.
One employee prepping food without a hair restraint.

43 - In-use utensils: properly stored: 3-304.12 (F) Containers of water used for storing in-use utensils must be maintained at a temperature of at least 135 F and cleaned at least every 24 hours or when container has accumulated soil or residue.
Scoop for rice stored in 74F water. CDI - Taken to 3 comp. Sink. Do not store rice scoop in lukewarm water. If stored in water, water must be 135F+

44 - Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled: 4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted.
Metal containers stored on top of each other while wet and did not allow for air drying. Stored inverted to allow for air drying.

47 - Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used: 4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair.
Both WIC doors are not self latching and securely closing door unless pushed on. Repair.

violations.comments:

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P -Observed raw steak/beef stored above grilled onions in the tall reach-in cooler. -CDI- PIC corrected storage order and moved the onions.

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. -Observed baked potatoes miss cooling parameters after cooling overnight in WIC. Observed potatoes above 41F, and PIC stated they have not been removed from the WIC since being placed there last night. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the baked potatoes.



For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P -Observed marinara sauce, grilled mushrooms, and alfredo sauce holding below 135F in hot steam wells. -CDI- Because all items were originally placed in hot wells for holding less than 1 hour ago, PIC reheated all items to 165F.



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
-Observed raw shrimp in breader prep top above 41F. All other foods in unit were properly cold holding at or below 41F. PIC stated the shrimp was just thawed and placed in the unit less than one hour ago. -CDI- PIC placed shrimp in WIC for rapid cooling.
-Observed all TCS foods in mac station prep top above 41F (cavatappi noodles, alfredo sauce, shredded cheese, kids mac sauce, bacon mac sauce, mac sauce). All other foods in prep unit cold drawers were properly cold holding at or below 41F. Observed prep top is surrounded by heating elements (grill/fryer) and PIC stated the lid must be covering the prep top at all times to maintain cold holding temperatures. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the foods listed above 41F. EHS recommended placing the items on 4-hour TPHC during rush periods (weekends/dinner service) or using ice beneath the containers to maintain temperature.
-Observed container of garlic butter above 41F, stored at room temperature. PIC stated garlic butter is left out or microwaved to assist in thawing process. PIC stated butter was removed from cold holding approximately one hour ago. -CDI- PIC moved butter to cooler for rapid cooling. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. violations.comments:
4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed low temp dish machine unable to properly dispense sanitizer during full wash cycle. PIC stated new container of sanitizer had been recently opened leading to a potential oxygen bubble in the line. CDI - After repeated full wash cycles, PIC was able to observe proper concentration of sanitizer. PIC has contacted chemical technician who arrived onsite during inspection to verify repairs. 
For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed numerous pans with residue present on the interior surface of pans stored clean. EHS observed sticker residue present on clean pans stacked on each other. EHS provided education and stated sticker residue shall be removed to prevent contamination when stacking pans together. CDI - PIC removed all pans with residue to three compartment sink to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. (0)
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. EHS observed large container of Mac and cheese in WIC above 41F (see temp chart). PIC stated that Mac and cheese was prepared yesterday and cooled in WIC in large container. EHS observed thin film accumulating on top of Mac and cheese; PIC stated food employees did not stir product enough to facilitate proper cooling. PIC stated this is a procedure that will need to change for long term compliance. PIC mentioned utilizing smaller pans and ice wands to facilitate quick cooling. PIC confirmed mac and cheese had been in WIC since made yesterday. CDI - Due to missing cooling parameters, Mac and cheese was voluntarily discarded. REPEAT. (1.5)

For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed Mac and cheese cooling in very large cambro container, EHS observed Mac and cheese still above 41F from cooling yesterday. EHS provided education and alternatives for cooling for long term compliance. EHS observed a plastic lid on large container as well. EHS observed slaw in make until actively cooling from being prepared prior to inspection. PIC stated this is not the approved cooling method. PIC stated items should be stretched onto sheet pans, as thin as possible, to facilitate maximum air flow. PIC stated facility has cooling wands and will begin using those for mac and cheese, sauces, soups, etc. CDI - Mac and cheese was voluntarily discarded due to missing cooling window. PIC intervened and moved Cole slaw prior to obtaining cooling rate. EHS observed Cole slaw at 41F prior to end of inspection. REPEAT. (1)

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water. rows.general_comments:
Instructions for using Time and a Public Health Control (TPHC)
1. Ensure food starts at 41F or below, or 135F or above. 
2. Label the item with start time. If food will not exceed 70F in any part at any point, 6 hours may be used. If food will exceed 70F, it should be given 4 hours. 
3. At the end of the 4 or 6 hours period, remaining must be discarded. Do not cool or save items after the time window is expired. 
4. PIC should oversee disposal and ensure compliance. 
5. Maintain the written procedures onsite. Form here: https://mecknc.widen.net/s/pvtc855zds/tphc-template-english

PIC is encouraged to reach out with any questions or support needs. 

Note: Buffet now operating only between noon and 3pm on Saturdays and Sundays, according to PIC.

violations.comments:
5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf.
Observed front hand sink fully blocked by pots and pans. 
CDI- Dishes removed to allow hand sink access. (-0)

REPEAT.
3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
Observed numerous single service trays of fried rice which were filled, lidded, and stacked for storage inside WIC to cool. Most containers observed between 43-44F more than 13 hours later. 
CDI- Rice voluntarily disposed. EHS spoke to PIC and head chef at length about proper cooling method; cold air must be able to reach the food. Use metal, shallow containers without lids, and avoid stacking items which are actively cooling. (-3)

REPEAT.
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed yogurt and other TCS sauces on prep top in ice bath at 50F in top portions of food. EHS discussed cold holding and TPHC with PIC. Time will be used going forward. Also observed melted butter which PIC states was intended to hold at room temp. EHS advised that butter is TCS and cannot be held at room temp unless starting below 41F or above 135F, and properly labeled for TPHC. 
CDI- items rapidly cooled below 41F in walking before returning to ice bath at prep top with 6 hour TPHC label. Butter reheated above 165F and returned to naan oven area for 4 hour TPHC. (-1.5)
NOTE: If ice is not used to keep product below 70F for the duration, 4 hour TPHC must be used instead of 6. (-1.5)

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed all TCS foods in cook line fliptops without date marks. Chef and PIC explain that items are dated after cooking and before cooling (verified), but not dated once they are portioned for storage at the cook line for daily service. EHS discussed with staff need to date marks all ready to eat, TCS foods that are held onsite more than 24 hours. Primary containers can only be the sole bearer of date mark when the foods are stored in the same equipment. 
CDI- EHS verified cook/prep date of items. All items dated during inspection. PIC is advised to set up a date mark system for flip top, whether that be on the containers, or the fliptop lid above in corresponding order. (-1.5)
