violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf EHS observed items H and I out of compliance during inspection. EHS observed walk in cooler and all TCS items inside unit above 41F during inspection. EHS observed ambient temperature at 51F and by the end of the inspection (3 hours), WIC did not drop below 47F. PIC stated door was opened for at least an hour while putting away a large delivery. EHS observed no active control or procedures in place to monitor the temperature of the food inside or the temperature of the unit. Facility was observed actively cooling items in WIC. EHS observed no documentation or tracking of these items, EHS was unable to verify how long TCS foods inside walk in cooler had been cooling or the time frame the food was above 41F. EHS observed no active managerial control during inspection. Facility has received immediate suspension and EHS will follow up once repairs have been made to re-open facility. 10-day VR required. (1)

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf EHS observed no hand towels available at both front hand sinks in kitchen. CDI - PIC supplied hand towels for each hand sink. (0)

3-201.11(C) Packaged food shall be labeled as specified in Law (e.g. Identify food name, specific ingredients, manufacturer name and address, nutrition information, labeling in English. - Pf EHS observed numerous unopened plastic containers of various sauces in WIC. PIC stated these items are obtained from the Chinese market. EHS observed two open bags of seasoning in dry storage without proper English labeling, these items EHS has observed in previous inspections. EHS verified with invoices. EHS advised that items in facility without proper labeling in English are unapproved. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded the open bags of flour and removed the unopened containers of sauce from facility for return. (0)

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. EHS observed chicken and beef stored in bags together in the same container in WIC. EHS observed food employee separating these items when EHS entered WIC. EHS observed pork, fish, and beef thawing in individual compartments at the three compartment sink. Beef and pork were observed in original packaging, however, the fish was removed and thawing in standing water. EHS advised against thawing multiple proteins at the three compartment sinks. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order, beef and pork thawing in three compartment sink was removed and placed into WIC. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation


3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed raw eggs, raw shrimp, and beef being stored over RTE items in WIC. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order. (1.5)
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed multiple containers stacked on top of each other with sticker residue and food debris present on exterior surfaces of containers. EHS advised due to stacking items on each other, there is a contamination for the food contact surface in contact with soiled surface. CDI - PIC removed these containers to dish machine to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. REPEAT. (3)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed all TCS items in WIC above 41F during inspection. PIC stated large food delivery arrived at facility at 1pm and door was left open for an hour and a half while items were put away. EHS advised that the door shall not be left open for extended periods of time to prevent the ambient temperature from rising too high. Facility observed not monitoring temperatures during this process. EHS observed no available temperature logs during inspection. EHS unable to verify how long items were in the temperature danger zone during inspection. EHS observed temperature of WIC dropped 4 degrees within the time of inspection. WIC was unable to drop below 41F during inspection and remained at 47F during this time. EHS observed TCS foods inside unit above WIC documented during the beginning of the inspection failing to cool properly due to temperature increase. Facility voluntarily discarded TCS foods cooked earlier today, food that was delivered to establishment prior to inspection was moved to WIF or different cold holding unit. TCS foods prepared prior to today were voluntarily discarded. EHS issued immediate suspension.PIC stated a repair technician can arrive shortly to repair. EHS will return tomorrow to verify repairs and lift suspension. If any TCS foods are observed above 41F the suspension will not be lifted. 3-day VR required. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed items in walk in cooler without proper date marking. PIC stated they prepared these items in house yesterday. These items included cooked vegetables, cooked tripe, and fried chicken. EHS observed cut cabbage held in WIC beyond 7 days. Facility has improved since last inspection and established a date marking system, but will need to continue to work on monitoring and training employees for long term compliance. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded cabbage and placed date marks on the vegetables, tripe, and chicken. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed fried chicken and raw beef cooling in WIC from preparation today. EHS observed these items cooling actively in WIC that was holding above 41F. After two hours, EHS observed inadequate cooling rates due to the increased ambient temperature of the WIC. CDI -PIC voluntarily discarded items due to not being able to verify the time these items had been cooling. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf EHS observed raw fish, pork, and beef thawing in three compartment sink in separate compartments. Fish observed thawing in standing water while beef and pork were thawing without running water and just placed into the compartment to thaw. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC ran water and opened drain to fish compartment and placed other proteins in WIC to continue thawing. (0)

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. EHS observed numerous containers of spices and flours throughout kitchen without any labeling. EHS stated all items taken from original container shall have a label to identify item in container. REPEAT. (2)

2-402.11 Use head coverings, beard guards and clothing to restrain body hair from contacting exposed food, equipment, and utensils. EHS observed food employees preparing foods without proper hair restraints. (0)

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments: 4-903.11(B)(1) Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows for air drying. EHS observed numerous containers stacked as clean with water still present on interior surface of container. EHS advised to stagger containers to allow for air drying prior to stacking. REPEAT. (0.5)

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments: 4-302.14 Provide a test kit that accurately measures sanitizer concentrations. -Pf EHS observed no available test kit for chlorine dish machine during inspection. 10-day VR needed. (0.5)

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS observed gaskets soiled with black residue in front where dumplings are prepared. EHS observed shelving in WIC soiled with residue and debris. Increase cleaning frequency to avoid accumulation. REPEAT. (1)

6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair. EHS observed broken light cover above dish machine. Missing tiles underneath three compartment sink. Repair. 


6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. EHS observed dust accumulating on AC vent above dish machine and expo station. EHS observed flooring in WIC and underneath three compartment sink soiled with debris. Increase cleaning frequency to avoid accumulation. REPEAT. (1)

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed cooked pasta cooling in make unit reach in. PIC stated pasta was cooked an hour prior to inspection. EHS observed no change in temperature during inspection (see temp chart). EHS observed tomato sauce cooling from being prepared at 11am. EHS observed sauce still above 70F (see temp chart). EHS provided education on cooling methods and explained cooling parameters. PIC voluntarily discarded tomato sauce due to missing cooling parameters, PIC placed cooked pasta into smaller containers and placed into freezer to quickly cool.EHS observed pasta at 41F prior to end of inspection. REPEAT. 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

4-301.11 Provide equipment in number and capacity so that cooling, heating, and holding temperatures are achieved. -Pf EHS observed WIC currently turned off to accommodate for electrical repairs being conducted on roof of facility. EHS explained due to hazards and to protect equipment from damage, PIC has turned off WIC. PIC stated this unit has been off for the past ten days. PIC stated the length of repairs is unknown. EHS stated that the WIC is a required piece of equipment to provide adequate capacity for cold holding/cooling. PIC stated that more information will be gathered in the next few days and relayed back to EHS. PIC stated that facility is operating on a somewhat limited menu, EHS and PIC reviewed items on the menu; especially items that are cook/cooled. PIC stated only three items are being cooked/cooled (pasta, soup, and sauce). PIC stated that majority of menu items are cooked from scratch per order. PIC stated facility has eliminated most bulk ordering and only order what is needed. Currently, facility is operating out of a make unit, two single-door freezers, one two-door reach in cooler, and low-boy 2 door cooler. EHS will return in ten days to compliance with capacity. (0.5)

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. EHS observed numerous in use containers of sauce/oils without proper labels. EHS observed bottles throughout kitchen and near expo station without any labeling. REPEAT. (2)

EHS observed non-food contact surfaces of make unit and reach in freezer soiled with food debris and residue. EHS advised to increase cleaning frequency to avoid accumulation. (0)

violations.comments:
2-401.11 (A). Employee beverages must be stored in a designated area where contamination of food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and single-use articles cannot occur. - Observed an employee cup of coffee not provided with a lid to be stored on the overhead shelf adjacent to the microwave and directly above a prep counter with active food prep/cleaned utensils on it.

CDI - Employee beverage voluntarily discarded.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed 3 trays of raw shelled eggs to be stored on the top shelf of the RIC directly above opened packages of RTE vegetables and containers of RTE juices. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC rearranged storage order.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed an insert container of onion jam containing house made caramelized onions to be date marked 7/20-8/20. When questioned, the PIC stated that they make it in large batches and freeze the product, then taking out smaller amounts to be used on the service line as needed. The container observed in the opentop was originally prepared and frozen on 7/20 and then removed from the freezer on 8/1.

CDI - EHS provided education on properly date marking TCS items that are frozen. Pulled from frozen date of 8/1 placed onto the container with discard date being 8/6.

- Observed opened containers of 2% milk, whole milk, almond milk, and oat milk in the coffee station 2 bar lowboy refrigerator to not be provided with date marks of any kind. PIC stated they go through multiple containers of each milk a day and that all the opened containers were from the previous day. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC date marked all opened milks.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

rows.general_comments:
- Facility was found to now be donating their food at the end of the day. Items observed on a rack in the WIC and properly labeled at the time of the inspection. Items observed included sliced steak, mashed potatoes, grilled chicken and sushi rice. EHS informed the facility that they cannot donate sushi rice as it is an item that they time stamped for discard at the end of the 4 hour TPHC and held outside of any temperature control.
- Facility is to develop a list of the items they would like to donate and provide it to the EHS as the facility holds a majority of the items on the service line on 4 hours TPHC for quality purposes but they are held within proper temperature ranges as well (mashed potatoes in the service line steamtable were observed at 179F). EHS confirmed that all items are discarded at the end of the 4 hours if they are not to be donated. All items that are to be donated must be maintained either below 41F or above 135F at all times while on the service line.

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. EHS observed hand sink by front make line obstructed by plastic lid and grapes. CDI - PIC intervened and instructed employee to remove obstructions. (1)

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed numerous items throughout front make line without proper date marks. PIC stated that some items are kept at the end of service and some items are discarded, based on amount and time prepared. EHS provided education, stating information provided during last inspection. All date mark required items in make line shall be date marked to ensure compliance unless specified in an SOP that item will be discarded at end of service. CDI - PIC verified prep dates with items in WIC and prep list posted on make line. PIC added dates to all items. REPEAT. (3)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
EHS observed a large container of chicken stock cooling in walk in cooler overnight that missed the cooling window. Item was in a large plastic container on the bottom shelf in walk in cooler. EHS also observed eggplant lasagna cooling at a slow rate in walk in cooler during inspection. Over a 60 minutes period the only cooed 26 degrees, which makes the cooling rate much too slow. See temperature chart. 
CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the chicken stock. PIC placed eggplant lasagna in an ice bath to ensure rapid cooling. After 30 minutes the eggplant lasagna reached 84F. After an additional 15 minutes the item had reached 69-64F. PIC placed an additional ice bath on top of the product to rapidly cool (PIC used a parchment paper barrier between the product and the ice bath. See temperature chart. Facility has a remaining 4 hours to reach 41F. 
**REPEAT** -0.5- 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf - Observed the white board in use for TPHC times/items to not be updated with the correct date. EHS advised the staff that should they use a white board for the TPHC tracking than they must ensure they change the date every day.

CDI - Date added to the TPHC white board.

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments:
4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. - Observed a stack of small single service plastic paper plates stored in the cabinet below the toaster at the buffet area with their food contact surfaces face up, subjecting the food contact surfaces of the plates to contamination. No other means of protection were provided and the top plate was observed to be contaminated by food debris/coffee marks.

CDI - Contaminated plate voluntarily discarded and plates flipped upside down to protect the food contact surface.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments: 4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. - Observed the sanitizer dispenser at the 3 compartment sink to not be in good repair and to be dispensing a quaternary ammonia solution >500ppm. Facility does not use the sanitizer dispenser in the sink unless there is an emergency as they have a properly working high temperature dishwasher and prefilled sanitizer dispenser bottles for wiping down surfaces. Maintenance contacted Ecolab at the time of the inspection for the repair. EHS advised staff that if they are to use the sanitizer dispenser than they must dilute the solution with more water before using.

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. Observed hand sink blocked several times throughout inspection by huge pot and immersion blender. CDI - PIC moved preparation to allow for hand washing.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P. Observed tofu and cheese stored below raw shell pulled eggs. CDI - PIC rearrange storage order to prevent contamination.

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P observed chemical sanitizer dish machine dispensing sanitizer at 10ppm. CDI - EHS and PIC primed dish machine three times. Dish machine is dispensing sanitizer at 50ppm. 



For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed hot box HH 15 dishes of rice below 135. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded, increased hotbox temperature, and made new rice. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed WIC holding TCS foods between 43F and 50F, with an ambient temperature of 44F. RIC on the cook line was also unable to maintain TCS foods at 41F or below, with an ambient temperature of 45F. Rice cakes and pork dumplings were observed cold holding above 41F on the counter.

All TCS RTE foods from the WIC were voluntarily discarded. Raw meats at 45F or below were relocated to the second, operational WIC for rapid cooling. All TCS raw meats at 45F or below from the RIC were moved to the three door RIC for rapid cooling. Rice cakes and pork dumplings were moved to the LB for rapid cooling.

The PIC contacted maintenance and was informed that maintenance will arrive on site tomorrow morning at 9am to repair units. The establishment may complete dinner service today using the available operational cold holding equipment.

The establishment has an additional, smaller operational WIC available to support dinner service on 8/26. The establishment shall contact EHS once repairs have been completed. The WIC and RIC must be repaired and maintaining TCS foods at 41F or below prior to resuming normal operations.

If the WIC and RIC are unable to maintain TCS foods at 41F or below by the next service, the establishment shall remain closed until the units are repaired and proper cold holding temperatures are verified. EHS will return tomorrow verify that the WIC and RIC are maintaining TCS foods at 41F or below.

violations.comments:
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed multiple containers of cut and diced tomatoes, and pico in WIC with temperatures above 41F that began cooling more than 4 hours prior. CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded tomatoes and pico.





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed raw shrimp, raw burgers and multiple containers of cooked chicken in WIC with temperatures above 41F. PIC stated that the items are warm because they are too close to the door that is sometimes left open. CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded the chicken and took raw shrimp and raw burger patties to WIF to quickly cool. EHS observed items reach 41F by end of inspection.



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments:
2-301.14 (D) Wash hands after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using tobacco, eating, or drinking out of a container that does not have a straw and lid.- P
Observed employee coughing and return to handling packaged sandwiches in display case without washing hands. CDI hands washed.

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Observed nozzles at drink machine with build up and in need of cleaning. CDI began removing nozzles to clean. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-401.11 Cook raw animal foods to required temperatures. Do not interrupt the cooking process without approved procedures. -P
Observed fried breaded chicken filets that reached 113-138F in thick portions. Employee stated fryer indicates oil needs to be filtered which causes oil to cool down thus not fully chicken. CDI filets moved to separate fryer and reached 178F and above. Observed grilled chicken that came off the grill at 146-160F. Employee stated they cook grill chicken on timer for 5 minutes on each time. Suggest checking temperatures and cooking longer. CDI placed back on grill for extra 5 minutes and reached 170F. 
Improper cooking was mentioned in the last two inspections. Facility must take extra precautions to ensure items are fully cooked prior to holding or service.

violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf. 
3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P.

TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

rows.facility_name: BAD DADDY'S BURGER BAR OF BALLANTYNE
rows.address:
15105 JOHN J DELANEY DR SUITE A
 
CHARLOTTE, NC 28277

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf. EHS observed food debris and scouring pad in hand sink at beginning of inspection. CDI - PIC removed items from hand sink. (0)

3-304.15(A) Discard gloves after a task is complete or any time they are damaged or soiled. -P EHS observed secondary gloves being placed over in use gloves as “burger mitts” and then removed after touching raw proteins. EHS observed that these gloves are tight fitting and do not allow for the contaminated glove to be removed efficiently without contaminated the glove underneath. EHS provided education. If facility would like to continue this method and SOP shall be produced so that employees can be trained on this process and different, loose fitting, gloves shall be ordered so that employees are able to remove outside glove without risk of contamination. CDI - PIC stated facility will use dedicated utensils for raw proteins until a determination can be made on burger mitts. PIC instructed employee to remove all gloves and wash hands prior to returning to working with food. (1.5)

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed salmon being stored behind RTE pork in lowboy cooler. EHS observed all raw proteins stored in top drawer, while RTE foods were being stored in bottom shelf. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order of low boy drawers. REPEAT. (3)

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed food contact surfaces of pans stored as clean with food debris present on interior surface of pans. EHS observed multi use utensils such as robo coupe soiled with food debris. EHS observed sticker residue present on exterior surfaces of plastic cambros that are stacked together after being sanitized. CDI - PIC moved soiled equipment to dish machine to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. REPEAT. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. EHS observed interior of ice machine soiled with black residue. EHS advised to increase cleaning frequency to avoid contamination. (3)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed make unit 2 (toppings unit) above 41F, EHS observed all TCS items inside unit above 41F (see temp chart). PIC stated temperatures haven’t been checked today but is aware the unit has been causing issues. PIC stated all items are removed at the end of the night and placed into the WIC for storage. At the beginning of the day, these items are placed back into the unit for service. PIC stated they stocked unit right before opening. EHS observed ambient temperature of unit at 47F throughout inspection. PIC stated a technician will be contacted and should be onsite by today/tomorrow. Facility will utilize temporary TPHC until unit can be repaired. EHS stated facility shall not place any items in bottom of make unit until repaired. REPEAT. 3-day VR required. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed numerous items in make units and in WIC without proper dates. PIC stated items in WIC were prepared this morning and items in make units were taken from WIC. PIC verified prep dates with food employee on site during inspection. EHS observed date marking out of compliance throughout facility. EHS stated items prepared today and that can be verified can be dated and retained, any items not made today were voluntarily discarded. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded chicken wings, cream cheese dip, cooked onions, and cooked mushrooms due to missing date and being unable to verify date item was made. Items such as cut lettuce, tomatoes, sliced cheeses, sauces were verified by prep list and dated. REPEAT. (3) *** This is the second time facility has been marked full points for date marking. EHS advised during next inspection if no improvement is noted facility may be required to complete a risk control plan for long term compliance. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
2-301.14 (E) Wash hands after handling soiled equipment or utensils. -P. Observed employee handling wiping cloth to clean surfaces and then go back to preparing food without washing hands. CDI- education provided to employee and employee properly wash hands.
2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P Observed employee wash hands and use bare hands to turn off faucet and return to food preparation on line. CDI- employee rewashed hands and used a barrier to turn off faucet. 



For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M .
6-301.11 Provide soap for handwashing at each handsink. -Pf. Observed no soap at hand sink in prep area. CDI- soap provided.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed almost all sauces in unit behind wok line holding 43-46F. CDI- all sauces in unit for greater than 4 hours were discarded. Sauces placed in the unit this morning at 9-10am were allowed to be brought to walk in to cool. Ambient air temp of unit observed at 37F. Unable to determine cause of temperature violation at time of inspection. Observed cooked portioned bags of beef in top of prep unit 48F and zucchini at 50F. CDI- beef was over stacked. Top layer removed and placed in walk in, zucchini voluntarily discarded. Facility has had cold holding violations noted on every inspection since March 2024. A long term compliance visit will be made to implement risk control plan for cold holding.

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf. Observed chicken salad cooling at a rate of 0.06F/min inside prep unit. CDI: Item was moved to reach in freezer to cool.

9 - No bare hand contact with RTE foods or pre- approved alternate procedure properly followed: 3-301.11(B) Do not contact exposed ready-to-eat food with bare hands. Use suitable utensils, single-use gloves or dispensing equipment. -P. Observed food employee handle cooked/ready to eat lamb with bare hands. CDI: Items were placed back into oven and reheated above 165F. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link: Handwashing and No Barehand Contact https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M

22 - Proper cold holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P. Observed scallops, filet, duck sitting out on the counter above 41F. CDI: Items were moved to refrigeration to cool. All other cold holding was correct. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

Observed lamb and filet being offered undercooked on menu. Menu did not have a disclosure. CDI: PIC corrected menus during inspection.

29 - Compliance with variance, specialized process, reduced oxygen packaging criteria or HACCP plan: 8-103.12 Comply with the procedures in the HACCP plan as submitted and approved as part of a variance or local approval. Facility was unable to provide approval letter. CDI: Items were voluntarily discarded.

violations.comments: 2-401.11 (A). Employee beverages must be stored in a designated area where contamination of food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and single-use articles cannot occur. Observed 2 uncovered employee beverages in kitchen over prep area and on dish machine.

violations.comments:
6-301.11 Provide soap for handwashing at each handsink. -Pf Observed no soap at the prep area handwashing sink. CDI- PIC refilled the soap.

5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf. Observed a metal storage container inside of the cooking station handwashing sink. CDI- PIC removed the container.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. Observed a container of raw chicken stored directly over an uncovered container or raw ribs in the WIC. CDI- PIC corrected storage order.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation
3-302.11 (A)(4) Except when the food is being cooled, store food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. Observed two speed racks stacked with pans of food that had been cooked one day or multiple days prior to inspection with no covering.

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed multiple plates stored as clean with visible food debris on food contact surface. CDI- PIC placed the dishes to be W/R/S.


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed a hotbox filled with cooked brisket holding at 127-128F. PIC stated that the brisket had been placed in the hot box for lunch service. CDI- PIC reheated the brisket to 165F. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C). Observed containers of sliced turkey, cooked chicken, and grilled chicken with no date label. Another container of chicken had an incorrect label with July as the prep date. CDI- PIC was able to confirm when all items were made and labeled each container. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Insects & rodents not present; no unauthorized animals
violations.comments:
6-501.111 Keep the premises free of insects, rodents, and other pests. Observed many flies throughout establishment during inspection. PIC stated that Ecolab comes monthly for pest control. 

6-202.15 Protect outer openings of establishment from insect or rodent entry. Observed the kitchen door leading outside propped open during the inspection.

3-302.15 Wash fruits and vegetables prior to use. Observed multiple avocados in a flip top with the stickers still attached. PIC confirmed that the avocados had already been washed and were ready for service.

3-304.12 (F) Containers of water used for storing in-use utensils must be maintained at a temperature of at least 135 F and cleaned at least every 24 hours or when container has accumulated soil or residue. Observed in use utensils on grill top in water holding below 135F. Ensure water is holding 135F and above.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed insert containers of fresh mozzarella with pesto to be at temperatures of 50-51F and actively cooling following prep in the opentop and refrigerated drawers across from the wok at the cookline. PIC stated that both the mozzarella and pesto are refrigerated but during the prep process this morning it may have caused the temperature to rise. Cookline opentops and refrigerated drawers are not approved nor designed for rapid cooling and facility must ensure that all items are at or below 41F prior to bringing up to the cookline refrigerators. REPEAT.

CDI - Containers moved to the blast chiller to rapidly cool.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

72 HR VR REQUIRED, EHS will return to ensure cooler is cold holding TCS items below 41F.

violations.comments:
2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. EHS observed no CFPM during the beginning of inspection. CDI - PIC with serv safe arrive during inspection. (0)

For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed cold unit nearest the soup above 41F. EHS observed all TCS food inside unit above 41F and observed ambient of unit at 55F. EHS observed defrost symbol on unit throughout inspection and advised facility have unit looked at to ensure the unit is working properly to maintain food at 41F throughout service. EHS observed items through out the top of the other make tables above 41F (see temp chart). PIC stated no temperatures were documented today and food employee stated food was placed at 9am. EHS advised that facility should be monitoring temperatures throughout the day to ensure long term compliance. EHS verified make unit was still above 41F prior to end of inspection, it did not cool down from defrost. Facility will utilize temporary TPHC for service until unit can be assessed. 3-day VR required. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed numerous items without proper date markings in WIC and reach in compartments of make tables. EHS observed cooked chicken, shrimp, pesto sauce, and various cut greens without any date markings. PIC stated items in top of unit are always discarded per policy at the end of day but leftover items in the reach in compartments are moved to WIC. EHS advised those items would need to have date marking when the intent is to hold item over 24 hours. PIC stated due to cooling these items, the food employees possibly forgot to place the date on the container once cooling had been completed. All items that are not required to be cooled were correctly dated. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC confirmed with food employee that these items had been prepared this morning. EHS advised that food may be required to be discarded during future inspections if no date marking is present on containers. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

rows.general_comments:
Facility is in violation of permit. EHS Observed dish ware in use at facility. Facility does not have a dish machine limiting dish washing capacity. Dish ware may NOT be used. Single service utensils only. EHS observed cooked and cooled chicken and ground beef. Chef stated that they cook and cool chicken breasts, chicken wings and ground beef. Facility does not have the capacity to cool cooked foods from hot. Raw proteins must be cooked to order or cooked and held hot. Any leftover hot items must be discarded end of day. Future violations may result in permit action. 

**If facility wants to add a dish machine Mecklenburg county health department (environmental health) must be contacted prior to**

Facility refrigeration equipment:
1 tall reach in cooler
1 tall reach in freezer
1 prep top / low reach in cooler

Note: Salmon, shrimp, grilled chicken breast (for Caesar salad) cooked to order. 
Wings will be pre-cooked in the oven, held out on prep table and placed on TPHC. TPHC procedures given to PIC and filled out onsite. Facility may keep wings for 4 hours during service. Wings must be discarded after 4 hours. NO COOLING WINGS.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods. -P Observed raw eggs and fish stored behind ready to eat food in two separate flip top units. violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments: 3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P. Observed two containers of rice that had just passed the 4 hour TPHC window and were present on the sushi line. Ensure staff are discarding the rice at the 4 hour completion time. Recommend setting a more visible time clock for the rice in addition to the stickers. CDI, Rice discarded by sushi chef.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf. Observed pasteurized eggs in squeeze bottles at 44 F cooling in reach in unit. Observed crab tip and another TCS sauce that had been cooling for 1 hour at 48 and 68 F in deep, covered, plastic containers. CDI, PIC opened the containers. EHS returned later and products had been moved to shallow pans and crab dip was in the freezer. Ensure that you are using uncovered shallow pans during the cooling process. Recommend using metal vs. plastic. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. Observed a squeeze bottles of water and oil with no label. Keep these products properly labeled. CDI, labeled by staff.

3-304.12 (C ) Store in-use utensils on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment. Observed tongs stored on oven handles where staff could brush up against them while walk past equipment. Keep tongs stored in a cleaner location. CDI, tongs moved to a clean surface.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments: 4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. Observed some cutting boards stored clean with stains and rough surfaces. Observed rice cookers with damaged handles and starting to collect residue in crevices. Replace all damaged cutting boards and equipment.

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments: 4-501.14 Warewashing machines and the compartments/drainboards of sinks used for washing and rinsing equipment, utensils, raw food, etc. shall be cleaned before use, throughout the day to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils, and at least every 24 hours if used. Observed the interior of the dish washing machine collecting residue. Ensure the dish machine is clean every 24 hours.

5-205.15 Maintain a plumbing system in good repair. Observed leaking fresh water supply pipes under the dish pre-rinse area. Repeat Non-Compliance. Keep plumbing in good repair so that standing water does not collect on the floor.

6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair. Observed walk in refrigerator doors rusting. Repair or replace the doors.

Install more lighting so that the entire walk in is at least 10 foot candles of light intensity 30 inches above the floor.

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P- Observed sanitizer bucket used to wipe down prep surfaces with a sink and surface reading of 3010 PPM lactic acid. Food that missed the cooling window was voluntarily discarded.

violations.comments:
REPEAT. 10 DAY VR.

REPEAT.
6-301.11 Provide soap for handwashing at each handsink. -Pf
Observed empty soap dispenser at only kitchen hand sink. PIC had to leave kitchen area to procure soap.
CDI- Soap refilled. EHS advised soap must be present at the hand sink and during all operating hours. (-2)

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P 
Observed commercially heated skillet potatoes and scrambled eggs in oven for hot holding at 127-133F. PIC and written procedures onsite state the intention for reheated foods prior to placement on the serving line in hot holding. EHS advised PIC that hot holding is not maintained at current oven settings. To use TPHC after initial reheat, foods must be labeled with start time. 
CDI- Potatoes and eggs reheated above 165F in oven. (-0)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed shredded cheese, whipped butter, and cream cheese between 47F-60F inside mini cooler stated to be in cold holding. EHS advised PIC that mini cooler cannot maintain 41F or below with frequent opening and TPHC should be used. 
CDI- All items above 41F voluntarily disposed. (-1.5)

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed shredded cheese dated for 08/07-12/28, which PIC confirmed was purposeful. EHS provided education on date marking, and that shredded cheese must be dated no more than 7 days after opening commercially sealed package. Also observed opened packages of skillet potatoes and gallon of milk without date marks, which will be kept onsite more than 24 hours. 
CDI- Cheese voluntarily disposed, EHS confirms opening date of milk and potatoes, PIC date marks. (-1.5)

rows.general_comments:
EHS observed facilities employee health policy missing information on when employees can return to work. PIC stated that the general policy is to obtain a doctors note. This is a correct determination and PIC was knowledgeable of procedure and able to provide the information during inspection. EHS stated policy should include this information to ensure employees know that is the expectation. 

Commercial pesto in facility states on packaging item shall be only held for ten days. EHS was unable to verify when the pesto in WIC was opened; PIC voluntarily discarded. violations.comments:
2-401.11 (A) Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and other items needing protection can not result. - Observed an employee eating their lunch directly on top of the cookline cutting board upon EHS entry to the kitchen.

CDI - PIC refilled dispenser.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed 2 containers of cheddar cheese cubes used for the cheese corn in the WIC to be at temperatures of 45-47F. CDI - Moved to RIF and observed at 40F within 40 mins.

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed numerous items prepared for catering in WIC above 41F. PIC stated these items were prepared prior to opening within the last four hours. PIC stated procedure is to prepare items one at a time then immediately place into WIC for storage until order is picked up. PIC stated temperature should have been checked prior to being placed into storage and if the temperature was above 41F, item should have been left with the lid off to cool. EHS advised that the intent once these items are placed into the WIC is cold holding, due to cooling process not being followed and temperatures of cooling process are not being monitored. CDI - PIC provided education to staff, instructed food employee to remove lids of all items prepared this morning to allow for quick cooling. (1.5)

rows.address:
400 E MARTIN LUTHER KING JR BV 
 
CHARLOTTE, NC 28202
rows.general_comments: - Facility management informed the EHS that the pit stop cafe will no longer be operational starting 9/1/26 as their busy season concludes. EHS was aware since December 2025 of the plans to close both the pit stop cafe and the nascar concession stand that was only operational exclusively for race viewing parties (separate permits) during the construction this summer. The current plan is to combine both concepts into one new kitchen space in the facility. They are planning on the new pit stop cafe to be operational day to day out of the new kitchen space for patrons in the hall of fame day to day and pit stop cafe will also take over the responsibility of providing food/snacks during the race viewing parties, combining them into one permit. New pit stop cafe will have a new menu. Management are aware of contacting the main office to submit architectural drawings when they are ready and doing the necessary steps in obtaining the new permit. Plans currently are that the new kitchen space will not be open until sometime next year and management do not have a more accurate time line currently.

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P - Observed a container of pulled pork to be stored in the under the counter hotbox at a temperature of 75-94F. Hotbox appears to be not functioning properly with the inside only being at 85F despite being set to 165F. PIC stated that they had prepared the pulled pork at 8:30am and put half of the container in the steamtable and the other half in the hotbox. Steamtable was observed fully functional and PIC is aware to not keep any TCS items in the hotbox until it is repaired/replaced.

CDI - Pulled pork in the hotbox voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed packages of hot dogs, pulled pork, 2 garden salads, and 4 ham/turkey sandwiches to be at temperatures of 45-48F in the 2 door lowboy. Lowboy ambient observed at 48F at the time of the inspection and the PIC stated all items were brought up to the pit stop cafe at approx. 9am. Facility management arrived on scene to inform the EHS that the pit stop cafe will no longer be operational starting 9/1/26. EHS was aware prior to the inspection that the pit stop cafe would eventually be a part of the ongoing facility wide renovations that began this summer. Due to this, the facility is not going to repair/replace the refrigerators for the remaining 2 weeks of service as they planned on getting all new equipment when they build out the new kitchen space for the pit stop cafe anyway and the current equipment would be discarded. For the remaining weeks of service the facility is not to use the broken equipment and is to utilize only the WIC in the shared kitchen space in the banquet kitchen. REPEAT. 3 day VR to observe continued compliance on not holding TCS foods in the lowboy.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments:
3-403.11 (A),(D) Reheat all TCS foods to 165F within 2 hours if food is to be hot held until service. -P
Observed garlic sauce about to miss reheating requirements during inspection. See temperature chart. Sauce had been reheated in steamwell, as opposed to being reheated on the stove before being placed into steamwell.
CDI - Sauce placed on stove to complete reheating within proper timeframe.
0 pts.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed various TCS foods in WIC, prep unit, and veggie lowboy holding above 41F during inspection. Ambient in all units out of compliance. See temperature chart. All out of temperature foods voluntarily discarded. Maintenance contacted during inspection. Facility opted to voluntarily close until repair. PIC to confirm units are working with REHS by sending photo evidence of ambient air temperature recorded on a thermometer before resuming service.
72 hour VR required.
1.5 pts.
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

0 pts.

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed portioned macaroni and spring mix in cold drawers above 41F.
CDI- EHS confirmed foods were last at 41F in WIC this morning at 11:00am. Items rapidly cooled at returned to cold drawers with lesser quantity to facilitate cold holding. EHS advised PIC on use of TPHC, as well. (-0)

3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf
Observed short ribs and pork thawing in prep sink without running water, in 78F water. EHS advised on proper thawing methods.
CDI- Thawing concluded, products removed from sink for cooling in WIC. (-0.5)

2-303.11 Remove jewelry on hands and arms while preparing food. A plain ring, such as a wedding band, is allowed.
Observed Chef at cook line with dangling bracelet while engaged in food handling tasks.

3-304.12 (C ) Store in-use utensils on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment. The utensils and storage surface must be cleaned and sanitized every 4 hours.
Observed knife with blade stored beneath hot wells.

rows.general_comments: EHS decided not to pursue a risk control plan at this time. Facility has replaced two of the prep unit that were having trouble maintaining temperatures of 41F or below during previous inspections. PIC stated that temperatures of units and food are checked twice a day and the unit has been functioning properly. EHS observed an increased temperature in the kitchen, especially the pizza prep area as a large pizza oven is behind the prep unit. EHS will make return visit to determine if the unit has been repaired. If the unit is not able to maintain TCS food temperatures are 41F or below during the verification visit facility will be placed on a risk control plan.

Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P 
Observed one employee recomtaminate hands by not turning the hand sink off with a paper towel. CDI - Employee was educated and they rewashed hands.

13 - Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated: REPEAT
3-202.15 Food packaging must be in good condition, intact and protect the food inside. Pf
Observed three dented cans in dry storage. CDI - Items were removed to be returned to the supplier.

22 - Proper cold holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed 70 degree fried onion straws and fried garlic. CDI - These items were added to the TPHC policy and were labeled for the time they finished cooking.

33 - Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control: REPEAT
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed a deep plastic container of potato soup attempting to cool while sitting on top of a bed of ice. CDI - Item was moved to a metal pan and placed in the walk-in to rapidly cool. Observed cauliflower attempting to cool in the prep cooler. CDI - Item was brought to the walk-in to rapidly cool.

37 - Food properly labeled: original container: 3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta.
Observed one container of salt/pepper without a label.

38 - Insects & rodents not present; no unauthorized animals: REPEAT
6-501.111 Keep the premises free of insects, rodents, and other pests.
Observed fruit flies in the mop sink area. Improvements made from previous inspection.

39 - Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display: REPEAT
3-303.12(B)(C)(D) Unpackaged food may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice except: whole raw fruits or vegetables; cut raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, or potatoes; tofu; and raw poultry and raw fish received immersed in ice.
Observed boiled eggs stored in water. Improvements made from previous inspection.

41 - Wiping cloths: properly used & stored: REPEAT
3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses.
3-304.14(E) Store sanitizer containers used for wet wiping cloths off the floor and to prevent contamination of food, equipment, and utensils.
Observed several soiled wiping cloths stored on prep surfaces. Observed 0ppm Quat in the sani buckets. Observed a sanitizer bucket stored on top of a prep surfaces.

51 - Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices: 5-202.13 An air gap between the water supply and flood level rim shall be at least twice the diameter of the water supply inlet and not less than 1 inch.-P
Observed two spray hoses hanging below the flood rim. CDI - Spray hoses were hung up on a hook.

54 - Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained: 5-501.113(B) Keep dumpster, outside waste containers covered with tight-fitting lids or doors.
Observed open dumpster doors.

55 - Physical facilities installed, maintained & clean: REPEAT
6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair.
Observed chipping floor paint throughout the kitchen and degrading cement in and around the dish machine room.

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Chorizo and potatoes were cooled in deep pan with lid in bottom of small sandwich cooler. violations.comments:
3-603.11 (B)(2) Consumer Advisory Disclosures that are asterisked to a footnote shall state, * Items are served raw or undercooked, or contain (or may contain) raw or undercooked ingredients. -Pf EHS observed consumer advisory missing proper disclosure. EHS observed food employee putting items in WIC to cool tightly covered in plastic wrap; PIC provided education to staff. CDI - EHS verified temperature of turkey was below 41F prior to 4 hour cooling window expiring. Cooked onions were left uncovered to quickly cool. (0.5)

rows.general_comments: - EHS held conversations with the PIC regarding the floor tiles throughout the kitchen. Cracked/broken/missing floor tiles have been cited out on 5-6 inspections in a row. At the start of the inspection the EHS observed the facility cleaning behind the cookline equipment using buckets of water and a hose to help get the grease up. During this process water was observed to be pooling up and stuck in the areas where the tiles were missing causing potential for cross contamiantion if all the water is not mopped up from each missing tile. EHS informed the manager on site at the time of the inspection that this is a repair that must be made as there cannot be stagnant water throughout the cookline. The floor must be smooth and easily cleanable. EHS informed the manager that they need to reach out to the EHS with a plan of action and a timeline for the repair within 2 weeks or an intent to suspend may be issued for the repair.

violations.comments:

2-101.11 (A) PIC shall be present during all hours of operation. -PF Upon arrival EHS observed significant food preparation going on and no one identified as being in charge. 2-301.14 (D) Wash hands after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using tobacco, eating, or drinking out of a container that does not have a straw and lid.- P 
2-301.14 (H) Wash hands before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with food.- P

violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments:
3-403.11 (A),(D) Reheat all TCS foods to 165F within 2 hours if food is to be hot held until service. -P Observed cheese dip with 10 minutes left in the reheating process still at 137F on the expo line. CDI: Product was rapidly reheated on the stove to over 165F. Observed corn on the cob reheating in a soup crock still at 108F with 30 minutes left to reheat. CDI: Soup crock turned up higher and corn rapidly reheated except for 1 ear which only reached 157F. That one piece was voluntarily discarded. 

Note: EHS discussed with staff the process for reheating cheese dip. Cook on the line stated the reheats it to 140-145F before placing on the line. The back up is only heated to about 100F and then placed in the hot box to come up to 140-145F before placing on the line. However, cheese dip is cooked and then cooled and then reheated for use. All cheese dip must hit 165F within 2 hours of reheating. Today, the cheese dip on the cook line and in the hot box was reheated fully prior to placing back on the line or in the hot box after only being out of the cooler for approximately 40min per the cook.

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Observed consome for birria, refried beans and charro beans still cooling from yesterday in the walk in cooler above 41F. CDI: Items voluntarily discarded. REPEAT VIOLATION 
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed fajita meat and carne asada meat cooling in walk in cooler at a rate of 0F/min. Items had approximately 1.5 hours left to cool. CDI: Products were separated out and left open/uncovered to properly cool. REPEAT VIOLATION 





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed cooked onions and peppers stored on top of vent for flat top grill. Items were below 135F. Line cook stated that product would be heated again and then placed in the hot well where it would remain for service. Product was then placed in the hot well and temped below 135F. CDI: EHS directed PIC to have someone heat the product to over 165F. Product was reheated but to 145F and placed in a pan for storage. EHS then advised PIC to have staff continue reheating and the product was then 170F before placing on the line. All other hot holding was observed in compliance today. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed sliding door reach in cooler with salsas and items for elote corn holding above 41F. All items in unit from yesterday were voluntarily discarded. Salsas portioned and placed in the unit today were relocated to the walk in cooler to rapidly cool. REPEAT VIOLATION VERIFICATION REQUIRED by 8/20 to ensure cooler is working and food is held at 41F or below. PIC stated that they have called someone to repair/evaluate the cooler today. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C)

REPEAT VIOLATION Some improvement as now all items have a date mark and through discussion, and evaluation of process, these were the only incorrect dates.

rows.general_comments: Facility is receiving multiple TCS foods from Milkbread Davidson facility. Per NCDHHS, retail food establishments may not sell or transfer food to another retail food establishment with different legal ownership without a North Carolina Department of Agriculture (NCDA) permit. Facility must ensure Milkbread Davidson location has an NCDA permit or discontinue receiving food from Milkbread Davidson. Prior to the next inspection, foods shall either be obtained from an approved source or prepared in the establishment.

violations.comments:
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
-Observed cut watermelon in WIC and prep unit held past its 7-day shelf life (prep dates of 8/10 and 8/2). Observed cooked barley in WIC held past its 7-day shelf life (prep dates of 8/10). -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the watermelon and barley. -Improvement noted since last inspection and Risk Control Plan. Facility currently utilizes date marking log book to monitor all dates of food products. Per PIC, watermelon is seasonal item. EHS and PIC discussed methods to ensure future compliance, including adding a column on the date-marking log that states “discard by end-of-day” so employees/managers know which products expire at the end of the day. 
-REPEAT-

violations.description: Compliance with variance, specialized process, reduced oxygen packaging criteria or HACCP plan
violations.comments:
3-502.12 Obtain Health Dept approval for the HACCP plan required for on site reduced oxygen packaging.
-P/Pf. violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf- 
Observed several foods in the WIC not cooling at the proper rate. Foods were cooling at a rate of 0 after 15 minutes and still at 0 after 30 minutes. WIC went through a long defrost cycle and came up to 42F-43F ambient during this process. Ambient temperature shortly went back down to 37F. Foods that were cooling were also lidded. All foods were still within 4 hour cooling window. -CDI- PIC moved cooling foods into the WIF to speed up cooling process and all foods cooled to 41F by the end of the inspection. 
Ensure ambient temperatures are regularly checked and ensure proper cooling methods are maintained. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

22 - Proper cold holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed various items in under grill unit holding above 41F during inspection. See temperature chart. All items in unit voluntarily discarded. Maintenance contacted during inspection. All out of temperature foods voluntarily discarded. Raw meats at or below 45F moved to WIC. Facility to utilize adjacent units to store items until repair.
72 hour VR required.
Repeat. 3 pts. Risk Control Plan to be discussed during follow up visit.

Observed no time label for any TCS food being held on time during inspection.

Repeat. 3 pts. Risk Control Plan to be discussed during follow up visit.

PIC stated all items had been portioned out earlier in the day, and had likely warmed up due to the amount of time they spent outside of temperature control during this process. All items missed proper cooling window.
CDI - All items voluntarily discarded.
0 pts.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.
0 pts.

0 pts.
