violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF. Observed files for staff have been recently updated by an auditor and the Employee Health forms were all new with no signatures. Interviewed the PIC and one employee and they have knowledge of the policy. Ensure that proof of employee health training is maintained. CDI, provided new employee health policy document and all staff working were re-trained and signed the proof of training. 




For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P Observed one employee use gloves to handle raw chicken, discarded the gloves, and then washed his hands for less than 20 seconds. CDI, advised PIC to have employee re-wash hands and they completed proper hand washing. Ensure staff are aware to properly wash their hands per food code requirements. Observed all other handwashing by staff to be in compliance. 



For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M .

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments: 3-202.15 Food packaging must be in good condition, intact and protect the food inside. Pf. Observed 3 cans of tomato sauce dented on the seems. No signs of the cans bulging. Ensure staff are returning damaged canned goods received. CDI, cans placed in the office to be returned.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P Observed cooked chorizo stored below raw meat products. Observed raw fish stored behind cooked corned beef in a drawer unit. Observed crab cakes stored in front of raw beef in a drawer unit. CDI, All items moved to an approved location so that there is no risk of contamination.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation




3-302.11(A)(8) Separate unwashed produce from ready-to-eat foods. Observed unwashed produce stored above washed lettuce. Ensure that unwashed produce is stored below ready to eat foods. 


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation
3-302.11 (A)(4) Except when the food is being cooled, store food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. Observed non-tcs salad toppings stored uncovered at the salad prep area. CDI, products covered.

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed can opener blade with a heavy amount of residue. Ensure the can opener is cleaned more often. CDI, can opener moved to dish washing area for cleaning. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Observed several pans of rice cooling for 2 hours that did not achieve 70 F. CDI, products discarded. Ensure that staff are stirring dense products during cooling and placing the product in a thinner layer. Recommend tracking the time cooling officially starts at 135 F. That way the PIC or designee can determine if cooling has been achieved during the proper time. 


3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed pasta that had been cooked in cooled earlier in bags at 61 F, cool to 58 F after an hour. Product was in sealed bags and stacked together. CDI, product had another 2 hours left in cooling. Product bags opened and placed on sheet tray. Product cooling rate achieved an acceptable rate by the end of the inspection. 

For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed drawer unit with steaks and raw burgers at 42 - 44 F. Drawer was cracked at the time of the observation. Closed drawer and returned for a second assessment and drawer was open again and the burgers were at 48, steaks at 44. Fish and chicken in drawer units was 41 and below. Ensure staff are properly closing the drawers to maintain cold holding temperatures. Recommend use of clean ice bags to maintain temperature of products. CDI, products were place in drawers 3.5 hours ago, move to freezer for cooling, and 41 F was achieved. 

Observed flip top used for burger toppings with sliced cheese at 44 F. CDI, Products had been in unit less than 4 hours, placed in walk in for cooling. Clean ice bags placed on the food items to maintain temperature. All other products in unit at 41 F or below. Recommend keeping the flip unit below to maintain temperature of the food. The ambient temperature in the kitchen today was 90 F and along with the temperature of grills and fryers, additional steps need to be taken to ensure food is kept cold. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments:

violations.comments: 3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed lids to flour and rice in the rolling white bins with damaged or missing lids. Replace the bins and keep the food covered.

violations.comments: 4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments: 4-501.14 Warewashing machines and the compartments/drainboards of sinks used for washing and rinsing equipment, utensils, raw food, etc. shall be cleaned before use, throughout the day to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils, and at least every 24 hours if used. Observed the interior of the dish washing machine with residue and mold. Clean the inside of the dish machine daily.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed one drawer with some debris and also shelving collecting debris behind equipment. Ensure these areas are kept clean.

5-202.14 Prevent backflow or back siphonage prevention devices installed shall meet American Society of Sanitary Engineering standards. -P. Observed pressurized hose and nozzle on the mop sink spigot with no additional back flow on the hose line. When hose is not in used disconnect from the spigot or install a back flow prevention device on the spigot. CDI, hose disconnected.

6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair. Observed damaged and rusted walk in refrigerator doors. Repair or replace the doors.

violations.comments: 6-303.11 Provide required lighting intensity. Observed lighting in meat walk in refrigerator below 10 foot candles of light intensity. Add additional lighting to this refrigerator, similar to the other walk in.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed cooked beans, romaine lettuce, tzatziki sauce, and spinach mix cooling at inadequate rates during inspection. EHS observed tzatziki and spinach mix cooling in large containers. Tzatziki was observed covered. Cooked beans were placed into deep plastic container and placed on cooling rack in WIC. Romaine lettuce was left in large plastic container and stored near WIC door. EHS observed no active monitoring of cooling during inspection. EHS provided education and gave PIC educational hand outs for approved cooling methods. CDI - PIC instructed food employee to stretch tzatziki and spinach mix onto thin sheet pan to facilitate more airflow and quicker cooling. PIC instructed food employee to stir beans throughout the cooling process and will move beans into smaller containers to allow for more effective cooling. EHS confirmed adequate cooling rates prior to ending inspection (see temp charts). (0.5)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

rows.general_comments: - Facility has an approved TPHC procedure for milk carafes but due to them not selling a large amount of drip coffees and it being a waste of milk they have stopped doing it daily and was not observed at the time of the inspection. The time log is posted by the entrance to the coffee bar and was observed filled out from the last day they had set up milk carafes, 8/11. The time stamps on the log were observed to be for 5 hours total (7am-12pm). Facilities current TPHC procedure is filled out for 4 hour TPHC holds. EHS reviewed the TPHC procedure and informed staff that 6 hour TPHC is an option if they would like to go that route as long as the milk in the carafes remains at 70F or less for the duration of the 6 hours. If they would like to go this route they must update the TPHC procedure to reflect that. Alternatively they can continue to follow the 4 hours TPHC procedure that they already have filled out, which has no temperature requirement for the duration of the TPHC hold, but staff must ensure they are only holding the carafes for 4 hours and not 5 like the logs state they have been previously.

violations.comments:
2-501.11 A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. -Pf PIC unable to find appropriate procedure for clean-up of vomiting or diarrheal events. CDI - EHS provided PIC with county procedure. (0)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf EHS observed paper towels missing handsink in the front area and in the back area by the three compartment sink. CDI - PIC supplied hand sinks with paper towels. (1)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed deli sandwiches in open air cooler above 41F (see temp chart). Facility prepares various deli sandwiches/wraps in house. Once prepared, sandwiches are placed into WIF to cool prior to bringing to the front display cooler. EHS observed only the sandwiches near the front of the unit above 41F. PIC stated temperature of unit is monitored frequently but not specifically the food. PIC stated these sandwiches have a two day shelf life and are discarded, but remain in unit the entire time. These items were prepared either yesterday or the day before. EHS provided education, advising to take temperatures of the sub sandwiches throughout the day to ensure long term compliance with cold holding. CDI - Due to being above 41F for an unknown amount of time, all TCS items observed were voluntarily discarded by PIC. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Proper eating, tasting, drinking or tobacco use
violations.comments: 2-401.11 (A). Employee beverages must be stored in a designated area where contamination of food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and single-use articles cannot occur. Observed open container of employee drink on prep top table, along with an unopened can of soda. All employee drinks must be stored below and away from food, food prep surfaces, and utensils. Also found screw-top water bottle. All drink containers must have a lid and a straw, and cannot be screw-top drinks as these must be handled to open, and then hands must be washed. CDI by moving drinks.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed American cheese at 43F, sliced tomatoes at 44F, broccoli at 44-50F. These items must be stored at 41F or below. CDI by moving items to walk-in freezer to cool to below 41F. Also observed American cheese and sliced tomatoes filling pans above pan indentation, which is impacting their ability to maintain proper temperature. Re-train employees to not fill containers in prep coolers above the pan indentation. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses. Observed sanitizer in solution not at proper strength. If using quat, must be between 200-400ppm depending on product, observed minimal change in strip when dipped. Also observed that cloth had been used to clean surface, rather than having surface cleaned with cleaning cloth and detergent. Sanitizer is to be used on a cleaned surface, and sanitizer must be maintained as clean. If contaminated, sanitizer container must be cleaned, container re-filled, and clean sanitizer cloth placed out for use. CDI by re-filling containers.

violations.comments:
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. rows.general_comments:
During inspection EHS observed that facility is holding all in-use products on the line (including expo) on Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC). EHS and PIC discussed at length the procedures surrounding the use of TPHC. PIC was knowledgeable about the process. EHS provided PIC with the County TPHC form so that all products could be added, facility procedures for not include specific items (referenced ‘proteins’). 

EHS advised PIC of complication that can arise from holding entire line of TPHC. EHS will continue to evaluate this process during future insepctions and if violation are noted facility may be required to reduce the amount of items being held on TPHC. Facility is required to maintain equipment even if TPHC is being used.

violations.comments:

Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf - Observed 2 large bowls of sushi rice to be held using TPHC but were not time stamped at the time of the inspection. Chef stated that they discard the rice after 4 hours and only prepare sushi rice for the lunch and dinner rushes. The bowl observed at the time of the inspection was prepared at approx. 1pm.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed 2 containers of cooked chicken cutlets to be stored in the WIC with a date mark of 5/8 and one container of cooked sausage links with a date mark of 12/28. PIC stated that one container of chicken was cooked on Sunday and the other was pulled from the freezer on Thursday with the sausage links being pulled from the freezer on Thursday as well. PIC stated that with the chicken and sausage they are cooked weekly and the extra is frozen to be used as needed. EHS explained that original cook dates as well as pulled from freezer dates are required on the containers. PIC stated staff has been getting lazy with taking old labels off of the containers which is why the dates observed today were not correct. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC date marked all 3 containers with cook/prep dates and the 2 containers pilled from the freezer were labeled with pulled from freezer dates.

- Observed insert containers of sliced ham, cut meatballs, sliced tomato, and mozzarella cheese to be date marked for 3/25 in the opentop refrigerator. PIC stated that they are all from this Sunday as they often go through multiple containers a day and are closed on Mondays but staff does not change the date marks when refilling the containers. EHS advised the PIC that if the date mark labels are not proving to be an effective date marking system they must adjust the system to one that works for the facility such as white boards or paper logs. EHS also advised that should the smaller insert containers be filled from bulk batches in the WIC they must match the bulk dates. REPEAT.

CDI - Date marks corrected to proper 8/9 dates.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

rows.general_comments:
EHS noted that cold holding has come fully under control as a risk factor onsite, but the establishment remains out of compliance for cleanliness to sight and touch of food contact surfaces, as well as pattern of residue inside the chemical dish machine. EHS will return for an onsite verification within 10 days and determine the need for resumption of a Risk Control Plan. PIC is advised to have the chemical dish machine pressure sensor repaired at earliest opportunity. 

Lastly, EHS noted the establishment received Taylor Farms pre-washed, shredded ice berg lettuce and mixed lettuce with cabbage. EHS checked the onsite batches and determined they are not involved in the recall, and supplied from California, not New Mexico. PIC states they are diligently washing all produce before used, including pre-washed, shredded lettuce. PIC advised to monitor their supplier and abide by FDA recall guidelines, and continue complaint methods of produce washing. 

PIC encouraged to reach out with questions or support needs.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P -Observed two pans of diced chicken, one pan of diced adobo chicken, and three pans of black beans below 135F in hot holding cabinet (see temperature chart). Per PIC, SOP’s for black beans state to add water to the top of the cooked black beans (lukewarm, not boiling water). Additionally, chicken is prepped/diced after cooking is finished, then placed in the hot cabinet. To prevent future hot holding violations, EHS recommends having only one or two pans of chicken out for dicing at a time, and storing the rest of the pans in the hot cabinet until needed for immediate prep. Alternative solution is to place chicken back on the grill after dicing it, and before placing it in the hot cabinet. -CDI- PIC reheated chicken on grill to over 165F within 10 minutes. PIC voluntarily discarded the beans.
-REPEAT-

2-401.11 (A). Employee beverages must be stored in a designated area where contamination of food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and single-use articles cannot occur.
EHS observed employee beverages present on prep units during inspection. EHS reminded staff that drinks must be located in designated area. 
-0-

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Observed dishes stored in clean dish storage with visible sticker residue present. Dishes were stacked so that sticker residue is touching the food contact surface. 
CDI- Dishes were taken to dish area to be w/r/s. 
-0- 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
EHS observed facility adding labels to products with the wrong prep date. Facility is pulling small portions from larger batches in the WIC and then labeling them for today (portion date) instead of the date the item was cooked/prepared. EHS and PIC discussed this at length since the facility is also placing shift stickers on items. EHS advised using two labels since utilizing the shift labels are facility policy. EHS observed one container of cut melon and a speed rack of blacked fries with no date marks. EHS advised that facility review date marking policies and train staff on which date should be used for product. 
CDI- EHS allowed PIC to add date marks to food as it could be traced back to larger portions in the walk in cooler. 
**REPEAT** -3- 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

3-304.12 (C ) Store in-use utensils on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment. The utensils and storage surface must be cleaned and sanitized every 4 hours.
EHS observed finishes being stored between prep tables on the cookline. EHS advised that cooking utensils shall be stored in a location/area that is able to be sanitized every 4 hours. 
CDI- Food employee removed the knifes. 
-0-

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments:
3-101.11 Food shall be safe for consumption, unadulterated and honestly presented. -P - Observed a tray of roasts on the speed rack in the WIC that were contaminated with mold. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed containers of pancake batter and French toast batter containing raw shelled eggs to be stored on a shelf in the WIC directly above bins of fully cooked chicken wings and a bin of RTE deli meats.

CDI - PIC rearranged storage order so batters containing raw shelled eggs were moved to the lower shelf.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. - Observed 2 trays of quiches, a tray of grits, a tray of roasted corn, and a bin of chicken wings to be at temperatures of 45-49F in the WIC and had missed the final cooling window. PIC stated all items were cooked the day prior and cooled overnight.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded all items that missed their cooling window.

For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed insert containers of shredded mozzarella, pooled eggs, pooled egg whites, shredded Gouda, and a large insert container full of deli containers with 2 broken eggs each in it to all be at temperatures of 45-62F. PIC stated he does have a TPHC procedure for only the deli containers of pooled eggs but was under the impression that they only were held on time if the temperature was above 41F and was not currently holding them on time. Temperature issue appears to be more procedural as the right side of the same opentop had items all below 39F and the lowboy portion was also observed below 40F. PIC stated that all items were not stored in the unit overnight and were filled this morning at approximately 8am when they opened.

CDI - All items placed on temporary TPHC to be discarded at 11:45am. PIC to update TPHC form to hold all items on TPHC going forward.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed insert containers of salsa verde to have date marks of 7/5 and 7/9 in the lowboy portion of the opentop across from the stovetop. PIC stated that the salsa verde is stored frozen and is pulled from the freezer as needed with the original prep date being the dates currently on the containers. No pulled from freezer dates observed. PIC stated one container he had just pulled today and the other was pulled this weekend. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC put pulled from freezer date on both containers.

- Observed insert containers of beef sausage, ham (x2), and turkey bacon in the opentop across from the flattop grill to not have date marks of any kind. PIC stated all items were from the day prior. REPEAT.
- Observed insert containers of diced beef sausage, diced ham (x3), and diced tomato in the opentop/lowboy across from the stovetop to not have date marks of any kind. Tomatoes were prepped on 8/7 with the other date marked containers in the WIC. Diced ham was done on 8/8. Diced sausage was done on 8/9. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC date marked all items with proper date marks.

*Risk control plan to be introduced for continued date marking violations in the facility with this being the 4th inspection in a row with date marking out and the 2nd time being marked out on full points*

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Toxic substances properly identified stored & used
violations.comments:
7-201.11 Store toxic materials to avoid contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service/use items. -P - Observed a chemical spray bottle containing a bleach solution to be stored on the top shelf directly above a prep station where and employee was actively prepping various foods throughout the inspection.

CDI - Bottle relocated to lower prep shelf next to sanitizer buckets.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed trays of cooked chicken wings, quiche, grits, and roasted corn to all miss their cooling windows and being observed at 45-49F in the WIC after being in there overnight. All items were observed densely packed onto the speed rack with little to no room for cold air to flow around the products to facilitate rapid cooling. Facility has limited WIC space and PIC stated that staff has the habit to currently try and cool large quantities of items down at once on the speed rack, resulting in the speed rack to be full and densely packed. Facility must adjust their cooling procedure by staggering the prep days/times for items that need to cool down and/or utilize the WIF freezer for rapid cooling.

CDI - All items voluntarily discarded that had missed their cooling window.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Menudo was cooling on speed rack out of temperature control and measured 95F. Employee stated it was finished cooking 1.5 hours ago. Ensure employees put TCS foods in walk-in cooler or freezer quickly after cooking so the food reaches 70F within 2 hours. Also, nopales were above 41F and cooled in reach-in cooler for over 6 hours. TCS foods must be cooled in proper equipment such as an ice bath, walk-in cooler or freezer. TCS foods must be cooled in shallow pans or containers and left loosely covered or uncovered to facilitate rapid cooling. CDI - Employee educated on cooling methods. Nopales were discarded and the menudo measured below 70F at the 2 hour mark after employee moved pans to the walk-in cooler.

10 day VR required.
1 pt.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf- Observed non vented lettuce container cooling in the lowboy. Lettuce was cooling at a rate of 0.03. Lettuce cooled to 41F by the end of the inspection, and within the 4 hour window.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed multiple items cooling in 2-door RI cooler. EHS observed all items tightly covered with plastic wrap. EHS observed inadequate cooling rates during inspection (see temp chart). EHS observed these items cooling in 2-door RI unit which is actively used throughout service, causing ambient temperature to increase and decrease a lot. Facility has obtained an additional refrigeration to replace drink cooler that was being used in kitchen for raw proteins. EHS suggested dedicating one cooler for cooling and cold holding storage while using the other unit to work out of during service. This way, the “cooling” fridge doors can remain closed so ambient temperature does not fluctuate during the cooling process. EHS advised to removed plastic wrap from items cooling to facilitate more air flow. CDI - PIC removed plastic wrap, and placed all items on ice baths to cool quickly. REPEAT. (1) **This is the third full point deduction for cooling methods. EHS provided education and stated a risk control plan could be implemented in future inspections if improvement has not improved. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to dispense sanitizer at correct concentration. EHS primed unit and ran a few cycles and observed 0ppm after each cycle. PIC contacted EcoLab and will move to single service items until unit can be repaired. 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed all items in make unit above 41F. PIC stated no items are left in make unit over night. PIC stated items are prepared in the morning and immediately placed into unit for service. PIC stated by doing this, facility was trying to ensure food was fresh each day. PIC stated due to high heat in the kitchen, facility wanted to avoid food being out of temperature. EHS stated that items shall be cooled properly prior to placing into make units for cold holding. Due to high heat and frequency of use items will struggle to cool in make unit. EHS observed ambient temperature of unit at 48F. PIC stated make unit has not been observed in disrepair. Temperatures are checked daily but not documented. PIC stated all food was prepared or removed from WIC at 10:30am. EHS allowed facility to utilize temporary TPHC on items in make unit and instructed PIC to discard items at 2:30pm. EHS provided PIC with TPHC procedure and provided education. PIC stated items will be prepared the night before and placed into WIC over night to cool prior to moving to make unit. EHS emphasized educating food employees on checking temperatures at a frequent rate so that issues observed during this inspection could be prevented. PIC stated facility recently went through some turn over and have had to hire new kitchen staff. EHS stated TPHC is only for temporary use to allow facility to operate, PIC stated make unit will be assessed as soon as possible. 3-day VR required. (1.5)

violations.comments:
3-101.11 Food shall be safe for consumption, unadulterated and honestly presented. -P - Observed an insert containers of diced tomatoes and marinara sauce in the 1 door lowboy at the pizza station to be contaminated with mold.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. - Observed an unopened tube of raw ground beef to be stored on the speed rack in the WIC directly above an insert container of raw salmon filets.
- Observed an insert container of raw chicken tenders to be stored directly on top of a box of raw salmon filets in the WIF.

CDI - Storage order rearranged.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P - Observed the chemical dishwasher to be testing at 0ppm sanitizer at the time of the inspection. Dishwasher was found to be hooked up to quaternary ammonia, which is not designed for use in a chemical sanitizing dishwasher. Facility did not have any chlorine sanitizer on site for the chemical dishwasher at the time of the inspection but the machine appeared to be fully functional. 3 compartment sink was also found to not be dispensing properly concentrated solutions. EHS showed staff how to temporarily make a sanitizer solution using the bleach bottle on site and that they must sanitize dishes this way until the dishwasher gets sanitizer or the 3 compartment sink dispenser is fixed. 3 day VR to observe the dishwasher have appropriate chemicals and properly testing for sanitizer. REPEAT.

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. - Observed the deli slicer, a blade to a blender, and multiple stacks of metal insert containers of various sizes to be stored as clean with visible food debris/sticker residue on their food contact surfaces.

CDI - Deli slicer broken down and all dirty items brought to the 3 compartment sink to be W/R/S. EHS advised the facility cover the deli slicer when they are not using it as they stated only using it once every 2 weeks to slice cheese.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed insert containers of raw burger patties, sliced cheddar cheese, cooked diced chicken, and cooked ground beef to be at temperatures of 45-48F in the grill refrigerated drawers. PIC and cookline employee stated that the items remain in the lowboy overnight and are not moved to the WIC at the end of the day. Ambient of the refrigerated drawers was observed at 48F at the time of the inspection. All out of temperature TCS items voluntarily discarded due to being out of temperature for an unknown amount of time. 3 day VR to observe repair to the refrigerated drawers.
- Observed an insert container of buttermilk to be stored on the counter adjacent the fryers at a temperature of 47F. Cookline employee stated they usually store it on ice but the inspection interrupted the set up this morning and they didn’t get to it yet.

CDI - PIC relocated buttermilk to WIC to rapidly cool.

- Observed insert containers of cooked ground beef, cooked diced chicken and portioned bags of cooked penne pasta to be at temperatures of 44-46F in the WIC. All items were not removed from the WIC today and were in the WIC since yesterday as per the PIC and cookline employee.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded all out of temperature items in the WIC.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

CDI - PIC date marked cheese sauce.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf EHS observed active cooling during inspection without any managerial control. EHS observed rice cooling without any temperature checks, rice was left at room temperature during entire inspection. EHS advised PIC to move rice to try and meet cooling parameter, however, rice was never moved. EHS cold holding issues in WIC and make units during inspection. PIC unable to provide temperature logs or explain frequency of temperature checks. PIC was not able to answer EHS questions on cooling process and cold holding requirements during inspection. EHS observed no available working thermometers to verify temperatures during inspection. PIC was unable to exhibit active managerial control during inspection for items H & I listed under 2-103.11. EHS will return within 10 days to observe improvement with active managerial control. 

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.
6-301.14 Post a handwash sign at each handsink. EHS observed missing hand washing signs by every hand sink in kitchen. CDI - EHS provided PIC with signage. (0)

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed a large amount of pans stored clean with visible sticker residue present on exterior of pan. Facility re-uses large plastic tubs for food storage. EHS observed tubs with stickers peeling and present on outside of container. EHS approved tubs can be re-used, however stickers need to be removed prior to stacking for storage. EHS observed immersion blender soiled with food debris. CDI - PIC removed all pans and containers with sticker residue to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. EHS observed cooked basmati rice actively cooling on prep counter during inspection. PIC stated rice was cooked at 11:30. By 1:30, EHS observed rice at 89F. EHS observed butter in large cambro sitting under prep table at room temperature. PIC stated butter is unsalted and was melted down yesterday. EHS explained that unsalted butter is TCS, due to melting butter down it would need to follow the same cooling process as mentioned for other TCS items. violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P 
Observed cooked falafel and potato wedges on hot line holding below 135F during inspection. See temperature chart. PIC stated items are typically held on TPHC, but the timer used to track time for these items is broken. Facility is holding items on temperature until replacement arrives. PIC stated both items are typically sold out within 30 minutes.
CDI - Both items to be placed back on TPHC and tracked with time sticker until replacement timer arrives.
0 pts.
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed various items throughout kitchen holding above 41F during inspection. See temperature chart. Ambient in togo prep and togo lowboy observed at 44F during inspection. Maintenance contacted during inspection. All items in units for longer than 4 hours voluntarily discarded. All items in units for less than 4 hours moved to WIC. REHS and PIC additionally discussed keeping cold items on service line on time throughout the summer. All items observed holding multiple degrees lower at the bottoms of the pans than the tops. REHS provided additional TPHC form.
72 hour VR required.
Repeat. 3 pts. Risk Control Plan to be discussed during follow up visit.
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments:
3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed multiple TCS items in front left prep unit at prep line with temperatures of 45F-50F. violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf
Observed sliced lettuce, shredded cheese, and bottled dressings on TPHC with label incorrectly stating the prep time (when removed from temp control) as the required disposal time. PIC explained that new staff member is still being trained and was experiencing difficulty with the date mark label system. 
CDI- All prep dates verified with GM and prep employee. Items relabeled, correctly, for TPHC. *Disposal should be 4 hours after removal from temp control (if food exceeds 70F), or up to 6 hours if food does not exceed 70F. 

3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P
Observed bottled ranch, chipotle sauce, mayo, and other TCS dressings at make line labeled for TPHC twice; first label states yesterdays required disposal time, second sticker states today. Assistant manager stated the dressings are cooled in the WIC and put out again with new stickers the next day, which is a TPHC violation. EHS explained that all foods labeled for time must be disposed after 4-6 hours outside temp control. Foods cannot be returned to WIC and placed on TPHC or in cold holding for later use. 
CDI- TCS dressings and sauces voluntarily disposed. (-1.5)

County version of TPHC procedure may be found at: https://mecknc.widen.net/s/pvtc855zds/tphc-template-english
EHS observed McDonalds corporate TPHC procedures onsite. A review with staff is needed to ensure staff understand and execute compliant TPHC.

violations.comments:
3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
EHS observed four pans of chicken in walk in freezer with a temperature of 80F at 3:30pm. PIC stated that the chicken began cooling at 1pm. 
CDI PIC voluntarily discarded the chicken as it did not reach the required 70F in two hours. PIC was knowledgeable about cooling processes such as using ice baths and leaving lids open. PIC provided education to employees. 
-0-
For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed cooked beef, cooked chicken, and cooked tofu and garlic oil holding above 41F in prep unit. Ambient temperature of the unit is 55F. After 30 minutes the units ambient air temperature was 58F. 
CDI- EHS allowed PIC to cool items are they were placed into the unit less than 4 hours from the walk in cooler which is functioning properly. EHS advised facility to utilize smaller prep unit on the line for TCS items until prep unit can be repaired. All items in top of unit are being held on TPHC. 
**REPEAT** 3-day VR Required. 
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C). Observed the following items on the line without date marks: cooked chicken (x2 in lowboy) cooked beef, garlic oil, seaweed salad, cooked chicken (x2 in walk in cooler) and cooked broccoli. 
CDI- EHS allowed PIC to date items as they were pulled from larger portions in the walk in cooler and PIC was present when items in walk in cooler were prepared. EHS advised PIC that all items should be date marked and not just the larger portions in the walk in coolers.
**REPEAT** -1.5-
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

rows.general_comments:
Facility has changed several menu items and processes since opening and original permit was issued. Some of these have been evaluated by EHS C. McKenzie and amendments made, however EHS observed additional changes today. Observed facility is using induction burners inside facility to cook scrambled eggs while using oil in the pan. This is producing grease laden vapors. Additionally, facility has added cooking and cooling of ground turkey, potatoes, sweet potatoes, and mushrooms to their processes. Facility is now receiving boiled eggs already cooked. Ground turkey is cooked and cooled once per 2 weeks, and frozen. Mushrooms and sweet potatoes are done no more than 2 qt at a time in the oven, and potatoes are done in the oven as well, but produce approximately 6qt at a time. Facility has a cooling procedure which involves cooking and placing product in shallow pans and cooling uncovered in space within the reach in freezer. This was NOT observed during the inspection today. However, based on volume a new permit condition will be added to state:

“Permit amended by EHS A. Hall on 7/30/26 to reflect facility has changed processes to include ONLY cooking and cooling the following: 
- mushrooms: roasted in the oven, cooled in shallow pan in reach in freezer to 41F (max 2 qt at one time)
- sweet potatoes: Roasted in the oven, cooled in shallow pan in reach in freezer to 41F (max 2qt at one time)
- potatoes: roasted in the oven, cooled in shallow pans in reach in freezer to 41F (max 6qt at one time)
- ground turkey: cooked on approved outdoor grill, cooled in shallow pans in reach in freezer to 41F (max 5lbs at one time; done approximately every 2 weeks)
- Facility is still cooking bacon on the grill approximately 1x per week as of today.

Due to space constraints, only 1 item may be cooling at any given time. No additional cooling will be permitted without the addition of proper cooling equipment. Dedicated reach in freezer space shall be used and kept free for cooling when cooking and cooling will take place. Failure to cool as required by parameters in the Food Code, observation of cooling violations, or any deviation from the above without prior approval and evaluation by MCHD will result in permit action and the removal of cooling approval.”

EHS discussed with PIC options for eggs including cooking in the oven and holding hot or on TPHC for the day, receiving a pre-cooked egg product and heating to order, or cooking the eggs on the grill to order. Grill must be maintained on site to be evaluated as a part of the inspection and visits going forward as a part of the grill bill approval. Today, grill was stored at an off-site storage area and was unable to be evaluated. Failure to comply with all permit conditions will result in permit action. 

Additional permit violations noted/relevant to the inspection today:
Establishment does not have a type l hood. Cooking that produces grease laden vapors is prohibited per building code.
Induction burner is approved for cooking vegetable soups, boiled quinoa, and boiled eggs only. Consult Mecklenburg County Mechanical Inspector for
more information.

Establishment is provisionally approved to cool small batches of quinoa and boiled eggs with use of ice bath and direct ice method. Soups will be discarded at the end of each business day. Observations of cooling violations may require this approval to be rescinded by MCHD.

6/27/25- Permit amended by C McKenzie to reflect approval for establishment to use grill bill N.C.G.S. 130A-248(c2). Approved menu items include bacon, eggs, pancakes, and french toast. This approval does not cover any aspects regulated by other jurisdictions. Owner is responsible for ensuring this establishment meets applicable building, fire, city water, and zoning codes.

301 S COLLEGE ST SUITE CSL5
 
CHARLOTTE, NC 28202
rows.general_comments:
Note: Removed cold smoked salmon from menu. No undercooked proteins served. Dish machine is not dispensing sanitizer. Facility moved to single service items only until fixed. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days. 

Pasteurized eggs used only. No raw shelled. 

Facility hot seals bags of soups and sauces. Items are cooked, cooled, bagged and heat sealed. No vacuum is pulled on the bags. EHS saw air in bags. No items are hot bagged. 

Ambient air temp of the walk in cooler behind the dish pit area was 44F. Items in the walk in cooler were temping the same. Facility voluntarily discarded all TCS items that were not in temp. PIC called for maintenance. Facility has the capacity and space to function without. Facility has 3 walk in coolers and 2 walk in freezers. Items discarded: approximately 13 packs salami, 13 pks turkey, 2 boxed yogurt, 4 cases of liquid eggs, 6 cartons buttermilk, 3 cases egg yolks, 6 cases tomatoes, 1 bag cooked beets, 4 cases of raw chicken, among other items.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf Observed issues with cold holding, sanitizing dishes, TPHC and date marking. EHS educated PIC on all topics. 

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P Observed dish employee washing dishes without sanitizer. Dishes were being run through the dish machine, however, sanitizer was not pulling. PIC called maintenance. Facility will switch to single service dishes only. VERIFICATION REQUIRED WITHIN 3 days. Dishes sanitized in the 3 comp sink after washing in the dish machine. 
4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed can opener and stacks of pans soiled with old food debris. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed sweet potatoes, roast beef, dill sauce, barley, yogurt, tomatoes and feta cheese in the prep top unit at bistro holding above 41F. CDI- All TCS items out of temp voluntarily discarded. PIC will not use WIC until fixed.

rows.general_comments:
Per discussion with PIC, it was made known that caramelized onions may be cooked at home and brought to facility at times. Cooking food or obtaining food from an unapproved source per 3-201.11 is unacceptable. Refrain from cooking items outside facility going forward.

The use of commercial cooking equipment that produces grease-laden vapors without an exhaust hood and automatic fire suppression system is strictly prohibited under NC fire and mechanical codes. Facility must cease use of electric fryers until speaking with plan review.

Inspection led by REHS Ericka Jolley.

violations.comments:
2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection.
Observed PIC with no CFPM on duty at time of inspection -1-

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P 
Observed raw shell eggs in WIC stored atop mushroom. Observed raw shell eggs stored above pre-portioned sauce cups in RIC on line. CDI - PIC restored proper storage order. -1.5-

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
Observed tubs of sliced meats (roast beef & ham) cooling in WIC with tight fitting lids not meeting appropriate cooling rate. See temperature chart. CDI - PIC removed lids and re-located tubs of meat to WIF to rapidly cool.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P
Observed French fries intended for hot hold below 135F. CDI - EHS discussed placing French fries on TPHC if they are being hot held. Otherwise, going forward facility will strictly cook fries to order. Fries were placed on TPHC at time of inspection.

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed 1 jug of milk in RIC on cook line with no date marking. Per PIC, milk had been open for 48 hrs. CDI - PIC placed date marking on milk jug.

33 - Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control: 3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Also Observed container of pork in metal container piled above chill line and densely packed not allowing air to flow. CDI.. Items were voluntarily discarded.

violations.comments:
4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. Observed shelving in various areas used for storage chipping and/or rusted. 
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. Observed raw wood used to line shelf underneath of microwave.

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments: 4-302.14 Provide a test kit that accurately measures sanitizer concentrations. -Pf Observed no quat sanitizer test strips on site. Facility has a quat dispenser they were using at time of inspection (see #16). Provide quat test strips or discontinue use of quat sanitizer. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days by 8/7 to ensure test strips in place for sanitizer in use.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed significant build up on equipment throughout including but not limited to shelving, speed racks, sides/exteriors of equipment, interior of microwave, and on gaskets of refrigeration. Ensure thorough and more frequent cleaning.

5-205.15 Maintain a plumbing system in good repair. Observed 3-comp sink hot water knob/valve broken and unable to turn off to temper water for sanitizer dispenser. 
5-202.14 Prevent backflow or back siphonage prevention devices installed shall meet American Society of Sanitary Engineering standards. -P Observed pistol grip sprayer and hose with water left on coming from mop sink. Provide high pressure back flow or disconnect hose when not in use. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days by 8/1 to ensure no back flow concern.

6-101.11/6-201.11 Floors, walls and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable. Floors shall be non-absorbent in areas subject to moisture. Observed unfinished dry wall above mop sink area. Observed flooring is severely damaged, peeling, pitted, and no longer smooth and easily cleanable throughout. 
6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed dust build up in hard to reach areas of facility including walls, ceiling tiles and AC vents. Observed debris and other small items on floor throughout kitchen in hard to reach areas. Observed build up on floor in corners and underneath/between larger pieces of equipment.

violations.comments:
4-702.11 Utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use, after cleaning.-P 
Observed back prep counter with knives blades sitting out stated to be sanitized with Ecolab peroxide multi-surface cleaner, which is not a sanitizer.
CDI- EHS advised all staff present on which chemicals onsite are sanitizers (quat and bleach are available, and test strips). EHS advised that sanitizing must come after the cleaning step at the required frequency for food contact surfaces. Bleach mix made, labeled, and used to sanitize food contact surfaces. (-1.5)

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed can of sausage gravy stated to be opened on Sunday without date mark.
CDI- PIC labeled gravy. EHS advises labeling all TCS once opening unless to be used within 24 hours. (-0)

REPEAT.
5-205.15 Maintain a plumbing system in good repair.
Observed hand sink slow to drain and basin nearly overflowing after just one 20 second hand wash cycle. Restore hand sink drainage. (-1)

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed salami dated 7/18, potato salad without a date, ham 7/21, turkey 7/17, roast beef 7/20, chili 7/27-8/5, salsa 7/27-8/5, spinach dip dated 8/2, salsa cups dated 7/6. EHS found some items dated with discard date and some items dated with prep date. To maintain consistency and ensure dates are being discarded by the expiration date, pick either discard date, prep date or both. Do not write prep date on some items and discard on others as this can make the date marking system confusing to employees. During visit employees could not tell EHS which dates were which. More training needed on date marking. CDI- Potato salad and spinach dip dated for correct date. All other items discarded. Items held for more than 24 hours should be dated. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 

-Observed chicken wrap in front lowboy above 41F. All other TCS foods in the cooler were properly cold holding at or below 41F. Observed date mark sticker on wraps stating that they were prepped this morning, approximately 2 hours ago. -CDI- PIC moved wraps into WIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed wraps at 41F.

-Observed pasteurized egg carton in cold drawer above 41F. Observed all other food in cold drawers properly cold holding at or below 41F. Observed ambient temperature of cold drawers at 35F. -PIC stated pasteurized egg is held on ice during breakfast service, and at 10:30am, the breakfast station is closed and the egg cartons are moved into the cold drawers. PIC stated the egg carton was likely left at room temperature during the breakfast closing procedures (less than 1 hour ago). -CDI- PIC moved egg carton to WIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed egg carton at 41F. 

-Ensure food is properly cooled down to 41F or below before placing in expo reach-in coolers, as these coolers are opened frequently and are not efficient at cooling foods. -Do not leave pasteurized eggs at room temperature for extended periods of time. Ensure food is placed immediately in cooler/cold drawers after removing it from ice to ensure it maintains cold holding temperature (41F or below).


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

3-202.15 Food packaging must be in good condition, intact and protect the food inside. Pf - Observed one can of hoisin sauce to be stored on the dry storage rack with excessive dents along the top and bottom seams.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed a container of raw squid and raw tuna to be stored on the top shelf of the WIC above containers of RTE salsas, sauces, cooked birria, and cooked chicken.

CDI - PIC rearranged storage order to place raw items on the bottom shelves below all RTE items.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. - Observed an insert container of raw burgers to be stored behind an insert container of raw squid in the refrigerated drawers beneath the stovetop. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC rearranged storage order in the refrigerated drawers.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed an insert container of raw tuna to be stored in the cookline lowboy at a temperature of 64F. PIC was unable to state why or for how long the item was out of temperature for.
- Observed thawed ROP packages of raw tuna in the sushi bar lowboy refrigerator at temperatures of 45F and PIC was unable to state how long the items were out of temperature for.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded all out of temperature raw tuna.

- Observed trays of raw shrimp, raw yellowtail, and kani to be in the sushi display case at temperatures of 44-46F. PIC stated nothing is kept in the case overnight and it is brought up into the case upon opening at 11am.

CDI - Trays moved to the WIF to rapidly cool and observed at 41F 30 mins later.

- Observed an insert container of prepped/plastic wrapped fresh basil rolls to be at a temperature of 55-57F in the lowboy refrigerator across from the kitchen entrance. PIC stated that they had just made the items prior to the EHS arrival and that staff is supposed to place the items into the cooler following prep to cool down to 41F before bringing up to the line.

CDI - Plastic wrapped fresh basil rolls moved to a sheet pan and placed into the WIF to rapidly cool and observed at 39F 1 hour later. 

- Observed containers of shredded mozzarella and shredded mixed cheeses to be stored in the top refrigerated drawer beneath the flattop grill at temperatures of 45-48F. PIC stated that nothing is kept in the drawers overnight and EHS observed the drawers being opened and closed frequently for tacos during the lunch period. Other items in the rear of the drawer observed at 41F.

CDI - Containers of shredded cheeses moved to the WIC to rapidly cool.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed one insert container of house made coleslaw stored in the cookline lowboy refrigerator to have a date mark of 7/18, making today day 11. REPEAT.
- Observed a container of house made salsa roja to be in the WIC with a date mark of 7/21, making today day 8. REPEAT.

CDI - Past date items voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Toxic substances properly identified stored & used
violations.comments:
7-202.12(A) Use poisonous or toxic materials according to manufacturer's label. Use pesticides approved for use in commercial food service only.-P - Observed a canister of “Raid Ant & Roach” spray to be stored on the floor adjacent the food prep sink at the kitchen entrance. This pesticide is not commercially approved and states is for “household use only”. PIC stated using it for the floor drains to help with fruit flies.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments: 3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor. - Observed various fruits and vegetables to be stored directly on top of the wire storage racks in the cookline lowboys, without any barriers of protection.

3-304.12 (C ) Store in-use utensils on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment. The utensils and storage surface must be cleaned and sanitized every 4 hours. - Observed multiple knives to be stored in uncleanable crevices between the steamtable and the opentop refrigerators at the cookline.

3-304.12 (A) In-use utensils in TCS food, must be stored with handles above the food and top of the food container. - Observed a rice scoop to be stored with its handle in direct contact with the rice in the rice cooker.

CDI - Handle removed.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf PIC stated he came in this morning and walk-in cooler was above 41F. PIC did not discard the TCS foods that were out of temperature. CDI - PIC educated on when to discard food. TCS foods must be discarded if it has been out of temperature for 4 hours or more. 

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

violations.description: Proper eating, tasting, drinking or tobacco use
violations.comments: 2-401.11 (A). Employee beverages must be stored in a designated area where contamination of food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and single-use articles cannot occur. Employee drink stored on prep table. Employee drinks must be stored separately from food prep areas. REPEAT

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P Container of raw fish stored on top of box of fries in walk-in cooler. Do not store raw animal foods above ready-to-eat foods. CDI - PIC corrected storage order. 0 pts.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-703.11 After cleaning, equipment, food contact surfaces, and utensils shall be sanitized using an approved method.-P Employee was washing and rinsing utensils and did not use sanitizer after washing and rinsing. CDI - Employee educated on wash, rinse and sanitize process and she filled sink with chlorine sanitizer solution.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P All TCS foods in walk-in cooler measured 44-52F. TCS foods in cold holding shall measure 41F or less. CDI - PIC voluntarily closed and discarded out of temp TCS foods. Establishment may re-open once walk-in cooler is repaired and holds below 41F.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments: 2-301.14 (G) Wash hands when switching between working with raw food and working with Ready to Eat Food. - P Employee on grill was switching between handling raw meat and cracking raw eggs with gloved hands, and then went to handling plates and ready-to-eat foods without washing hands in between. Employees must wash hands in between handling raw animal foods and handling ready-to-eat foods or clean plates. CDI - Employee educated on when to wash hands and he washed hands. REPEAT

4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. Dish machine was only reaching 139F on EHS plate thermometer. Establishment must use sanitizer to sanitize dishes after washing and rinsing until dish machine is repaired. VR - Verification required within 3 days that dish machine has been repaired. REPEAT

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Chili and gravy measured 117-122F and 126-135F in hot holding. TCS foods in hot holding shall measure at least 135F. CDI - PIC reheated items to above 165F.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: No bare hand contact with RTE foods or pre- approved alternate procedure properly followed
violations.comments:

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed trays of raw salmon, raw bone in filets, raw burgers, and raw NY strip steaks to be cooling at rates <.083 degrees/min in the cookline 3 door lowboy. PIC stated having the trays out prior to and upon the EHS arrival to count the inventory on the product before placing them into the lowboy, which is a unit not designed nor approved for rapid cooling. EHS advised the PIC that if this is the normal protocol they should take temperatures of the product following the inventory count to ensure that they have not risen in temperature before placing into the lowboy on the cookline. All items in the lowboy overnight were observed at 38F or less. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC relocated all out of temperature and cooling trays of raw products to the WIC to rapidly cool.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-304.12 (B) In-use utensils for food that is not TCS must be stored with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed. - Observed scoops used for the bulk bins of flour and breadcrumbs to be stored with their handles in direct contact with the food inside.

CDI - Scoop handles removed and stored so that the handle is not in contact with the food inside.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed items(cut chicken, whipped feta, diced feta, and mozzarella) make units without any date marks present. violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed chicken salad and diced tomatoes cooling in WIC, tightly wrapped and covered with plastic lid. EHS observed one degree change after 35 minutes of cooling for chicken salad and 4 degrees of change for dice tomatoes. EHS determined both rates inadequate for cooling (see temp chart). EHS provided education. CDI - PIC removed plastic covering and lid and stirred product to promote fast cooling. EHS verified adequate cooling rate prior to ending inspection. REPEAT. (1)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses. EHS observed in use wiping cloths being held in sanitizer at 0ppm. CDI -PIC instructed food employee to discard all sanitizer and re-fill all in use containers. (0)

PIC stated unit has a bad compressor and is scheduled to be fixed tomorrow morning. PIC stated temperatures are being checked frequently to avoid items being above 41F. PIC was able to verify most items with temp logs conducted at 10:45am. EHS observed ricotta being stored over ice on make line. EHS observed ricotta over 41F (see temp chart). PIC stated ricotta is checked frequently and had been placed into ice thirty minutes prior to inspection. EHS provdied education; PIC stated facility will reduce amount stored on ice, switch to metal pans, and ensure enough ice is applied to allow for adequate cold holding. PIC removed spring mix, pizza sauce, and goat cheese to WIC to quickly cool; these items were verified at 10:45 with temp logs and observed below 41F. Bechemel was not checked this morning during line checks and was voluntarily discarded. Ricotta was taken to blast chiller to quickly cool. EHS will return tomorrow or verify repairs with unit. EHS instructed facility to utilize TPHC for a temporary solution until unit can be repaired. 3-DAY VR required. (1.5)
