3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed tomatoes, turkey, ham, chicken, pastrami, roast beef, American cheese, provolone cheese, cold holding above 41F in prep top. EHS checked ambient temp with thermometer along with the foods. PIC stated they do temp checks every morning and food was in proper temperature this morning. violations.comments:
2-301.14 (E) Wash hands after handling soiled equipment or utensils. -P- Observed food employee washing soiled equipment and dishware and then proceed to go and work at the fryer station engaging in food handling with no hand wash in between. -CDI- EHS made PIC aware of observation, PIC went over to the food employee coached him on what occurred, and had him properly wash hands prior to engaging back to food handling. Contamination prevented prior to occurrence. 
Ensure proper handwashing of staff, and ensure that staff is properly trained.

4-702.11 Utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use, after cleaning. -P- Observed a soiled metal pan sitting at the 3-comp sink. Pan was grabbed by a food employee, rinsed with the spray arm, and then about to be used for food prep. Visual soiling was still present on the pan prior to usage. -CDI- EHS informed PIC of observation. PIC stopped food employees from putting food in the container, took the dish to the 3-comp, W/R/S the dishware prior to usage. 
Ensure all food contact surfaces that are soiled are properly W/R/S prior to usage. 





For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P- Observed 2 full large metal containers of chicken in HH adjacent to drive thru, metal containers of chicken were all holding below 135F. EHS asked how long the facility will hold chicken under the light the PIC stated 1-hour prior to discard for quality, and stated chicken should be hot at 140F or above per SOP. -CDI- Chicken was voluntarily discarded by PIC. 
Ensure that food in hot holding is maintained at 135F and above. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

Observed approximately six (6) stacks of boxed food items (dry crackers and chips, frozen bread) stored on floor of dry storage area and walk in freezer, respectively. Elevate food items as required. REPEAT.

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments: 4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed four (4) stacks of recently delivered single service articles (Take-out containers) stored less than 6 inches off floor. Per conversation with PIC, containers were delivered earlier on day of inspection. Elevate as needed.

violations.description: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
violations.comments: 5-501.113(B) Keep dumpster, outside waste containers covered with tight-fitting lids or doors. Observed top loading door of dumpster unable to be closed. All other doors and lids at waste receptacles were properly closed. Contact waste management company to repair or replace jammed waste receptacles.

rows.violation_text:
16 - Food-contact surfaces: cleaned & sanitized: 4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. Observed minor buildup within interior of ice machine. Clean as needed to avoid contamination.

22 - Proper cold holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed one (1) portion of TCS food (sliced tomatoes) in ice bin at prep line with highest portion at 56F. Per date mark observation and conversation with PIC, tomatoes were prepared approximately 1 hour prior to EHS arrival. CDI - PIC rotated tomatoes to produce WIC (walk in cooler) for corrective cooling. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

CDI - PIC voluntarily disposed of out of date TCS foods. REPEAT.

Note: No escalation in point deduction due to noted improvement; observed no prepared portions of food requiring date marking and fewer out of date portions of food. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

CDI - after remixing sanitizer at three compartment sink, sanitizer was observed at 300 ppm.

Observed four (4) stacks of recently delivered single service articles (Take-out containers) stored less than 6 inches off floor. Per conversation with PIC, containers were delivered earlier on day of inspection. Elevate as needed.

violations.comments:
2-301.15 Only wash hands in handwashing sink. -PF
Observe food handler attempt to wash hands in vegetable prep sink. CDI - PIC re-educated and guided food handler to wash hands in hand wash only sinks.

violations.description: No bare hand contact with RTE foods or pre- approved alternate procedure properly followed
violations.comments:
3-301.11(B) Do not contact exposed ready-to-eat food with bare hands. Use suitable utensils, single-use gloves or dispensing equipment. -P 
Observed food handler stir RTE noodles with bare hands. CDI - EHS guided food handler to wash hands and re-heat noodles to 209F. -2-

6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf
Observed 1 handsink with no means to dry hands at the beginning of inspection. CDI - food handler placed new roll of paper towels at handsink.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. 
Observed WIF with pork being stored in a box that previously stored raw chicken. CDI - PIC removed pork from box and placed into a tub.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P 
Observed WIF with raw chicken stored above wontons and they were not in the original package. CDI - PIC restored storage order. 
-1.5-
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed no date marking being done throughout facility at time of inspection. 10 DAY VR Required to ensure date marking system is established and followed consistently. -1.5-

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P
Observed sushi rice not labeled with TPHC upon entry. CDI time stamp added when rice finished cooking. 

3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. 
Observed PIC labeling all food items with start and end time of 11-3. It was noted that all food items were placed on the line prior to 11 as they were already there at the start of inspection. EHS inquired about TPHC forms and PIC could not produce them, other than for sushi rice. CDI - EHS and PIC sat down to re-educate and re-evaluate which items are in need of TPHC and how to follow procedures properly. TPHC form was sent via email for PIC to fill out. Verification required.

violations.description: Toxic substances properly identified stored & used
violations.comments:
7-101.11 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials and personal care items shall bear a legible manufacturer's label. - Pf
Observed 1 bottle of cleaning chemical bearing no identifying label. CDI - PIC placed label to identify contents.

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water.
Observed 3 packages of thawing intact ROP fish in sushi RIC. Per manufacturer, fish shall be removed from ROP and thawed under refrigeration or cold running water. CDI packages cut opened.

rows.general_comments:
Facility utilizes spirulina powder. Additive is approved.

Prior to the next inspection, foods shall either be prepared in the establishment or obtained from an alternate approved source.

6 - Proper eating, tasting, drinking or tobacco use: 2-401.11 (A) Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and other items needing protection can not result. Observed staff drink on counter of cook line

10 - Handwashing sinks supplied & accessible: 6-301.14 Post a handwash sign at each handsink. Repeat-Observed no hand wash signs in hall bathrooms. Note- Staff bathroom is unavailable do to undergoing a renovation and the hand sink has been pulled out of the room.

15 - Food separated & protected: 3-302.11 (A)(4) Except when the food is being cooled, store food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. Observed unwrapped apples in the grab n go basket. Fruits with edible skins must be washed and individually wrapped if going to serve as grab n go. CDI-apples taken back to kitchen.

21 - Proper hot holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed undercooked eggs (sunny side up, over easy) hot held for service. Undercooked eggs cannot be hot held since they never met minimum cook temperatures. The only way to serve sunny side up eggs or over easy eggs that have been hot held is to use pasteurized eggs. If regular eggs must be cooked to order. CDI-eggs discarded



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed tuna salad date marked 7/14. Should have been discarded on 7/20. CDI-voluntarily discarded PIC believes it was misdated but no proof.

Cooked to order food must be asterisked and then the reminder statement needs the asterisk at the beginning of the sentence. VR required

40 - Personal cleanliness: 2-302.11 (B) Unless wearing intact gloves in good repair, a Food Employee may not wear fingernail polish or artificial fingernails when working with exposed food. - Pf. Observed staff with one glove on plating breakfast plates. Staff had both nail polish and artificial nails.

2-303.11 Remove jewelry on hands and arms while preparing food. A plain ring, such as a wedding band, is allowed. Observed staff with watch on handling food.

41 - Wiping cloths: properly used & stored: 3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses. Observed wiping cloth on counter, keep in sanitizer between uses.

45 - Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used: 4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed single service ware stored in dirty containers with eating side up. Store in clean containers with handles up.

49 - Non-food contact surfaces clean: 4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed cubby area behind line greasy, clean-up grease more frequently.

55 - Physical facilities installed, maintained & clean: 6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed ceiling flaking paint.

56 - Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used: 4-301.14 Hood systems and devices shall be in sufficient number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on equipment, walls, and ceilings. Observed hood area greasy, grease dripping, ceiling with grease splatters.

violations.comments:
REPEAT.
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P 
Observed grilled chicken breast and plantains below 135F in hot box. 
CDI- Temperature on hot box increased, foods reheated at stove above 165F before returning to hot holding. EHS discussed ensuring hot box’s is not overfilled, and is at the correct setting when being used for hot holding. (-3)

NOTE: This is the third consecutive violation for hot holding at this piece of equipment. If out of compliance at the next inspection, a risk control plan may be initiated. PIC encouraged to reach out with questions or support needs.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed sliced tomato’s in WIC and stick butter in lowboy at 43F. PIC explains both doors have been recently opened to load morning foods. 
CDI- Temperature deceased below 41F within 35 minutes. EHS advises staff to lower equipment temps, carefully monitor the TCS foods inside, keep doors closed as much as possible, and use shallow, metal containers where possible. Foods must remain at 41F in cold holding. (-0)

Observed torn caulking with dark stains on right side of prep sink across from cook line. Replace so fixture is cleanable and prevents entry of moisture. (-0)

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf Observed more trianing needed for coffee station employee. Employee is the only person at the coffee bar the entire shift. Observed violations with cold holding, date marking, employee health, hand washing and TPHC. EHS explained each topic to manager and employee and left copies of job aids/ food safety forms. 

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

2-301.14 (I) Wash hands after engaging in other activities that contaminate hands. -P Observed employee working at the register with customers then switch to making food and drinks without hand wash several times. CDI- Hands washed. EHS educated employee on when to wash and wash procedure. EHS also left hand wash signs in English and Spanish.

violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF- *Observed - No proof of training for staff regarding foodborne illnesses and symptoms. *CDI - EHS provided copy of employee health policy and reporting agreement for PIC to have current and future staff read, sign and date.

For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

*REPEAT* 3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D).

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. EHS observed lobster sauce cooling in WIC above 70F (see temp chart). PIC stated sauce was started at 9:30a and finished cooking at 10:00a. PIC stated neither cooking or cooling temperatures were documented. Based on the last known time when food was removed to be prepared, EHS advised sauce has not properly cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F. EHS observed sauce uncovered in WIC, however, EHS observed minor film on sauce and advised that active stirring and monitoring should be implemented to ensure long term compliance with cooling. CDI - Due to missing cooling parameter, PIC voluntarily discarded sauce. (0)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed cooked onions, raw seabass, raw hamburger beef, steak, and crab cakes above 41F during inspection (see temp chart). These items were located in the front compartments of sliding doors of low boy cooler at grill and low boy compartment of make unit. EHS advised that due to the high heat in the summer combined with the kitchen, that cabinet drawer cooling compartments can fluctuate when used frequently. PIC stated a line check was just conducted but temperatures of TCS foods in cabinet drawers were not observed. CDI - Due to not being able to verify how long these items were above 41F, PIC decided to voluntarily discard all items. EHS allowed PIC to keep raw burger meat due to being 45F. EHS advised to monitor temperatures of cabinet drawers coolers, during the summer especially, to ensure long term compliance for cold holding. (1.5)

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed lobster sauce prepared in house which failed to meet cooling parameters. EHS observed sauce left open in WIC, but observed thin film over sauce. PIC stated sauce was prepared by morning employee and left in WIC. EHS advised to continuously stir and monitor temperatures to ensure compliance with cooling parameters and methods. EHS observed raw shrimp cooling in WIC from being thawed and portioned, PIC stated this item was just portioned 30 min prior to inspection. EHS observed shrimp portioned in plastic bags and stored in WIC to cool. EHS observed double stacked pan of portioned shrimp with ice pan on bottom. EHS observed temperature of shrimp in contact with ice bath under 41F. However, EHS observed temperature of container not in contact with ice only decreasing 3 degrees in 30 minutes. EHS advised to spread out portioned shrimp onto sheet pans or place all in ice bath to quickly cool. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded lobster sauce due to missing cooling parameters, PIC spread shrimp out onto ice bath to ensure adequate cooling. (0.5)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed a bowl containing raw shelled eggs to be stored on the shelf in the WIC adjacent to and above opened packages of sliced/shredded cheeses. violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments:
3-403.11 (A),(D) Reheat all TCS foods to 165F within 2 hours if food is to be hot held until service. -P - Observed 2 container of rice to be slowly reheating in the tabletop steamtables at a rate of .833 degrees/min, which would result in the rice to not reach 165F within the required 2 hour reheating timeframe. Rice was observed at 66F after 30 mins of reheating. PIC stated this is a new process of reheating the rice as they’re trying to retain moisture after receiving complaints from customers that the rice is “crunchy”. EHS advised that the staff rapidly reheats on the stovetop before transferring to the steamtable.

CDI - Rice removed from steamtable and rapidly reheated on the stovetop to 165F+.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed an insert container of raw chicken to be at a temperature of 44F in the bottom refrigerated drawer at the cookline. All other items in the drawer were observed at 41F or lower. Container found at 44F was a small container at the front of the drawer and the drawer is opened and closed frequently, causing the product to warm up during lunch service. Staff confirmed that it had not been in the unit for longer than 1 hour.

CDI - Container moved to the WIC for rapid cooling.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed a container of cooked brussel sprouts to be date marked for 7/10. After conversations with the PIC and the staff they had mislabeled the container and it was from 7/19 with the prep staff member getting their dates mixed up. 

CDI - Container of brussel sprouts redated for correct date.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P EHS observed chicken burritos in hot box under 135F (see temp chart). PIC showed EHS temperature log. Temperatures taken at 8:45 detailed chicken for burritos were observed at 190F. PIC stated the burritos were prepared today by wrapping cold/hot ingredients to then be held in hot box prior to taking to the cafe upstairs for lunch service. PIC stated time begins when the food is taken from hot box to be sent upstairs. EHS advised that during this time(prior to placing on time) the burritos would need to be held at 135F or above, or time would need to be documented. PIC stated that would hinder operation due to lunch prep being conducted earlier in the day. 4-hours from that point would not last the full service. EHS advised to either keep items hot and monitor temperatures prior to placing on time, or beginning time earlier to account for time in between service. CDI- PIC reheated burritos in oven to 165F. EHS observed burritos at 165 within 15 minutes. (1.5)

2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF - Observed the facility to have signed employee health agreements on site but the agreements on site only had 5 reportable illnesses and not the required 6. Non-typhoidal salmonella was observed to be missing from the current signed forms.

CID - EHS provided updated copies of employee health policies with all 6 reportable illnesses.

For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed an insert container of raw clams to be stored on the top shelf of the lowboy refrigerator across from the stovetop, directly above containers of cooked vegetables. REPEAT.

CDI - Storage order rearranged, clams moved to the bottom shelf.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed containers of rosemary butter, miso butter, and scampi butter to be stored on the prep table adjacent the steamtable at temperatures of 70-76F. PIC stated that all butter mixtures are made from unsalted butter.

CDI - PIC placed items on temporary TPHC and time stamped the items for discard. EHS held conversations with the PIC on switching to salted butter or permanently holding the items on TPHC going forward to remain in compliance. New TPHC form would be required to be filled out if they opt to go with that method.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed an insert container of cooked vegetables to be stored in the cookline lowboy across from the stovetop and was not provided with a date mark of any kind. PIC stated that the vegetables were from the night before.

CDI - PIC date marked item.

- Observed an insert container of cut sausage to be stored in the cookline lowboy across from the stovetop with a date mark of 7/10, making today day 11. PIC stated it was for a pasta dish that he is no longer serving.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed an insert container of roasted corn to be at a temperature of 49F in the cookline opentop across from the stovetop. PIC stated that they had just cut the corn recently and that it was out of refrigeration during that time. The opentop refrigerator is a unit that it not designed nor approved for rapid cooling and following cutting/prep all items should be cooled back down in the WIC.

CDI - PIC relocated to the WIC where it was observed at 41F an hour later.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. violations.comments:
3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P Observed items on TPHC on the line prior to being placed in TPHC holding above 41F. Items were on the line set up for TPHC. Time stickers had not yet been printed. Unit was not on. CDI- All items taken to blast chiller to be cooled. 
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf Observed no time stamp for items held on TPHC. CDI- PIC printed stickers once food was at/ below 41F. 
3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. Observed no procedures for items held on TPHC. CDI- Items added to procedures. 

TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

violations.comments:
4-602.12 (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure
Observed top of microwave cavity with food debris and in need of more frequent cleaning.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P
Observed fried jalapenos being held atop counter warmer (no hot holding method in place) and cooked potatoes in hot holding unit, both below 135F. PIC stated the facility does not use TPHC. CDI - PIC placed fried jalapenos in hot holding unit to bring up to 135F and voluntarily discarded cooked potatoes.

REPEAT
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed batter (containing milk), 3 containers of tomato slices, multiple bags of shredded cheese, liquid egg, raw shrimp, cooked mushroom, French toast batter (contains egg), cut melon in fruit mix, canned peppers, and cooked mushrooms being cold held above 41F. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded items that were not made and verified to be prepared same day of the inspection and for items that were verified to be prepped day of inspection were placed in WIF or WIC to rapidly cool below 41F. EHS advised PIC to ensure the unit isn’t holding too many items, which would preclude proper airflow throughout the unit. -3-

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed grill lowboy holding turkey and tomato bearing no date mark. CDI - PIC verified prep dates and placed stickers accordingly. 

REPEAT 
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed 1 pan of marinara in serving hot hold and 1 pan of marinara in 3 door standing RIC with prep date of 6/25, exceeding the 7 day parameter. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded marinara pans. EHS did not escalate points due to no increase in severity. -1.5-

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta.
Observed containers of unlabeled spices and products in squeeze bottles without working name. Label at earliest opportunity. (-1)

3-302.15 Wash fruits and vegetables prior to use.
Observed avocado on prep line with sticker in tact. PIC indicated they were washed prior to placing items on line.

Observed open make line tomatoes at 52F and lettuce at 45F. PIC stated that foods were prepped this morning, 2 hours prior. -CDI- Foods were moved into WIC to cool, foods were cooling at a proper rate. 
Observed cheese slices over stacked in PT 2 at 45F at the fill line and above, below the fill line the foods were 40F-41F. PIC stated that the cheese was prepped 2 hours prior. -CDI- Cheese moved into WIC to cool, foods were cooling at a proper rate. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed a lack of a date marking system for the carry over deli meats and cheese that were present in the deli case. EHS discussed when the foods in the deli case were prepared to which the PIC was able to answer. Foods were able to be back dated. EHS further discussed that if any foods held in the deli case over night that the foods shall be properly date marked. Ensure a consistent date marking system is established for the deli case. 
-CDI- Back dated foods that were not properly date marked. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P 
Observed 2 separate employees use bare hands to turn off the faucet after washing hands then prepare to work with food. -CDI- EHS coached on proper hand washing. Employees re-washed hands. (2 pts)

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing -Pf- Observed sponges, debris, and deli cup present in rear hand sink upon the EHS arrival. Ensure that hand sinks are used for hand washing only. -CDI- Items removed from hand sink.

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. Observed the inner portion of the ice machine with debris and residue present. Ensure that ice machine is cleaned, maintained as clean, and cleaning frequency is increased. 

4-703.11 After cleaning, equipment, food contact surfaces, and utensils shall be sanitized using an approved method.-P- Observed food employee at the 3-comp sink washing and rinsing soiled equipment. EHS did not observe a sanitize step occurring. When EHS asked why the 3rd basin was not filled with sanitizer the PIC stated that the food contact surfaces are sanitized with a spray bottle of chlorine bleach and immediately rinsed. EHS notes that chlorine concentration was above 200PPM. EHS also notes that the contact time on the sanitizer manufacturers label states that dishes must soak for 2 minutes. -CDI- EHS coached food employee and PIC on proper sanitizing at the 3-Comp sink. PIC filled the sanitize basin with water and added chlorine bleach (liquid) per the manufacturers instructions for sanitizing food contact surfaces. After this was done the chlorine levels were reading at 100PPM. EHS told the PIC to write down this procedure and to train staff and check levels often enough to make sure that they are correct. Dishes were then placed back into the W/R/S process. 
Ensure proper W/R/S process is maintained and continued

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. - Observed the deli slicer to be stored as clean on a back prep table with visible food debris on the blade and the food contact surface of the pusher component. CDI - PIC broke down deli slicer and places all parts at the 3 compartment sink to be W/R/S.

REPEAT.

- Observed a bulk container of cooked pho noodles to have a date mark of 6/29 in the back cookline 2 door RIC. PIC stated that they don’t change the dates on the containers but cooked batches of the noodles every day or 2. The noodles on site today were prepared yesterday.

CDI - Date marks placed corrected on bulk container.

Facility is also getting lamb jus, veal jus and duck jus from something classic. All jus were previously removed form menu. See visit sheet 5/14/26. All other items will be cooked/ prepared with remaining in temperature food items. This is a temporary fix for the evening. Option not available for long-term based on safety standards.

violations.description: No bare hand contact with RTE foods or pre- approved alternate procedure properly followed
violations.comments:
3-301.11(B) Do not contact exposed ready-to-eat food with bare hands. Use suitable utensils, single-use gloves or dispensing equipment. -P Observed tomatoes being peeled with bare hands. CDI- Tomatoes voluntarily discarded. EHS explained to employee and manager that no bare hand contact is allowed for ready to eat foods. This is not the first time EHS has seen BHC at the facility. EHS has found manger Steffano BHC tomatoes for customer consumption previously (See educational visit 5/14/26).

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link: Handwashing and No Barehand Contact https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P observed raw seafood and unpackaged raw meat stored above unpackaged desserts and butter in tall reach in freezer. CDI- Storage order rearranged so that raw meats/ seafood is stored below ready unpackaged ready to eat food items. Observed cured egg yolks and marinated egg yolks in prep top stored on top of RTE items. CDI- cured egg yolks discarded (NOT AN APPROVED PROCESS. SEE VIOLATION #29). Marinated egg yolks placed on bottom.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed slicer heavily and can opener soiled with old food debris. CDI- Items taken to be cleaned. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed tomatoes, cured egg yolks, Roquefort, blue cheese (in prep top), Roquefort, lamb jus, duck jus, scallops, smoked salmon (low reach in), potatoes, dusk jus (tall RI 1), creme fraiche (store bought in tall tall RI 3). CDI- Items in prep top/ low reach in voluntarily discarded. All TCS items in 3 door tall reach in and 1 door tall reach in voluntarily discarded. Packaged and sealed items in 1 door tall reach in unit voluntarily discarded (Swiss cheese, whole milk, heavy cream, egg whites, liquid eggs, goat cheese and raw shelled eggs). Unit was holding at 48F. Tall reach in items voluntarily discarded. Observed 4 large pieces of cold holding equipment holding above 41F. Manager stated that the 6 door cold drawer unit (turned off) and the 2 door/ 3 cold drawer prep top units (48F) are in disrepair. EHS also found the 3 door tall reach in holding at 48F and 1 door tall reach in holding at 47F. All items out of temperature for over 4 hours were discarded. Facility will sell the remaining food in temp for dinner. Facility will not open next day until EHS has come to verify that units are fixed and food is safe for consumption. Facility has also changed menu to include the cooking and cooling of more items. See general comments. violations.comments:
3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. Observed no written procedures for TPHC. CDI- PIC had a blank copies of the template and filled out during inspection. 
3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P Observed food being removed from TPHC after 3.5 hours and placed in the tall reach in coolers for cold holding. CDI- All items on TPHC were discarded. EHS explained to manager that once an item in on TPHC it cannot be reverted back to temperature control. Items must be discarded only. 
3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P Observed foie gras and garlic confit placed on TPHC prior to being cooled to 41F. CDI- Items cooled to 41F in blast chiller.

violations.description: Compliance with variance, specialized process, reduced oxygen packaging criteria or HACCP plan
violations.comments:

After dehydration, egg yolks are removed from dehydrator and place in the refrigerator for holding. Eggs are then held for 3 days. CDI- Discarded. Eggs cannot be dehydrated at 90F overnight without a variance. Eggs can be cured in salt in the coolers holding at or below 41F and held for no longer than 7 days (this was the previous process discussed with managers and EHS).

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). Observed approximately nine (9) items in server RIC (salad bin and salad bowls) with door date marks denoting date of prep of 7/13. violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf -Observed cooked tempura shrimp held on 4-hour TPHC with no label identifying the time which the food was removed from temperature control. -CDI - PIC verified when shrimp tempera was originally removed from temperature control (11am) and properly added time stamp.

3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. violations.comments:

violations.comments:
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Cut cabbage in 2 large containers measured 49-50F. Employees stated it was prepared around 3 hours ago. Use ice as an ingredient instead of water so cabbage reaches 41F within 4 hours of preparation. Do not use drink coolers to cool TCS foods as they will not work as well as the freezer or commercial upright cooler. CDI - Employee added large amount of ice to both containers and the cabbage reached 41F within 4 hours of preparation. REPEAT

For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

rows.general_comments:
Establishment has until 08/10/2026 to meet the following transitional permit conditions:
1. Replace deteriorated green shelving with rubberized coating flaking/peeling off. (Done in WIC, still needed in dry storage)
2. Replace grease stained ceiling tiles in main kitchen.
3. Ensure walk in freezer and cooler doors self-close.
4. Replace warped gasket at walk in cooler. 
5. Remove unsealed wooden wall attachment to right of back hand sink. Replace with a cleanable and non-absorbent fixture, if needed.


An onsite visit will be made to confirm completion of transitional permit conditions on Friday, August 7th. PIC is encouraged to reach out with any questions or concerns in meantime.

violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments:
3-403.11 (B),(D) TCS food reheated in a microwave shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of 165 F within 2 hours and the food is rotated or stirred, covered, and allowed to stand covered for 2 minutes after reheating if food is to be hot held until service. -P
Observed rice noodles just completing commercial reheat for TPHC in microwave at 140F. EHS explained that due to reheat in microwave, commercial products reheated for TPHC or hot holding must reach 165F. (-0)
CDI- Noodles reheated to >165F before labeling for 4 hour TPHC at cook line.

3-202.12 Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.
Observed house made chili sauce stored in commercial package of another product, so sauce is not labeled with the proper food name. EHS advises PIC to purchase containers for storage of house made sauces and ensure they are labeled with product name. (-1)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed approximately eight (8) portioned bags of mozzarella in counter display cooler used to hold TPHC salads above 41F. violations.comments: 3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf Observed approximately seven (7) bags of portioned in house grated cheese blend (Asiago, Parmesan, and Romano) at counter top with no labeling. Per conversation with PIC, cheeses are portioned daily and voluntarily disposed of prior to the end of each shift. 3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. Store tags in chronological order for 90 days. -Pf

violations.comments: 6-301.11 Provide soap for handwashing at each handsink. -Pf Observed rear handsink (adjacent to 3 compartment sink) with clogged soap dispenser at time of inspection; soap within was observed dry and dispensing only in very small amounts. CDI - Food employee provided commercial hand soap bottle to be used for handwashing. EHS observed corrective handwashing performed by employee at newly restocked hand sink and effective handwashing throughout inspection.

4-602.12 (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure. Observed minor soils accumulation inside of microwave. Per conversation with PIC and observation, microwave is used to thaw wrapped and sealed raw animal foods, which are then fully cooked via stove top. Clean interior as needed.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed one (1) rice cooker of brown rice at temperatures between 127F and 133F. Per conversation with PIC, rice had been prepared on morning of inspection less than 30 minutes prior to EHS arrival. CDI - Food employee removed rice from pot and reheated to above 165F via wok at stove top. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). EHS observed proper use of date marking and labeling via white board and direct labeling in cold holding units (I.E. prep unit underside and WIC.) However, EHS observed one (1) TCS food item (sweet and sour chicken pieces) on whiteboard labeled as frozen on 6/29 and marked on bag as 6/24, while thawing in WIC at 38F. Per conversation with PIC, item had been improperly marked on bag based on white board, and thaw date had not been written on bag or board. CDI - EHS demonstrated thawing procedure by writing thaw date of 7/12 on whiteboard. Refine system used to track prep and thaw dates of TCS foods. REPEAT. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. violations.comments:
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P- Observed shredded lettuce that was prepared at 5:21 AM this morning per the sticker present on the lettuce. EHS took a temperature of the lettuce at 9:26 AM and the lettuce was 43F-44F. Lettuce was cooling in a lowboy in a tightly wrapped container. Ensure that ambient prepared foods cool to 41F within 4 hours. -CDI- lettuce was voluntarily discarded. 





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

rows.general_comments:
Arrived at facility, PIC stated they were having issues with the WIC which was not properly holding ambient or TCS items 41F and below. PIC stated that they had a temporary cold holding trailer with a lock delivered and in use since Saturday. PIC stated due to limited space in cold holding trailer, staff was utilizing WIC to cool items utilizing ice baths. During inspection observed some TCS items cooling in ice baths. Observed multiple TCS items (cut tomatoes, shredded cheese, cut lettuce), prepared earlier today (7:30 am), holding above 41F. All items throughout facility that were holding 41F and above were voluntarily discarded. 
Facility manager voluntarily closed facility and will not open until WIC has been successfully repaired.

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. - Observed no written procedures on site for the sushi rice that is held using TPHC. Item was observed properly time stamped and facility has had the document in the past but could not find it today.
- Observed no written procedures on site for the items at the wok line that are held on TPHC. As per the PIC the egg wash on the wok cart, the raw chicken, raw beef, raw shrimp, and cooked shrimp in the cookline opentop are all held using TPHC and are discarded if they last the 4 hours. All items were observed time stamped with an 11:30am time stamp except the egg wash, which was brought out of refrigeration at 11am when the facility opened. REPEAT.

CDI - Written procedures filled out for both the sushi rice and the wok line items at the end of the inspection. Egg wash time stamped for discard at 3pm

TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed a large bus bin of lo mein noodles to be cooling at a rate of .083 degrees/min and to miss the first cooling window with the noodles at 76F at the 2 hour mark. Bin was observed to be deeply filled, densely packed with noodles, and had plastic wrap covering the top of the container which all do not allow for adequate cold air flow around the product to facilitate proper cooling. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded due to it not reaching 70F within the first 2 hours of cooling.

- Observed approx 10-12 containers of smoked crab and a tray of kani to be observed at temperatures of 44-47F in the sushi counter lowboy refrigerator. As per the sushi employee all items were prepared that morning and immediately placed into the sushi lowboys to be used throughout the day. Date marks on the containers supported this statement. Containers of smoked crab were observed with tight fitting lids on and the tray of kani was observed with tight plastic wrap over the top of it, not allowing for adequate cold air flow around the product to facilitate proper cooling. Lowboy refrigerators are also not designed nor approved for rapid cooling and all cooling must be done in the WIC. REPEAT.
- Observed a container of cooked beef to be at a temperature of 94F in the cookline lowboy refrigerator and was observed to be actively cooling down per the cookline employee. Employee stated having cooked the item within the last hour before placing it in the lowboy, which is not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.
- Observed a container of lo mein noodles to be at a temperature of 66F in the cookline lowboy refrigerator and was observed to be actively cooling down per the cookline employee. Lo mein noodles were from the same bulk batch that was observed actively cooling in the WIC. Employees stated they needed noodles up at the cookline so they had taken from the batch still cooling and placed them in the cookline lowboy to use during lunch, which is not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.

CDI - PIC moved all items to the WIC to rapidly cool. Lids and plastic wrap removed from items.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

- Observed the bulk bins of sugar, flour, MSG, and rice in the dry storage area to not be labeled as to their contents.

Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed a large bus bin of lo mein noodles to be cooling at a rate of .083 degrees/min and to miss the first cooling window with the noodles at 76F at the 2 hour mark. Bin was observed to be deeply filled, densely packed with noodles, and had plastic wrap covering the top of the container which all do not allow for adequate cold air flow around the product to facilitate proper cooling. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded due to it not reaching 70F within the first 2 hours of cooling.

- Observed approx 10-12 containers of smoked crab and a tray of kani to be observed at temperatures of 44-47F in the sushi counter lowboy refrigerator. As per the sushi employee all items were prepared that morning and immediately placed into the sushi lowboys to be used throughout the day. Date marks on the containers supported this statement. Containers of smoked crab were observed with tight fitting lids on and the tray of kani was observed with tight plastic wrap over the top of it, not allowing for adequate cold air flow around the product to facilitate proper cooling. Lowboy refrigerators are also not designed nor approved for rapid cooling and all cooling must be done in the WIC. REPEAT.
- Observed a container of cooked beef to be at a temperature of 94F in the cookline lowboy refrigerator and was observed to be actively cooling down per the cookline employee. Employee stated having cooked the item within the last hour before placing it in the lowboy, which is not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.
- Observed a container of lo mein noodles to be at a temperature of 66F in the cookline lowboy refrigerator and was observed to be actively cooling down per the cookline employee. Lo mein noodles were from the same bulk batch that was observed actively cooling in the WIC. Employees stated they needed noodles up at the cookline so they had taken from the batch still cooling and placed them in the cookline lowboy to use during lunch, which is not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.

CDI - PIC moved all items to the WIC to rapidly cool. Lids and plastic wrap removed from items.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

37 - Food properly labeled: original container: 3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. - Observed all secondary containers used on the wok line rolling cart for spices, seasonings, and sauces to not be labeled as to their contents.
- Observed the bulk bins of sugar, flour, MSG, and rice in the dry storage area to not be labeled as to their contents.

38 - Insects & rodents not present; no unauthorized animals: 6-202.15 Protect outer openings of establishment from insect or rodent entry. - Observed the back door to the kitchen to not be fully closed, allowing for the potential entry of vermin into the facility. REPEAT.

CDI - Door closed.

- Observed a gap at the base of the back door when closed, allowing for the potential entry of vermin into the facility. REPEAT.

45 - Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used: 4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. - Observed multiple stacks of plastic to go containers and lids at the cookline to be stored with their food contact surfaces face up, allowing for the potential contamination of the food contact surfaces.

4-502.13 Single-use and single-service articles cannot be reused. - Observed plastic single service containers to be in use as bulk bin scoops throughout the facility.

47 - Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used: 4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. - Observed a cutting board to have large chunks missing, heavy scarring, and heavy staining which rendered it no longer easily cleanable.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

48 - Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips: 4-501.18 Maintain wash, rinse, and sanitize solutions clean. - Observed the wash basin of the 3 compartment sink to be filled and active warewashing to be going on at the time of the inspection and the wash water was observed to be heavily contaminated with food debris/grime. All dishes go through the chemical dishwasher after being hand scrapped/washed.

CDI - PIC changed solution and EHS discussed with staff the proper times to change the wash water.

49 - Non-food contact surfaces clean: 4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. - Observed the racks used in the dishwasher to have heavy accumulations of black grime. REPEAT.

56 - Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used: 6-305.11/6-501.110 Designate and use an area for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and possessions. - Observed a bin containing employee food and ingredients for employee meals such as raw pork to be stored on the middle shelf of the WIC, directly above boxes of raw vegetables to be used for consumers. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC relocated employee bin to lower shelf of the WIC.

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf. EHS observed hand sink by make line full of ice during inspection. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC removed ice from hand sink. REPEAT. (1)

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to dispense chemicals at proper concentration during inspection. PIC stated unit has only been used a few times this morning. PIC instructed food employee to prime unit and run another full cycle prior to checking. CDI - EHS observed proper concentration after unit was primed and a full cycle was ran. (0)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed all items in WIC above 41F during inspection. During initial assessment, EHS observed WIC at 43F, WIC quickly cooled to 41F within minutes. PIC stated food employee checked temperatures at 10:30am and everything was under 41F. PIC unable to locate today’s temperature logs. PIC stated the first employee that arrives to the kitchen is required to do a temperature check. Facility has installed data loggers in WIC to keep track of ambient temperatures. PIC showed EHS temperature line graph showing the last 24 hours of ambient temperature. EHS observed WIC has been above 41F for the last 24 hours. PIC stated due to temperature issues and information available from the data loggers, all TCS foods not prepared today will be voluntarily discarded. By the end of inspection, EHS observed WIC at 38F. EHS advised to complete temperature logs daily to ensure food temperatures are being documented. EHS did not observe any active cooling in WIC during inspection. EHS observed one item cooling in make unit during inspection. PIC stated items are placed into WIF to cool. All items in WIF at 41F or below. PIC voluntarily discarded all TCS foods in WIC that have been in unit overnight or longer than 4 hours. Repair technician arrived onsite as well to ensure unit is functioning as it should. Repair technician stated everything on unit is working properly. Repair technician stated that evaporator on unit is going bad but is still able to operate; part has already been ordered and will be installed within two days. EHS will conduct 3-day VR to observe long term compliance with cold holding. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

Risk Control Plan to be discussed if no improvement by next inspection.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-101.17 (A) Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a food contact surface. 
Observed cedar planks being used during the cooking process of the facilities Cedar Plank Salmon. PIC stated that Cedar Planks are single use and discarded. EHS explained to PIC and facility that the use or cedar planks for cooking, as a food contact surface is a process that requires prior approval from the state. Wood can only be used as a food contact surface if it is hard maple or an equivalently hard, close grained wood, and is used as a cutting surface, for confectionery operations as a paddle for scraping kettles, or as shipping containers for whole, uncut, raw fruits and vegetables and nuts in the shell. REPEAT -.5-
5-205.15 Maintain a plumbing system in good repair. Observed leak at pre-rinse at 3-comp sink, at drain under 3-comp sink, at hostess station ice bin. Repair. -0-

5-403.12 Liquid waste shall be disposed of in accordance with LAW. Observed condensate from smoker, rainwater near dumpster and drainage from roof through aluminum gutters near parking lot side entrance creating standing water pest harborages in parking lot. Also observed filter soaking barrel full of rainwater. Dispose of rainwater and other liquid waste in accordance perk law to prevent pest harborage. -0-

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
10 DAY VR.
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf 
Observed overall need for PIC to train staff on ware-washing processes. Staff not aware of which test strips should be used with which sanitizer, how to operate chemical dish machine, set up 3 comp sink properly, or able to identify sanitizer apart from soap. PIC must urgently retrain staff in proper ware-washing. A return visit will be made in 10 days to reassess staff and PIC on duty understanding of proper ware-washing. (-1)

REPEAT. 10 DAY VR.
4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Observed many dishes on rack above 3 comp sink stored as clean with visible grease residue/food debris, and black residue inside ice machine.
All dishes brought to ware-wash for re-w/r/s. A return visit will be made within 10p days to reassess ware-wash processes and ice machine. (-1.5)

4-702.11 Utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use, after cleaning.-P 
Observed no sanitizer at 3 comp sink dispenser, or sanitizer buckets set up for use with wiping cloths on prep surfaces throughout kitchen. Staff identify dawn dish soap as sanitizer when asked what is used for the sanitize step. 
CDI- EHS provided education on sanitizers and 3 comp sink ware-washing process. Quat sanitizer available at mop sink dispenser observed at proper concentration.

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
Observed two large containers of salsa in small lowboy at kitchen entrance which failed to reach 41F or below during overnight cooling.
CDI- Salsa’s voluntarily disposed of. (-1.5)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed ranch dressing and whipped cream in lowboy at 50F.
CDI- PIC voluntarily disposed. (-0)

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed sliced lettuce, diced tomatoes, and seafood medley in cook line fliptop without date marks, which was prepped yesterday. Also observed multiple date marking procedures in use; some TCS items dated with prep date, other with expiration date. EHS advises the PIC to ensure all staff are using the same date marking procedure, with ready to eat foods prepped and kept onsite longer than 24 hours all dated for no more than 7 days, with prep date as day 1. 
CDI- EHS verified prep date with chef and allowed dating of items. (-1.5)

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed tall containers of salsa cooling in lowboy, and stacked containers of portioned salsa cooling in fliptop above. Large containers failed to cool within 6 hours. EHS advises staff to cool foods in less dense, uncovered containers, which are not stacked; this allows entry of cold air. 
CDI- Salsa’s which failed to cool voluntarily disposed, portioned salsa relocated to WIC for rapid cooling, cooling methods discussed with staff. (-0.5)

violations.description: Insects & rodents not present; no unauthorized animals
violations.comments:
6-501.111 Keep the premises free of insects, rodents, and other pests.
Observed a live beetle in rinse compartment of 3 comp sink and several house flies and fruit flies in back of main kitchen. EHS verified regualr pest control services are provided. EHS advises increasing visit frequency and monitoring carefully. No contamination to food observed. (-0)

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments:
3-303.12(B)(C)(D) Unpackaged food may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice except: whole raw fruits or vegetables; cut raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, or potatoes; tofu; and raw poultry and raw fish received immersed in ice.
Observed containers of shredded lettuce in undrained water at several locations. EHS discusses with PIC and other staff need to store TCS produce without undrained ice or water. (-0)

3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses.
Observed many wiping cloths in use throughout establishment and no sani-buckets made up for their storage.
CDI- PIC sets up sani-buckets with quat. (-0.5)

3-304.12 (F) Containers of water used for storing in-use utensils must be maintained at a temperature of at least 135 F and cleaned at least every 24 hours or when container has accumulated soil or residue.
Observed utensils in 115F water at cook line. 
CDI- Water voluntarily poured out, utensils moved to ware-wash. EHS explains that utensils in warm water must be held hot at 135F or above. (-0.5)

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments:
4-903.11(C ) Single Service and Single Use items shall be kept in the original protective package or stored using other means that protect the item until used.
Observed many stacks of opened single service trays throughout kitchen removed from protective sleeve. EHS advises staff to keep single service articles in packaging or otherwise protected while awaiting use. (-0.5)

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
Observed all racks inside WIC severely rusted, no longer cleanable. Replace corroded racks. (-0.5)

4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair.
Observed lowboy upon entrance to kitchen with ambient temp in 50’s, not able to hold TCS foods. 
CDI- All cooling items relocated, PIC advised to call for work order and not store TCS foods inside until repaired and able to hold food at 41F and below.

violations.comments:
3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Salsa measured 49F in walk-in cooler. 3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Green salsa (110F) and queso (95F) were below 135F in hot holding. TCS foods in hot holding shall measure at least 135F. CDI - PIC reheated items to above 165F. 0 pts.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Pupusas in walk-in cooler measured 43-45F. Raw shrimp and raw tilapia in low boy cooler measured 54F and 50F. Pickled onions, raw shrimp, pico, and raw shrimp measured 45-50F in small sandwich cooler in between grills. PIC stated they got a truck 30 minutes ago from Sysco and the cooler door was propped open for 20 minutes while they put the food away. This caused the pupusas to warm above 41F. PIC also stated they were cleaning the bottoms of the both the other coolers this morning which probably caused the food to warm up. CDI - PIC moved items to walk-in freezer to cool quickly. REPEAT 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: No bare hand contact with RTE foods or pre- approved alternate procedure properly followed
violations.comments:
3-301.11(B) Do not contact exposed ready-to-eat food with bare hands. Use suitable utensils, single-use gloves or dispensing equipment. -P EHS observed food employee preparing RTE food into portioning bowl to hand to stir-fry cook. EHS observed food employee grabbing cooked noodles with bare hand. EHS intervened and instructed employee to stop, discard food, and wash hands. CDI - Food employee voluntarily discarded noodles, washed hands, and donned gloves prior to continuing working with RTE food. (2)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link: Handwashing and No Barehand Contact https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to properly dispense sanitizer at correct concentration. PIC ran a few full cycles and even primed unit. PIC contacted repair technician to schedule repairs and has switched to to-go orders only. Only single service items shall be used until unit can be repaired. EHS will conduct 3-day VR to observe compliance. (1.5)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed cut cabbage, cooked noodles, and raw eggs above 41F during inspection. EHS observed two containers of cut cabbage in WIC 2 (WIC closest to door) above 41F. This is the only TCS item facility stores in unit. EHS observed ambient temperature of unit at 42-43F. This unit never cooled below 41F during inspection. EHS observed cooked noodles and raw eggs in WIC 1 (middle WIC) above 41F. EHS observed ambient temperature at beginning of inspection at 44F, by end of inspection middle WIC was observed at 40F. Majority of TCS foods in middle WIC observed right at 41F during inspection. All other TCS items were observed actively cooling from being prepared at 3:00pm. PIC voluntarily discarded cooked noodles observed above 41F, raw eggs were placed into ice bath to quickly cool. PIC removed items cooling into WIF to finish cooling within time parameters. EHS observed ambient temperature of kitchen at 96F. PIC unable to verify if temperatures were taken today. PIC will contact repair technician to have both WIC assessed to ensure units can hold TCS foods at 41F during service. EHS will return in 3-days to assess units and compliance with cold holding. If temperatures issues are observed, facility could be placed on an immediate suspension or voluntarily close to repair units prior to operating. WIC 2 will only be used to store non-TCS foods until assessed. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments: 3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P EHS observed food employee placing cooked chicken on make line on TPHC. EHS observed this is the same fried chicken that was actively cooling in WIC. EHS asked food employee what temperature the chicken was and food employee verified temperature. EHS observed temperature of chicken at 48F. EHS provided education on TPHC. CDI - PIC placed chicken in WIF to quickly cool and stated chicken will be cooked to order until cooling has been completed. (0)

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed fried chicken, noodles, and cooked shrimp in WIC 1 cooling in large container covered with plastic wrap. EHS observed inadequate cooling rates during inspection. PIC stated typically items are cooled in smaller containers in WIF. CDI - PIC removed plastic wrap and stretched containers into smaller containers; placed all items cooling into WIF to quickly cool. EHS observed items below 41F prior to end of inspection. REPEAT. (1)

violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments: 3-403.11 (A),(D) Reheat all TCS foods to 165F within 2 hours if food is to be hot held until service. -P Observed meatballs reheating in steam table. PIC stated they start them in the microwave but that the target is at least 140F but not over 160F. The container of meatballs was being reheated for the second time and therefore must hit 165F. After 40 minutes, the meatballs had risen approximately 30 degrees and still had approximately 30 degrees left to go with 20 minutes left. CDI: Item continued to be reheated in the microwave to over 165F in the microwave. Meatballs going up to commercial reheat were also placed in the microwave due to them tracking to not make it to the required temperature as well. EHS recommended stirring throughout reheating processes. See temp chart.

cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.
