violations.comments:
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed tomatoes in walk in cooler prepared at 4:30am still above 41F. CDI: Tomatoes voluntarily discarded. EHS provided suggestions to PIC regarding cooling including but not limited to adding ice to the water after using veggie wash so the tomatoes remain 41F and below during preparation. Then, be sure to slice and place tomatoes in the walk in immediately after prep. EHS also discussed different placement of the tomatoes as they were right next to do the door. The facility received a large delivery this morning and they cleaned the walk in floors meaning the door was left open for some time with the tomatoes right at the door. Consider also uncovering tomatoes until fully cooled to 41F. 





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
violations.comments: 3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. Store tags in chronological order for 90 days. -Pf. Observed only one shellfish tag for oysters in the last 90 days. PIC indicated that other tags were accidentally discarded. CDI- by educating PIC on proper shellfish tag retention requirements.

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Observed carrots, potatoes, zucchini, plantains and cabbage cooling on counter upon arrival. All items were cooked at approximately 10:15-10:30am. PIC placed items over ice on counter. Ice bath was insufficient to properly cool foods in required time parameters. CDI- items placed in shallow pans in walk in cooler to ensure parameters were met. Repeat violation. If violations occur at next inspection a risk control plan will be required to be implemented. 



For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. -Observed raw katsu chicken stored above raw shrimp in the reach-in freezer. Raw katzu chicken was previously thawed and prepared at facility (breaded). -CDI- PIC corrected storage order. -No point escalation due to significant improvement in storage order noted in storage order since last inspection. All storage order in prep coolers and WIC was correct. -1/2 points-


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
-Observed prepped cream cheese in low reach-in cooler above 41F. All other foods in cooler were properly cold holding at or below 41F. Date mark showed cream cheese was prepped two days ago, and PIC stated cream cheese has not been removed from cooler since preparation date. -CDI- PIC lowered ambient temperature of cooler and EHS observed temperature of cooler drop to 36F. PIC voluntarily discarded the cream cheese.
-Observed steamed broccoli above 41F in wok prep top, stored in container directly on top of other foods. Broccoli was steamed this morning and needed for lunch service use. All other foods in the cooler were properly cold holding at or below 41F. -CDI- PIC moved steamed broccoli to WIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed broccoli cooling at sufficient rate to reach 41F within 6 hours of steaming. EHS recommended steaming broccoli a day in advance, so that the broccoli has sufficient time to cool in the WIC and be moved to the wok prep unit for use the next day.


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed approx 30-40 packages of various grab & go sushi rolls to be at temperatures of 43-47F in the sushi display case, sushi 2 door lowboy, and sushi sliding door lowboy. All rolls were prepared today at approx 8am. Sushi employee stated that there is less room in the shared WICs on Mondays so they use the other refrigerators to cool the prepped sushi rolls down. Lowboys, grab & go cases, and sliding door lowboys are all not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.

CDI - All actively cooling sushi rolls moved to the WIC, where they were then observed at 40F by 10:15am.

5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. - Observed the handwash sink in the cardinal cafe back room to be obstructed from use by a wiping cloth in its basin.

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments:
3-202.15 Food packaging must be in good condition, intact and protect the food inside. Pf - Observed a can of pumpkin with heavy dents along its seams and was stored on the can rack in the dry storage room of the banquet kitchen amongst wholesome cans.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed an insert container of raw shelled eggs to be stored on the speed rack in the club lounge prep kitchen RIC directly above insert containers of RTE cut leafy greens. REPEAT.
- Observed a package of cooked lobster meat to be stored on the same tray with insert containers of raw salmon filets in a way that would allow for the salmon filets to potentially contaminate the lobster package in WIC 3 in the banquet kitchen. REPEAT.

CDI - Storage order rearranged in the club lounge prep kitchen RIC and the banquet kitchen WIC 3.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed trays/containers of cut melon, onion cream cheese, plain cream cheese, yogurt, and cheddar cheese to be at temperatures of 45-51F on top of and adjacent to the cold plate at the club lounge buffet. EHS advised the PICs to place the items onto TPHC during both previous inspections but there has been a new executive chef during all 3 inspections resulting in this solution not being communicated to the staff of the club lounge. Breakfast buffet is only operational from 6:30am-10:30am. REPEAT.

CDI - Items time stamped for discard at 10:30am. EHS filled out TPHC document with the 2 sous chefs at the time of the inspection and explained the TPHC procedure to the staff in the club lounge. EHS reviewed the entire policy and how to properly document the time stamps with the staff.

- Observed a tray of cooked potato wedges to be at a temperature of 68F on a speed rack in the club lounge prep kitchen. Speed rack was outside of temperature control for an unknown amount of time and no employees were actively working with the items. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed a chub of ham to be in WIC 3 in the banquet kitchen and was not provided with a date mark of any kind. Prep staff stated opening the package yesterday (6/25).
- Observed a container of hard boiled eggs to be in the RIC adjacent the large dough mixer in the banquet kitchen and was not provided with a date mark of any kind. Prep staff stated that they had opened the package of hard boiled eggs the day before to make salads for the cardinal cafe grab & go.

CDI - PIC date marked items.

- Observed a container of sausage gravy mix to be in the banquet kitchen WIC 3 and was provided with a date mark of 6/13, making today day 14. Staff stated he had not been using it and had made fresh sausage gravy mix but had forgot to the throw away the old batch. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed approx 10 containers of arugula Greek salad to be cooling at a rate of 0.0 degrees/min in WIC 1 in the banquet kitchen. Items had their cooling process interrupted by the prep staff adding final ingredients, placing the lids on the containers, and moving them to the main floor kitchen 4 door RIC that is in the shared Dogwood kitchen space. All of these variables resulted in the salads to not cool down at all.

CDI - PIC had staff member bring all arugula Greek salads back down to the banquet kitchen, had the lids removed and placed back into WIC 1. EHS observed the items at 41F by 10am.

violations.comments:
3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed raw tuna stored over RTE sauces in sushi reach in unit. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order. (0)

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to dispense sanitizer during inspection. Facility has used dish machine since opening. PIC assessed unit and stated tubing installed on unit to deliver sanitizer has holes present and prevents the liquid from reaching unit. CDI - PIC was able to repair unit during inspection. EHS observed unit dispensing chemical at correct concentration prior to end of inspection. (0)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed numerous TCS items in WIC and 2-door sushi LB above 41F(see temp chart). After thirty minutes EHS observed no change in temperature. PIC stated on Wednesday ice build up was observed on back of unit in WIC. PIC stated units thermostat was adjusted to help with the freezing and must have been turned up too much. PIC stated yesterday WIC was observed at 42-43F, in response PIC turned unit back down. PIC was unaware the 2-door LB was in disrepair. PIC voluntarily discarded all TCS foods in WIC and 2-door LB and contacted repair technician. Due to additional refrigeration space and limited number of TCS items needed for service, facility will be allowed to temporarily operate while unit is being repaired. Facility will not be allowed to cook/cool any items until unit is repaired and must only store non-TCS foods inside WIC during this time, all other TCS foods shall be stored in extra units in kitchen area. All TCS items in sushi 2-door LB and WIC were voluntarily discarded. Sushi station has additional 2-door LB that is mainly used and all items can be sufficiently stored inside. EHS will return on Monday to ensure repairs have been done. If WIC has not been repaired, and IS will be issued. (1.5) *** Prior to EHS leaving facility EHS observed WIC at 40F, EHS advised facility to continue with what was previously discussed. Facility was advised to monitor internal temperature throughout the evening to ensure unit can consistently maintain temperature below 41F prior to beginning to utilize unit again. PIC stated repair tech will arrive at 6:30 to assess 2-door LB sushi unit and WIC. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed call items in sushi display case without proper dates. PIC stated that items were thawed/cut this morning and verified with items in reach in unit. EHS stated during last inspection, all items in sushi display shall be dated marked. PIC discussed issue with sushi chef who verified dates with prep list from this morning. CDI - PIC was allowed to date all sushi items. PIC stated moving forward all items will be dated. This is the same date marking issue discussed during last inspection. REPEAT. (3)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf
3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P
3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. 

Observed correctly written TPHC form for rice noodles, pork belly, beef, these items did not have times for removal from heat or cold. CDI-voluntarily discarded
Observed shrimp appetizer in individual portioned to-go boxes on counter at 80F. Asked staff if they were on TPHC, asked PIC when he arrived, that menu item is not on the TPHC form. Needs to be added to the form or held cold (<41F). CDI-voluntarily discarded



TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

violations.comments: 3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P EHS observed toss salad mix being stored at expo window on time. violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed cooked mushrooms, onions, tomatoes cooling from being prepared 30-45 minutes prior to inspection according to PIC. EHS observed items cooling at room temperature. EHS observed temperatures above 70F. PIC stated food is left out at room temperature until food has begun cooling and then placed into WIC. EHS advised that item only has two hours from time cooling begins to be under 70F. PIC removed items from speed rack and placed into WIC with tight fitting lids. EHS observed inadequate cooling rates after thirty minutes. At this time, these items had a remaining 20 minutes to achieve proper cooling. EHS intervened and advised to stretch items on sheet pans and placed into WIC to quickly drop temperature to meet parameters. CDI - PIC stretched onions, mushrooms, and tomatoes onto sheet pans and placed into WIC. EHS verified prior to two hour window and observed temperatures below 70F. (1) REPEAT. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:

- PIC stated that egg roll fillings are Cooked, Cooled, Wrapped, Frozen, and then Reheated to order. Permit states that COOLING IS PROHIBITED due to lack of cooling equipment. EHS discussed immediately stopping cooking and cooling proteins. Eggroll’s must be wrapped with raw fillings. If this is found again on another inspection, an intent to suspend your permit will be issued. Please reach out to EHS if you plan to install a blast chiller to continue cooling food items. 

- EHS discovered large blue container holding large batch of house-sauce. Container is unable to be submerged in 3 compartment sink. When asking PIC how they clean it, they stated it is sprayed down and brushed out. Discontinue use of large container and replace with smaller containers that may be submerged in 3 compartment sink - Bus tubs work great here. 

- TPHC procedures provided during inspection.

#25 - 3-603.11 - Ensure consumer advisory is provided for all under cooked food items. Facility recently printed new menus. Facility cooks and cools more than 4 items (chicken for chicken salad, ground sausage, spicy sausage and various sauces.). Risk 
category will be changed from risk 3 to risk 4.

violations.comments:

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Gravy (131F) and chicken (125F) measured below 135F in hot holding. TCS foods in hot holding shall measure at least 135F. CDI - PIC reheated items to above 165F. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Cassava leave in upright cooler (45F), rice (44F) and green rice (51F). TCS foods in cold holding shall measure 41F or less. CDI - PIC stated that these items are pulled out frequently to prepare orders which caused the food to warm up. The kitchen is extremely hot because the AC isn't working so ensure food is not left out and minimize opening doors to heat of kitchen doesn't warm food above 41F.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

rows.general_comments:
USING TPHC:
1. Ensure food starts at 41F or below.
2. Label foods for no more than 6 hours (if the food will not exceed 70F- 4 hours if it will)
3. Dispose all remaining at the end of the time window. Do NOT cool and reheat.
4. Full out and retain these procedures onsite: https://mecknc.widen.net/s/pvtc855zds/tphc-template-english

violations.comments:
6-301.14 Post a handwash sign at each handsink.
Observed no posted hand sink signs.
CDI- EHS provided county signs at both hand sinks. (-0)

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
Observed one container of white rice in WIC cooked yesterday at 45F, which failed to cool. EHS provided education to both present staff members about cooling methods. 
CDI- Rice which failed to cool on time voluntarily disposed. (-1.5)

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P 
Observed cooked potatoes at 103F in steamwell.
CDI- Potatoes reheated above 165F and returned to steamwell with lid. All other steamwell items in compliance. (-0)

REPEAT.
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed sliced spinach, lettuce, couscous, chorizo, feta cheese, diced tomato, and mayo in cold well/lowboy above 41F. See temp chart. 
CDI- Items rapidly cooled in WIC. EHS advises that lowboy was overfilled past its capacity, and cold air cannot circulate if fans are blocked. Ambient air in unit observed at 40F. Work order should be placed and TPHC should be used while awaiting repair. Open lid make top should be maintained with cabinet air between 35F-38F to maintain TCS foods at 41F or below. 

*Risk Control Plan or permit action may be taken if cold holding is out of compliance at the next inspection, due to repeat violations.

REPEAT.
3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed several undated pans of rice cooked today or yesterday in WIC. Observed multiple containers of shredded lettuce cooling, sliced tomato, and TCS bottled dressings prepped yesterday or today without date marks.
CDI- EHS confirmed prep date with chef who prepared. Items with unknown prep date voluntarily disposed. Rice and sliced lettuce dated. (-1.5)

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
REPEAT.
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed numerous containers of rice cooling in WIC with parchment placed on top of rice, followed by lids, and contains stacked 3-4 high. Lower containers are not able to cool in these conditions. Provide shallow, uncovered, well spaced containers for cooling TCS foods. 
CDI- Cooling methods discussed with PIC. Failed cool rice voluntarily disposed.

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta.
Observed unlabeled oil mixture (non-TCS confirmed) in squirt bottle at make top, and small containers of decanted herbs on dry storage rack without labels. Label all spices and herbs with working name. (-1)

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P

Facility to maintain temperature log for WIC until REHS return.
72 hour VR required.
1.5 pts.

violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. violations.comments:
4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. 
After checking dish machine final rinse gauge and running department disk thermometer through the machine, it was discovered that disk thermometer showed 148F on final rinse, and in-place thermometer on machine showed final rinse of 139-140F. Person running dish machine needs to know what to look for when processing utensils. Facility also needs to purchase a disk thermometer in order to monitor maximum temperature of final rinse to be at least 160F. Facility has called company so that they can repair the dish machine. Utensils must be processed through 3-compartment sink to properly wash, rinse, and sanitize. VR visit must be made within 3 days to see that dish machine is properly running and properly sanitizing. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed par-cooked chicken wings at 46F in refrigerator; conversation with kitchen manager as well as observation of other food items in this refrigerator shows the appearance that these wings were likely left out on a counter before being placed in refrigerator. Chicken wings come from reach-in freezer where they are at 32F, and all other items in the refrigerator where the chicken wings were at 46 were at 39F. Assure that items are removed from bag and that bag is then placed quickly back into refrigerator. CDI by items being placed on sheet tray into walk-in freezer, where they were later measured at 31F.


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (A) Provide consumer advisory for animal foods served raw or under-cooked. Consumer advisory must include disclosure and reminder.-Pf
3-603.11 (C )(2) A Consumer Advisory Reminder shall include asterisking the food item to a footnote that states: * Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness.- Pf
Observed no consumer advisory present on facility's online menu. Facility's physical menu has consumer advisory.
Observed no asterisks on any menu items for facility's physical menu correlating with the footnote. PIC stated caesar dressing is made in-house and includes raw eggs. PIC also stated steak is cooked to temp per order. violations.comments:
4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. 
Observed high temp dish machine unable to reach 160F after multiple cycles were run. PIC stated last time ECOLAB was on-site for routine maintenance was early this month. PIC contacted ECOLAB rep for repairs. ECOLAB rep stated they will make a visit tomorrow morning. Facility has properly concentrated QUAT sanitizer used at the 3-compartment sink. PIC stated they will only utilize the 3-compartment sink to wash/rinse/sanitize all multi-use equipment and utensils until repairs have been made.
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (C )(2) A Consumer Advisory Reminder shall include asterisking the food item to a footnote that states: * Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness.- Pf
Observed no asterisks for consumer advisory on new menu, which includes 5 menu items that are served raw or undercooked. Under "shareable plates" section, spicy tuna crispy rice (for raw tuna chunks). Under "signature entrees" section, Korean power bowl (for sunny side egg). Under "Brunch" section, 1) avocado toast 2) breakfast smashburger 3) fried chicken biscuit sandwich (all for undercooked eggs).
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed two pans of sliced tomatoes cooling at a rate of 0.05 deg/min, inside the blast chiller, unable to meet the cooling rate. Tomatoes were cooling inside the blast chiller in plastic plans that were tightly covered with seran wrap. Date labels showed tomatoes had been just prepared and placed inside to cool.
CDI: PIC removed seran wrap to allow proper cold air flow.
Observed cast iron dishes of portioned out spinach dip cooling at a rate of 0.09 deg/min, inside the drawers of make table 1, unable to meet the cooling rate. Cast iron dishes were covered with seran wrap. Spinach dip was prepared less than 4 hours prior to EHS's observation. 
CDI: PIC removed seran wrap from spinach dip and moved dishes into the blast chiller to rapidly cool down.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. - Observed no written procedures on site at the time of the inspection for the 4 hour TPHC procedure that the facility uses for the sushi rice as per the kitchen manager. Facility was not open so EHS was unable to observe the TPHC procedure in action but PIC stated they do use 4 hour time holds on sushi rice in bins after cooking.

CDI - EHS filled out TPHC written procedures with the PIC at the time of the inspection.

TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water. - Observed packages of raw frozen tuna thawing in its ROP packages on the countertop in the back kitchen area. Thawing instructions state “remove from package while thawing” and no cuts were observed in the packaging.

CDI - PIC placed packages under running water (<70F) and removed from ROP after thawing was completed.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments: 4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. - Observed the WIC to be maintaining a temperature of 53F during the entirety of the inspection. All items were discarded prior to the EHS arriving (see 6/23 visit sheet). Repair company was on site this morning at 8:30am and had repaired the electrical issue in the compressor that caused the breaker to trip. The unit had continued to drop for the first hour after the repair company left but stopped at 53F and will not go below that. WIC only has non-TCS vegetables in it and facility has contacted the repair company to come out again and take another look at it while the EHS was on site. EHS to follow up on the repair later this week. Facilities other refrigeration was observed functional and plans to operate for the day with the items they have and will not use the WIC for TCS products.

violations.comments:

CDI - PIC removed chicken from containers and placed on new ice bath, EHS observed chicken under 41F prior to end of inspection(see temp chart) REPEAT. (1)

4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. Observed high temperature dish machine not reaching 160F for sanitizing according to EHS plate thermometer. For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-401.11 Cook raw animal foods to required temperatures. Do not interrupt the cooking process without approved procedures. -P Observed sliced roast beef in RIC drawer at sandwich prep line. PIC stated that the roast beef is cooked on a spit at wood fired oven to 110F, sliced, cooled, cold held, then cooked to 165F for service per order. PIC does not have approved procedures for non-continuous cooking in facility. PIC stated that they will fill out an application for procedures to continue this procedure once approved. PIC stated that until procedures are approved, roast will be cooked to 130F for 110 minutes to be in compliance with the food code. CDI: non-continuous cooked roast beef voluntarily discarded.

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P - Observed the chemical dishwasher to be testing at 0ppm of chlorine at the time of the inspection. CDI - PIC date marked items.

- Observed a container of house made pesto to be stored in the cookline refrigerated drawer with a date mark of 5/20. Facility does not currently have a procedure of putting “pulled from freezer” dates onto items. EHS explained the date marking procedure when items are frozen and why they require to have pulled from freezer dates. Prep employee stated pulling the container of pesto in question out of the freezer on Sunday (6/21).

CDI - Pulled from freezer date placed onto container.

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed cut salmon and cut chicken actively cooling in grill make unit. PIC stated salmon was placed into unit and cut an hour prior to inspection. after thirty minutes, EHS observed inadequate cooling rate (see temp chart). EHS observed cooked chicken bagged into sets for harissa chicken. EHS observed chicken above 41F (see temp chart). PIC stated chicken was placed into unit at noon but was left out unintentionally for longer than needed prior to being placed into unit so item needed to cool after. No temperature was checked after being placed into unit. EHS observed diced tomatoes being stored in WIC in numerous pans tightly covered with lid. PIC stated items should not be covered, and removed lid. EHS observed inadequate cooling rate after 25 minutes (see temp chart). PIC stated tomatoes were cut at 1:30pm. CDI - Due to having 15 minutes left to cool, PIC removed harissa chicken and placed into blast chiller to quickly cool. PIC removed salmon from make unit and placed into blast chiller. EHS observed chicken at 41 within 15 minutes. EHS observed salmon at 41F prior to end of inspection. PIC moved diced tomatoes to blast chiller. EHS observed adequate cooling rate by end of inspection. EHS advised to ensure temperatures are taken by staff throughout the day to ensure when items are moved they are cooled prior to storage, and to ensure proper cooling methods are followed. REPEAT. (1)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. 
Observed no written procedures for TPHC onsite.
CDI- EHS provided county form. 

FORM HERE: https://mecknc.widen.net/s/pvtc855zds/tphc-template-english

3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf
Observed fried chicken on TPHC without time label.
CDI- EHS verifies correct start temp >165F and allows PIC to mark for time. (-1.5)

3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf
Observed raw chicken thawing on prep top at 45F.
CDI- EHS advises PIC on proper thawing methods. Chicken returned to WIC. (-0)

REPEAT.
3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses.
Observed numerous used wiping cloths on prep tops throughout front and back of kitchen.
CDI- Sani-buckets made up for wiping cloth storage, sanitizer concentration verified. (-1)

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-202.11 Multiuse food contact surfaces shall be smooth, free of open seams, cracks, chips, pits, sharp internal angles, crevices and assembled to allow access to clean. -Pf
Observed one fryer basket with metal wire coming apart from frame, no longer safe to use.
CDI- Basket voluntarily disposed and replaced with new. (-0)

REPEAT.
4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized.
Observed funerals cutting boards with deep scoring, no longer cleanable. Replace at earliest opportunity. (-0.5) 

4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
Observed rusted metal racks inside WIC, no longer cleanable. Replace racks which are corroded; not smooth and cleanable.

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments: 3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed a box of mini apple pies and a box of brownies stored directly on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Ensure food boxes are stored at least 6 inches above the floor.

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments: 4-903.11(B)(1) Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows for air drying. CDI- PIC removed equipment to the dish washer to be re-washed. REPEAT.

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments:
4-302.14 Provide a test kit that accurately measures sanitizer concentrations. -Pf. Observed no available chlorine sanitizer test kit to measure the chlorine sanitizer concentration in the dishwasher. CDI- EHS provided chlorine sanitizer test kit to PIC. Ensure sanitizer test kit is used and remains available.

4-501.14 Warewashing machines and the compartments/drainboards of sinks used for washing and rinsing equipment, utensils, raw food, etc. shall be cleaned before use, throughout the day to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils, and at least every 24 hours if used. Observed food debris and lime scale build-up on the interior of the dish washer machine. The dish washer machine is not cleaned every 24 hours. PIC must educate staff on cleaning the dish washer machine at required frequency.

REPEAT
4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed food debris and grease residue build-up on wire rack shelving in the clean equipment room and by the cut table. Also, the wire rack shelving above the 3-comp sink has grease residue build-up. Increase frequency of detailed cleaning shelving. Observed excessive residue build-up on the pizza oven tracks and on top of the pizza oven and needs cleaned.
Observed food residue build-up on the exterior handles and the interior sections of the make-line cooler, the standing 2 door reach-in cooler, and the standing 2 door reach-in freezer. Ensure all equipment is cleaned and cleaned frequently enough to prevent build-up.

6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed food debris and residue build-up throughout kitchen primarily the walls and floor area around the pizza oven. Walls and floors need to be maintained clean. REPEAT.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed raw calamari stored over RTE foods in make unit reach in compartment. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order, no contamination observed.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. EHS observed raw calamari and raw turkey being prepped/thawed at three compartment sink with no visible separation or protection. PIC stated raw ground turkey was left at three compartment sink drain board to drain excess liquid. EHS observed raw calamari in the next compartment over thawing at room temperature. EHS advised to utilize prep sinks when preparing raw proteins and avoid using three compartment sink for these tasks. Facility has two prep sinks; one is a two compartment sink. CDI - PIC removed calamari and placed at empty prep sink under running water; ground turkey was moved to WIC. No contamination observed. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation(1.5)

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed numerous pans and plastic containers stacked on top of each other, stored as clean, with visible sticker residue present on pans. CDI - PIC removed all pans with residue to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. EHS observed buffalo chicken dip in WIC at 44F. PIC stated dip was prepared yesterday and placed into WIC. PIC stated item has not left WIC since being placed there yesterday. EHS observed dip with tight fitting lid. EHS observed ground beef patties being cooled from preparation 3.5 hours prior to inspection. EHS observed patties at 45F with 15 minutes left to go, tightly covered with plastic wrap and lid. PIC stated temperatures have not been taken of these items during cooling process. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded chicken dip, patties spread out and placed into WIF uncovered. EHS observed patties at 41, 15 minutes later.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed ground turkey, sweet potatoes, queso, and tomato sauce cooling at inadequate rates during inspection (see temp chart). EHS did not observe active monitoring of this process for any item during inspection. Tomato sauce observed in ice bath in prep sink, however, EHS observed no active stirring. EHS observed ground turkey in deep plastic containers with plastic wrap and tight fitting lid over turkey, EHS observed queso in WIC actively cooling with no stirring. EHS provided education. 3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. Store tags in chronological order for 90 days. -Pf

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed one pan of roasted cauliflower date-marked with a prep date of 6/10, stored inside the lowboy portion of make table 1. Observed one pan of roasted cauliflower date-marked with a prep date of 6/11, stored inside the lowboy portion of make table 1. Food employee stated these were the correct date of prep and are not frozen.
CDI: Food employee voluntarily discarded both pans of roasted cauliflower, since they had surpassed the 7-day window.
Observed a pan of marinated cut tomatoes date-marked with a prep date of 6/10, stored inside lowboy cooler 2. Food employee stated they batch prep this food item and freeze it before thawing out prior to serving. Food employee stated he pulled this out of the freezer 2 days prior.
CDI: Food employee created second date label with thaw date of 6/16 to depict the "clock start date."
Observed a cambro full of roasted mix veggies that was date-marked with a prep date of 6/09, stored inside the lowboy portion of make table 2. Food employee stated that was the correct date of prep and is not frozen.
CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded cambro, since it had surpassed the 7-day window.
Observed a pan of roasted smashed potatoes date-marked with a prep date of 6/10, stored inside the WIC. PIC stated this was the correct date of prep.
CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded potatoes, since it had surpassed the 7-day window.
Observed a pan of braised beef date-marked with a prep date of 6/10, stored inside the WIC. PIC stated this was the correct date of prep, but was frozen then thawed out 2 days prior.
CDI: PIC created second date label with thaw date of 6/16 to depict the "clock start date."
REPEAT VIOLATION.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

EHS observed litter accumulating around dumpster area. EHS observed items such as shelving and wood pallets being stored outside of dumpster area. EHS advised to clear out area of unnecessary items and litter. (0)

6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. EHS observed large amount of residue on the ceiling in hibachi dining rooms due to preparing food during hibachi service. EHS advised to increase cleaning frequency of ceilings and walls of dining rooms due to food being prepared in room. (0)

violations.comments:
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
-Observed gnocchi (6/9) held past its 7-day timeframe. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the gnocchi.
-Observed vegetable stock with two date marks on the container (6/3 and 6/16). -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the stock.
-Observed pomodoro sauce with an illegible date mark, that appeared to state 6/10. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the sauce.
-Observed hard boiled eggs without a date mark. -CDI- PIC verified eggs were cooked yesterday and properly added a date mark.
-Observed multiple foods in WIC with improper date marks (ex.- bread dough with label of 11/18). -CDI- PIC confirmed all improperly labeled date marks were prepared within the past 7 days and will correct date marks/train employees on proper date marking procedures.


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed containers of grilled chicken strips, cut lettuce, and Swiss cheese to be in the cookline lowboy at temperatures of 44-49F. Items in the opentop are held using TPHC and were properly time stamped at the time of the inspection. PIC stated that staff leave the opentop open throughout lunch usually and stated that is why the lowboy is running warm. Ambient observed at 49F. PIC stated that the items have been in the lowboy since approx. 9am and were not sure how long the items have been out of temperature for. 

CDI - All out of temperature items voluntarily discarded. Ambient of the unit was observed at 41F and the lettuce moved up into the unit while the EHS was typing the report was able to hold/maintain 41F. EHS advised the staff to not keep the lid open during rushes or if they are going to do that they should not keep TCS foods in the lowboy portion as it causes temperature issues during that period.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed pan of black pepper bean sprouts cooling inside the WIC and not changing in temperature after 38 minutes had surpassed. Pan was made of plastic and covered with a lid.

violations.comments:

violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF - Observed no signed employee health agreement on site at the time of the inspection. REPEAT.

CDI - EHS provided written copy of employee health agreement and had both kitchen employees sign at the time of the inspection.

For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P - Observed the dishwasher to be testing at 0ppm of chlorine at the time of the inspection. Sanitizer bottle was observed empty at the time of the visit.

CDI - Sanitizer bottle changed, machine primed, and retested at 150ppm.

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P - Observed a container of tater tots to be at a temperature of 96F on the counter beneath the heatlamp at the cookline. PIC stated that they make the tater tots in the oven every day and then they sit under the heatlamp until needed. EHS advised the PIC that switching to TPHC could be more beneficial since they are often only open from 7-11pm and typically sell through it on busier weekend nights.

CDI - Tater tots placed on temporary TPHC. EHS filled out TPHC procedure with PIC and explained the process to the PIC to utilize going forward.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed 2 opened packages of hot dogs in the lowboy refrigerator that were not provided with date marks of any kind. Upon questioning it was discovered they were opened the previous Wednesday, making today day 8 for the items. EHS explained how the 7 day date marking window and with the facility being closed on Monday/Tuesday the EHS advised that the kitchen staff discard all TCS items on Sunday night or first thing Wednesday morning to avoid date marking violations in the future.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. -Observed handsink behind bar (serving coffee) with items stored inside. -CDI- PIC removed items to make handsink accessible.

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments: 3-101.11 Food shall be safe for consumption, unadulterated and honestly presented. -P -Observed tomato stored in prep unit with visible blue/white growth. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the tomato.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P -Observed raw chicken and raw lamb stored above shrimp and cooked crab meat in the tall reach-in cooler. -CDI- Storage order was corrected.



For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P -Observed cooked mushrooms, raw shrimp, and cooked crab meat above 41F in tall reach-in cooler. All other TCS food in tall RIC was at or below 41F. PIC stated the mushrooms, shrimp, and crab meat were originally stored in the under-grill cold drawers this morning, yet the cold drawers have not been cold holding properly recently, so the food was moved to the tall RIC after realizing the cooler was malfunctioning again. PIC stated the cold drawers underneath flat top grill have not been cold holding below 41F recently, and they are waiting on cooler parts for repair. -Do not store TCS foods in the under-grill drawers until the cooler is fully repaired and properly maintaining food at or below 41F. -PIC stated the food was moved to the tall RIC less than one hour ago, therefore PIC placed mushrooms, crab meat, and shrimp on ice in tall RIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed shrimp, mushrooms, and crab meat cooling at sufficient rates to reach 41F. -Contact EHS when cooler is repaired- 3 day verification visit required-
REPEAT

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
-Observed sliced ham (6/7) and cooked carrots (6/7) held past their 7-day timeframe. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the carrots. PIC stated the date mark on the ham was incorrect and it was actually prepared yesterday, 6/16. PIC corrected date mark.


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed TCS food items stored inside WIC 1 cold holding above 41F. Ambient air temp of WIC 1 was at 48F, and EHS noticed WIC door was left open, with employees constantly going in and out of the unit. Facility conducts equipment temperature checks and records temperatures digitally using tablets, but WIC 1 temperatures were not taken this morning. Ambient air temp dropped to 45F after 22 minutes. Another ambient air temp was taken at 11:30AM (over an hour from the first initial ambient air temp reading) after unit was blocked off from employee use, and WIC 1 was still temping 44F-47F (immediate spike in temperature when door is opened). EHS noticed ice buildup on fan inside the unit, and heavy condensation dripping from the fan. PIC entered a work order in for technicians to come out and check on the unit. All TCS food items from WIC 1 were moved into WIC 2, as WIC 2 has plenty of storage space to hold TCS food items. PICs stated they understand to keep raw chicken stored separated from all other TCS food items inside WIC 2. 
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P- Observed raw fish stored over RTE ribs in the WIC. Ensure that no raw food is stored over RTE foods. -CDI- PIC rearranged storage order so that raw was no longer over RTE.

EHS ran the dish machine 3 times and after each run of the machine, the chlorine concentration was 0PPM. -CDI- Dish machine was primed using the sanitizer primer switch and then was reading at approximately 100PPM afterwards. 
Ensure that dish machine is properly primed and is maintains proper sanitizer concentrations. 



For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf- Observed a tub of ambient prepared croaker fish at 50F in the fish RIC. Food employee stated that they were prepared 15 mins prior to EHSs arrival. After 30 minutes the fish were 49F. EHS notes that the fish were packed into a large bus tub. -CDI- PIC moved croaker fish into WIF to properly cool. Fish were cooling at a proper rate by the end of the inspection. 
Ensure proper cooling methods are followed. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed inadequate cooling rates for quinoa salad. EHS observed item actively cooling in make unit with flip top lid open during entire inspection. EHS observed containers of quinoa salad in WIC covered and actively cooling. EHS observed inadequate rates during inspection. CDI - PIC removed lids from quinoa salad and replaced container in make unit with container observed below 41F. **EHS is notating an improvement on procedures observed. EHS observed numerous items actively cooling during inspection with proper cooling rates observed and efficient methods exhibited. EHS will de-escalate points due to improvement. EHS will deduct full points on next inspection if improvement does not continue. Last inspection EHS observed 1 item inadequately cooling vs. 1 item that was observed cooling properly. This inspection EHS observed 1 item with inadequate cooling rate vs 4 items observed with adequate rates. No risk control plan required at this time. (0.5) REPEAT. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. 
Observed a pan of marinated raw chicken skewers stored on a shelf above a pan of marinated raw red snapper, stored inside RIC 3.
CDI: PIC corrected storage order and EHS provided food storage order handout to serve as a visual aid.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed multiple TCS food items stored inside the lowboy cooler above 41F (see temp chart). Ambient air temp of the cold holding unit was 45F. PIC stated food items are not kept inside this unit overnight, and are pulled from the WIC in the morning. Food items have been stored inside this unit less than 4 hours. PIC moved all TCS food items into the RIF to rapidly cool down. PIC contacted technician to have cold holding unit checked for repairs. EHS checked ambient air temp again after PIC had manually adjusted temperature dial on the unit, and ambient air temp of the unit was now temping at 47F.
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed pan of paneer without a date label, stored inside the make table. PIC stated this was prepared yesterday.
CDI: Date label created.
Observed bottle of salad dressing (house-made w/TCS ingredients) without a date label, stored inside the lowboy cooler. PIC stated this was prepared on Sunday.
CDI: Date label created.
Observed pan of boiled potatoes and a pan of cut cabbage both missing date labels, stored inside the lowboy cooler. PIC stated these were prepared on Sunday as well.
CDI: Date label created. 
Observed opened jug of whole milk missing date label. PIC stated they opened this jug of milk on Sunday.
CDI: Date label created.
REPEAT VIOLATION.
*Note: Although a repeat violation, EHS not deducting full points today as facility has now established a date-marking system since previous inspection, and it appears some TCS food items were missed. PICs understood which food items require date labels and which do not, and understand that food items are not held past 7 days from prep.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water.
Observed ROP'd packages of raw salmon fillets thawing under running water, temping above 32F (no longer in the frozen state), without slits in the packaging.
EHS explained to PICs food item is required to be removed from the ROP'd packaging prior to thawing, per manufacturer's label to prevent biological contamination.

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta.
Observed a large bin full of various spices/seasonings used at the make line, unlabeled. Observed all bottles of different sauces/oils/vinegars used at the make line unlabeled.
Ensure all working containers of food items are labeled for easy identification.
REPEAT VIOLATION.

3-304.12 (B) In-use utensils for food that is not TCS must be stored with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed.
Observed scoops used inside rolling bins of sugar and rice stored with their handles commingled within the non-TCS food products.
CDI: PIC removed scoops from the bin to prevent contamination.

4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted.

Ensure pans are completely air-dried prior to stacking together.

2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. Observed no certified food protection manager on site during inspection.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed no date marking for items in prep top cooler. CDI: PIC prepared the items and was able to date mark them for when she prepared them. Observed ready to eat ham portions date marked for 10 days in the reach in cooler. Items were not held past 7 days today. CDI: Items marked to reflect the remaining number of days to be held.

violations.comments:
3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P- Observed raw chorizo stored over top of corn in the stand up RIC and several raw foods out of the original packaging in the Stand Up RIF stored over top of RTE foods. -CDI- PIC rearranged storage order. 
Ensure raw animal foods are not stored over RTE foods. 



For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P- Observed cooked onions and cooked onions in peppers in the HH Cabinet below 135F. When EHS asked when they were cooked and placed into the Cabinet PIC and food employees determined it was over 2 hours prior. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P- Observed rice in the WIC above 41F. Observed all TCS foods in the grill drawers above 41F. Ambient reading of the unit was 55F. Foods included raw beef, chicken, shrimp, RTE Al Pastor, and cut tomatoes. -CDI- All foods above 41F were voluntarily discarded. PIC called a refrigerator tech during the inspection. EHS will return to ensure that grill drawers is properly repaired. 
-3-DAY VR-

Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). Observed facility with several foods past date in the prep unit in both the flip and lowboy portion. PIC explained that foods were frozen on the original date. Foods did not have a second date once taken from the freezer. -CDI- Foods were able to be back dated to when they were pulled from the freezer. All foods were within the 7 day window. 
Ensure proper date marking procedures for when RTE foods are thawed for use. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments: 3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. 16 - Food-contact surfaces: cleaned & sanitized: REPEAT.
4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf.

Observed all 3 microwaves with significant food debris inside. Increase cleaning frequency.

20 - Proper cooling time & temperatures: 3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf- Observed multiple risk factor violations during inspection. **10 DAY VERIFICATION REQUIRED BY 5/24/2026** -1- **REPEAT** 
A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety

violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure. -Pf- Observed no signed attestation of EHP. Observed PIC unable to answer EHS’ questions about EHP. -CDI- PIC located copy provided at previous inspection, educated PIC and food employees and all employees signed at time of visit. **REPEAT** -1- 
For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

2-301.12 (A),(B), (C) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel) and use a clean barrier such as a disposable paper towel when touching surfaces such as a manually operated faucet handle to avoid recontaminating hands. -P- Observed food employee wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. -CDI- EHS educated food employee on using a barrier to turn off faucet and food employee rewashed hands. 
For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M . 
2-301.14 (F) Wash hands during food preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination, and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks. -P- Observed food employee handling raw carne asada and then go to handle spice containers, date marking stickers, and pen without washing hands. Observed food employee handle raw fish and then go to handle water handle on coffee machine without washing hands. -CDI- EHS educated food employee on when to wash and food employee washed hands. -0-
6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf- Observed no paper towels at handsink. -CDI- PIC replenished paper towel supply. -0-

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P- Observed raw bacon in container with RTE ham. -CDI- PIC corrected storage order. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation 
3-302.11 (A)(4) Except when the food is being cooled, store food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. Observed multiple items in RIFs, RIC, prep units and WIC with no protective coverings. **REPEAT** -3- 
3-302.11(A)(8) Separate unwashed produce from ready-to-eat foods. Observed box of unwashed peppers stored over RTE beans in WIC. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation 
3-304.15(A) Discard gloves after a task is complete or any time they are damaged or soiled. -P- Observed food employee using gloves to handle raw chicken and begin to handle spices, date marking stickers and other items without discarding gloves. Observed food employee handle raw fish and then begin to handle water nozzle of coffee dispenser without discarding gloves. -CDI- EHS educated food employee on when to discard gloves and food employee discarded gloves and cleaned off contaminated items.

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf.- Observed food debris on dishes stored as clean. Per PIC, some items not in use. -CDI- PIC moved items to dishpit to be W/R/S. Items not in use must be stored clean or removed from facility. **REPEAT** -1.5- 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P- Observed all items in top of meat prep unit above 41F, items on bottom of unit were at proper temperatures. Observed potatoes for pupusas and raw carne asada above 41F. Refer to temperature chart. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded items. **REPEAT** -3- **3 DAY VERIFICATION BY 5/15/26** **PIC TO NOT USE TOP OF PREP UNIT UNTIL REPAIRS CAN BE MADE** 
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). violations.comments:
4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. Observed cutting boards throughout no longer smooth and easily cleanable. Resurface or replace. 
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. Observed rust buildup on bottom shelves of 2 prep tables. Observed rusted shelving throughout in need of replacement. Observed shelving used to store clean dishes that had been spray painted. **REPEAT** -1- 
4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. Observed broken door handle gasket at RIF near WIC. Observed door on prep unit #1 not properly closing.

Observed dark growth inside of sanitizer tubing at 3-comp sink. Increased and more thorough cleaning frequency recommended. **REPEAT** -0.5-

Observed cracked floor tiles at FOH near cook line. Also observed multiple missing baseboards throughout the facility (Kitchen, back storage room, and WIC).

Observed broken RI unit and lowboy being used for storage. Observed other items not in use. Observed plates and some cold pans that per PIC were no longer in use. Remove any items no longer in use. **REPEAT** -1- 
6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed debris buildup on tops of paper towel dispensers. Observed food debris and water on floors. Increased and more thorough cleaning frequency recommended. 
6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair. Observed most lights with no light shields and one light shield hanging down, not fully intact. Replace.

violations.comments:
2-102.11 (A) - (C )(1), (4)-(16) The Person in charge shall demonstrate knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of HACCP principles, and the requirements of this code by (A) Complying with the Food Code by having no violations of Priority Items during the current inspection, (B) Being a certified food protection manager, or (C) by responding correctly to the inspector's questions related to the operation of the food establishment. -Pf- Observed facilities lack of control of food safety measures in the facility and an inability to demonstrate knowledge on food safety principles. 2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Observed 2 other foods employees wash hands with soap but do so for approximately 5-10 seconds. -CDI- PIC Simon and EHS discussed proper hand washing procedures, hands were rewashed following proper procedures.
